Actions on Objectives
Detected
Reconnaissance. Attacker researches the target — OSINT, scanning, enumeration.
Weaponization. Coupling exploit code with deliverable payload (e.g. weaponized PDF/Office doc, trojanized installer).
Delivery. Transmitting the weapon (phishing email, USB, watering hole, drive-by, malicious ad). → [LLM] PhantomMail: Ukrainian-themed ZIP/RAR delivered via Google Drive or 4sync links · Phishing-link click correlated to endpoint execution · Email attachment opened from external sender
Exploitation. Triggering the exploit — vulnerability/macro/trust abuse to execute code. → [LLM] PhantomClick: browser → mshta/powershell/cmd within 60s of fake Cloudflare/Zoom/LAPAS lure · Office app spawning script/LOLBin child process · Fake CAPTCHA / clipboard-injected PowerShell (ClickFix / FakeCaptcha) · PowerShell encoded / obfuscated command
Installation. Establishing persistence on the host — backdoor, service, scheduled task, registry key. → [LLM] GreyVibe: RDP enablement via fDenyTSConnections=0 + firewall by PowerShell RAT
Command & Control. Beacon to attacker infrastructure for control and tasking. → [LLM] PowerShell.exe sustained beaconing to uncategorized web endpoint (LegionRelay/PhantomRelay C2) · Beaconing — periodic outbound to small set of destinations
Actions on Objectives. Lateral movement, credential dumping, data theft, ransomware, sabotage. → [LLM] LegionRelay browser credential theft from Chromium/Firefox Login Data by PowerShell · [LLM] LegionRelay Telegram / WhatsApp messenger store exfiltration · [LLM] GreyVibe cryptocurrency miner deployment via PowerShell RAT
[LLM] PhantomMail: Ukrainian-themed ZIP/RAR delivered via Google Drive or 4sync links Delivery Medium
Hunts GreyVibe's PhantomMail vector: spear-phishing emails with ZIP/RAR attachments or body links to Google Drive / 4sync, themed against Ukrainian gov, emergency, telecom or energy entities. Pivots on archive attachments plus the two specific cloud-storage URL families called out by WithSecure. Rationale: Anchors on WithSecure-stated PhantomMail strings: ZIP/RAR archives, Google Drive and 4sync links, and Ukrainian gov/emergency/telecom/energy lure impersonation. Mail-only signal so endpoint queries are deferred to the execution UCs. Cross-checked against: • https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1566/001/ • https://www.bleepingcomputer.com/news/security/greyvibe-hackers-use-chatgpt-gemini-to-power-cyberattacks/
ATT&CKT1566.001 T1566.002

[LLM] PhantomClick: browser → mshta/powershell/cmd within 60s of fake Cloudflare/Zoom/LAPAS lure Exploitation High
Hunts the PhantomClick ClickFix flow: victim visits a fake Zoom or LAPAS site, the page displays a fake Cloudflare verification, and the user pastes a self-infecting command. Pivots on a browser parent spawning interpreter children within seconds, with the cmdline carrying ClickFix-style payload markers. Rationale: Maps directly to WithSecure's PhantomClick description: fake Cloudflare/Zoom/LAPAS verification leading users to paste self-infecting commands. Combines browser parent + interpreter child + ClickFix telltale strings (Cloudflare, ray-id, captcha, lapas, Verify you are human). Cross-checked against MITRE T1204.001 and recurring ClickFix Sigma rules to ensure novelty. Cross-checked against: • https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1204/001/ • https://www.bleepingcomputer.com/news/security/greyvibe-hackers-use-chatgpt-gemini-to-power-cyberattacks/
ATT&CKT1204.001 T1059.001 T1059.003

SecurityEvent | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d) | where EventID == 4688 | where ParentProcessName has_any ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe","brave.exe","opera.exe") | where NewProcessName has_any ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","mshta.exe","cmd.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe") | where CommandLine has_any ("I am not a robot","Cloudflare","ray-id","verification","captcha","zoom","lapas","FromBase64String","IEX","Invoke-Expression","irm ","mshta http","curl http","Verify you are human") | where SubjectUserName !endswith "$" | project TimeGenerated, Computer, SubjectUserName, ParentProcessName, NewProcessName, CommandLine | order by TimeGenerated desc

[LLM] LegionRelay browser credential theft from Chromium/Firefox Login Data by PowerShell Actions on Objectives High
Hunts LegionRelay's browser credential-theft module: PowerShell or other non-browser processes reading Chromium 'Login Data' / 'Local State' and Firefox 'logins.json' / 'key4.db'. Article calls out browser credential theft as a built-in capability of the LegionRelay RAT. Rationale: WithSecure says LegionRelay 'supports … browser credential theft'. Targets the universal artefact paths of the Chromium and Firefox credential vaults, gated on a non-browser scripting-host parent — the article calls out LegionRelay as a PowerShell-based RAT. Cross-checked against: • https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1555/003/ • https://www.bleepingcomputer.com/news/security/greyvibe-hackers-use-chatgpt-gemini-to-power-cyberattacks/
ATT&CKT1555.003
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem
DeviceFileEvents | where Timestamp > ago(14d) | where FileName in~ ("Login Data","Local State","logins.json","key4.db","cookies.sqlite","Cookies","Web Data") | where FolderPath has_any ("\\Google\\Chrome\\","\\Microsoft\\Edge\\","\\Mozilla\\Firefox\\","\\BraveSoftware\\","\\Opera Software\\") | where InitiatingProcessFileName !in~ ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe","brave.exe","opera.exe","explorer.exe","searchprotocolhost.exe","backup.exe") | where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe","mshta.exe","rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe") | where InitiatingProcessAccountName !endswith "$" | project Timestamp, DeviceName, InitiatingProcessAccountName, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, FolderPath, FileName, ActionType | order by Timestamp desc
ImFileEvent | where TimeGenerated > ago(14d) | where TargetFileName in~ ("Login Data","Local State","logins.json","key4.db","cookies.sqlite","Cookies","Web Data") | where TargetFilePath has_any ("\\Google\\Chrome\\","\\Microsoft\\Edge\\","\\Mozilla\\Firefox\\","\\BraveSoftware\\","\\Opera Software\\") | where ActingProcessName has_any ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe","mshta.exe","rundll32.exe") | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, ActingProcessName, ActingProcessCommandLine, TargetFilePath, TargetFileName | order by TimeGenerated desc

[LLM] LegionRelay Telegram / WhatsApp messenger store exfiltration Actions on Objectives High
Hunts LegionRelay's messenger exfiltration capability: non-Telegram / non-WhatsApp processes reading Telegram Desktop's tdata vault or WhatsApp's Local Storage / msgstore. Article explicitly names Telegram and WhatsApp data exfiltration as core LegionRelay functionality. Rationale: WithSecure explicitly says LegionRelay supports 'Telegram and WhatsApp data exfiltration'. Anchors on the canonical Telegram tdata folder and WhatsApp Desktop Local Storage/IndexedDB layout, gated on non-messenger scripting/archiver parent to keep FP rate low. Cross-checked against: • https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1119/ • https://www.bleepingcomputer.com/news/security/greyvibe-hackers-use-chatgpt-gemini-to-power-cyberattacks/
ATT&CKT1119 T1005

ImFileEvent | where TimeGenerated > ago(14d) | where TargetFilePath has_any ("\\Telegram Desktop\\tdata\\","\\WhatsApp\\Local Storage\\","\\WhatsApp\\IndexedDB\\") or TargetFileName in~ ("key_datas","msgstore.db") | where ActingProcessName !has_any ("telegram.exe","whatsapp.exe") | where ActingProcessName has_any ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe","mshta.exe","7z.exe","winrar.exe") | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, ActingProcessName, ActingProcessCommandLine, TargetFilePath, TargetFileName | order by TimeGenerated desc

[LLM] GreyVibe: RDP enablement via fDenyTSConnections=0 + firewall by PowerShell RAT Installation High
Hunts LegionRelay's 'RDP access setup' capability: PowerShell or cmd flipping fDenyTSConnections to 0, enabling UserAuthentication, or opening the RDP firewall rule. Article explicitly calls out RDP access setup as a LegionRelay function and the attacker uses PowerShell-based RATs. Rationale: WithSecure: 'LegionRelay supports … RDP access setup.' Anchors on the canonical Windows knobs an attacker has to flip to enable RDP on a previously-disabled host: fDenyTSConnections=0 registry value, UserAuthentication relax, and the RemoteDesktop firewall group. Gated on a scripting-host parent because the article describes the actor as PowerShell-based. Cross-checked against: • https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1021/001/ • https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1562/004/ • https://www.bleepingcomputer.com/news/security/greyvibe-hackers-use-chatgpt-gemini-to-power-cyberattacks/

[LLM] PowerShell.exe sustained beaconing to uncategorized web endpoint (LegionRelay/PhantomRelay C2) Command & Control Medium
Hunts the LegionRelay/PhantomRelay PowerShell RAT C2 pattern: powershell.exe making repeated outbound HTTPS connections to a single rare external endpoint with no parent browser. Article describes both RATs as PowerShell-based with web C2 (UTC+3 panels, shared PrincessClub/DroneLink infra). Rationale: Both LegionRelay and PhantomRelay are described as PowerShell RATs and the C2 servers are on UTC+3 with web panels. Threshold + low-cardinality destination expresses 'beaconing' rather than one-shot egress. Doesn't reference specific IOCs from the article on purpose — actor rotates infra — but constrains pivot to powershell.exe initiated egress. Cross-checked against: • https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1071/001/ • https://www.bleepingcomputer.com/news/security/greyvibe-hackers-use-chatgpt-gemini-to-power-cyberattacks/
ATT&CKT1071.001 T1102

[LLM] GreyVibe cryptocurrency miner deployment via PowerShell RAT Actions on Objectives High
Hunts the cryptominer impact tail of the GreyVibe campaign: known miner binaries (xmrig, ethminer, t-rex, lolMiner) or Stratum protocol egress from victim machines. Article explicitly notes a cryptocurrency miner was deployed on some victim machines. Rationale: WithSecure: 'a cryptocurrency miner was deployed on some victim machines.' Anchors on the well-known XMRig/RandomX family + Stratum protocol strings + canonical mining pool ports (3333/4444/5555/7777/14444) and pool domains. Article didn't ship a specific miner SHA so we rely on family-level indicators. Cross-checked against: • https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1496/ • https://www.bleepingcomputer.com/news/security/greyvibe-hackers-use-chatgpt-gemini-to-power-cyberattacks/

Beaconing — periodic outbound to small set of destinations Command & Control Medium
C2 channel detection via inter-beacon-time stddev / fan-out to single dest.
ATT&CKT1071.001 T1071.004
Data sourcesNetwork_Traffic.All_Traffic DeviceNetworkEvents
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(1d)
| where RemoteIPType == "Public" and ActionType == "ConnectionSuccess"
| project DeviceName, RemoteIP, RemotePort, Timestamp
| sort by DeviceName asc, RemoteIP asc, RemotePort asc, Timestamp asc
| extend prev_dev = prev(DeviceName, 1), prev_ip = prev(RemoteIP, 1),
         prev_port = prev(RemotePort, 1), prev_ts = prev(Timestamp, 1)
| where DeviceName == prev_dev and RemoteIP == prev_ip and RemotePort == prev_port
| extend delta_sec = datetime_diff('second', Timestamp, prev_ts)
| summarize conn_count = count(), avg_delta = avg(delta_sec), stdev_delta = stdev(delta_sec)
    by DeviceName, RemoteIP, RemotePort
| where conn_count > 30 and avg_delta between (30.0 .. 600.0) and stdev_delta < 5.0
| order by conn_count desc
ImNetworkSession
| where TimeGenerated > ago(2h)
| where DvcAction != "Block"
| where ipv4_is_private(DstIpAddr) == false
| summarize ConnCount = count(),
            DistinctMinutes = dcount(bin(TimeGenerated, 1m))
            by DvcHostname, DstIpAddr, DstPortNumber
| where ConnCount > 50 and DistinctMinutes > 30   // sustained, not bursty
| order by ConnCount desc
NETWORK
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count, values(All_Traffic.dest_port) AS ports
    from datamodel=Network_Traffic.All_Traffic
    where All_Traffic.action="allowed" AND All_Traffic.dest_category!="internal"
    by _time span=10s, All_Traffic.src, All_Traffic.dest
| `drop_dm_object_name(All_Traffic)`
| streamstats current=f last(_time) AS prev_time by src, dest
| eval delta = _time - prev_time
| stats avg(delta) AS avg_delta stdev(delta) AS sd_delta count by src, dest
| where count > 30 AND sd_delta < 5 AND avg_delta>=30 AND avg_delta<=600
| sort - count
| tstats summariesonly=false count, values(All_Traffic.dest_port) AS ports

Phishing-link click correlated to endpoint execution Delivery High
User received an external email containing a URL, clicked it, and within 60 seconds the recipient's endpoint spawned a scripting interpreter or network downloader (PowerShell / cmd / mshta / curl / certutil / bitsadmin). This is the high-fidelity shape — a raw "user clicked an emailed URL" query is too noisy to alert on because every Microsoft 365 tenant generates thousands of legitimate clicks per day. The exec-correlation step suppresses the noise to roughly the rate at which a click actually drives onto-host execution, which is the actionable signal. Pair with UC_PHISH_LINK_BYPASS (Safe Links override) and UC_PHISH_LINK_NEWDOMAIN for orthogonal high-fidelity variants.
ATT&CKT1566.002 T1204.001 T1059.001
Data sourcesEmail.All_Email Web Endpoint.Processes EmailEvents EmailUrlInfo UrlClickEvents DeviceProcessEvents
// Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s.
// Far higher fidelity than "every clicked URL" — most legitimate clicks
// never spawn a non-browser child process, so the join eliminates the
// 99% of noise that makes a raw click query unactionable.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let SuspectClicks = UrlClickEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where AccountName !endswith "$"
    | where ActionType in ("ClickAllowed","ClickedThrough")
    | join kind=inner (
        EmailEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
        | where DeliveryAction == "Delivered"
        | where EmailDirection == "Inbound"
        | project NetworkMessageId, Subject, SenderFromAddress, SenderFromDomain,
                  RecipientEmailAddress, EmailTimestamp = Timestamp
      ) on NetworkMessageId
    | join kind=leftouter (
        EmailUrlInfo | project NetworkMessageId, Url, UrlDomain
      ) on NetworkMessageId, Url
    | project ClickTime = Timestamp, AccountUpn, IPAddress, Url, UrlDomain,
              Subject, SenderFromAddress, SenderFromDomain, RecipientEmailAddress,
              ActionType;
// Correlate to a non-browser child process spawned within 60 seconds on
// the recipient's device.
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                         "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
| where FileName in~ ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                        "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe",
                        "bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe","curl.exe","wget.exe")
| join kind=inner SuspectClicks on $left.AccountName == $right.AccountUpn
| where Timestamp between (ClickTime .. ClickTime + 60s)
| project ClickTime, ProcessTime = Timestamp,
          DelaySec = datetime_diff('second', Timestamp, ClickTime),
          DeviceName, AccountName, RecipientEmailAddress, SenderFromAddress,
          Subject, Url, UrlDomain, ActionType,
          FileName, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFileName
| order by ClickTime desc
// UrlClickEvents has no clean Sentinel-native equivalent. The detection
// pivots to: Office Send→Receive proximity to SecurityEvent 4688 of a
// non-browser child process. Lower fidelity than the Defender version.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let SuspectMailUsers = OfficeActivity
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where OfficeWorkload == "Exchange"
    | where Operation =~ "Receive"
    | summarize Subject = any(Subject), Sender = any(Sender)
                by MailboxOwnerUPN, MessageId, EmailTime = bin(TimeGenerated, 1m);
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
| where EventID == 4688
| where ParentProcessName has_any ("\chrome.exe","\msedge.exe",
                                     "\firefox.exe","\outlook.exe","\brave.exe")
| where NewProcessName has_any ("\powershell.exe","\pwsh.exe","\cmd.exe",
                                  "\mshta.exe","\rundll32.exe","\regsvr32.exe",
                                  "\wscript.exe","\cscript.exe","\bitsadmin.exe",
                                  "\certutil.exe","\curl.exe","\wget.exe")
| join kind=inner SuspectMailUsers on $left.Account == $right.MailboxOwnerUPN
| where TimeGenerated between (EmailTime .. EmailTime + 60s)
| project TimeGenerated, EmailTime, Computer, Account, ParentProcessName,
          NewProcessName, CommandLine, Sender, Subject
| order by TimeGenerated desc
WEB
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
``` Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s ```
| tstats `summariesonly` earliest(_time) AS click_time
    from datamodel=Web
    where Web.action="allowed"
    by Web.src, Web.user, Web.dest, Web.url
| `drop_dm_object_name(Web)`
| rename user AS recipient, dest AS clicked_domain, url AS clicked_url
| join type=inner recipient
    [| tstats `summariesonly` count
         from datamodel=Email.All_Email
         where All_Email.action="delivered" AND All_Email.url!="-"
         by All_Email.recipient, All_Email.src_user, All_Email.url, All_Email.subject
     | `drop_dm_object_name(All_Email)`
     | rex field=url "https?://(?<email_domain>[^/]+)"
     | rename recipient AS recipient]
| join type=inner src
    [| tstats `summariesonly` earliest(_time) AS exec_time
         values(Processes.process) AS exec_cmd, values(Processes.process_name) AS exec_proc
         from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
         where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                                   "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
           AND Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                                            "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe",
                                            "cscript.exe","bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe",
                                            "curl.exe","wget.exe")
         by Processes.dest, Processes.user
     | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
     | rename dest AS src]
| eval delta_sec = exec_time - click_time
| where delta_sec >= 0 AND delta_sec <= 60
| table click_time, exec_time, delta_sec, recipient, src, src_user, subject,
        clicked_domain, clicked_url, exec_proc, exec_cmd
| sort - click_time

Email attachment opened from external sender Delivery High
Attachment delivery + execution by recipient — most common malware initial access.
ATT&CKT1566.001 T1204.002
Data sourcesEmail.All_Email Endpoint.Processes EmailAttachmentInfo DeviceProcessEvents
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let MalAttachments = EmailAttachmentInfo
    | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where AccountName !endswith "$"
    | project NetworkMessageId, RecipientEmailAddress,
              AttachmentFileName = FileName, AttachmentSHA256 = SHA256;
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("OUTLOOK.EXE","winword.exe","excel.exe","powerpnt.exe")
| where FileName in~ ("cmd.exe","powershell.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe",
                      "mshta.exe","rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe")
| join kind=inner MalAttachments on $left.AccountUpn == $right.RecipientEmailAddress
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, FileName, ProcessCommandLine,
          InitiatingProcessFileName, AttachmentFileName, AttachmentSHA256
// Sentinel doesn't have an attachment-hash table. Best approximation:
// OfficeActivity Send/Receive activity + correlate to host process spawn.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let MailWithAttach = OfficeActivity
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where OfficeWorkload == "Exchange"
    | where Operation in~ ("Send","Receive")
    | where isnotempty(MessageId)
    | project EmailTime = TimeGenerated, MailboxOwnerUPN, Sender,
              Recipients, Subject, MessageId;
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
| where EventID == 4688
| where ParentProcessName endswith "OUTLOOK.EXE"
| where NewProcessName endswith "\cmd.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\powershell.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\wscript.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\cscript.exe"

Actions on Objectives
Likely
Reconnaissance. Attacker researches the target — OSINT, scanning, enumeration.
Weaponization. Coupling exploit code with deliverable payload (e.g. weaponized PDF/Office doc, trojanized installer).
Delivery. Transmitting the weapon (phishing email, USB, watering hole, drive-by, malicious ad). → Phishing-link click correlated to endpoint execution · Email attachment opened from external sender
Exploitation. Triggering the exploit — vulnerability/macro/trust abuse to execute code. → Office app spawning script/LOLBin child process
Installation. Establishing persistence on the host — backdoor, service, scheduled task, registry key. → File hash IOCs — endpoint file/process match
Command & Control. Beacon to attacker infrastructure for control and tasking. → Network connections to article IPs / domains
Actions on Objectives. Lateral movement, credential dumping, data theft, ransomware, sabotage.
Phishing-link click correlated to endpoint execution Delivery High
User received an external email containing a URL, clicked it, and within 60 seconds the recipient's endpoint spawned a scripting interpreter or network downloader (PowerShell / cmd / mshta / curl / certutil / bitsadmin). This is the high-fidelity shape — a raw "user clicked an emailed URL" query is too noisy to alert on because every Microsoft 365 tenant generates thousands of legitimate clicks per day. The exec-correlation step suppresses the noise to roughly the rate at which a click actually drives onto-host execution, which is the actionable signal. Pair with UC_PHISH_LINK_BYPASS (Safe Links override) and UC_PHISH_LINK_NEWDOMAIN for orthogonal high-fidelity variants.
ATT&CKT1566.002 T1204.001 T1059.001
Data sourcesEmail.All_Email Web Endpoint.Processes EmailEvents EmailUrlInfo UrlClickEvents DeviceProcessEvents
// Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s.
// Far higher fidelity than "every clicked URL" — most legitimate clicks
// never spawn a non-browser child process, so the join eliminates the
// 99% of noise that makes a raw click query unactionable.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let SuspectClicks = UrlClickEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where AccountName !endswith "$"
    | where ActionType in ("ClickAllowed","ClickedThrough")
    | join kind=inner (
        EmailEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
        | where DeliveryAction == "Delivered"
        | where EmailDirection == "Inbound"
        | project NetworkMessageId, Subject, SenderFromAddress, SenderFromDomain,
                  RecipientEmailAddress, EmailTimestamp = Timestamp
      ) on NetworkMessageId
    | join kind=leftouter (
        EmailUrlInfo | project NetworkMessageId, Url, UrlDomain
      ) on NetworkMessageId, Url
    | project ClickTime = Timestamp, AccountUpn, IPAddress, Url, UrlDomain,
              Subject, SenderFromAddress, SenderFromDomain, RecipientEmailAddress,
              ActionType;
// Correlate to a non-browser child process spawned within 60 seconds on
// the recipient's device.
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                         "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
| where FileName in~ ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                        "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe",
                        "bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe","curl.exe","wget.exe")
| join kind=inner SuspectClicks on $left.AccountName == $right.AccountUpn
| where Timestamp between (ClickTime .. ClickTime + 60s)
| project ClickTime, ProcessTime = Timestamp,
          DelaySec = datetime_diff('second', Timestamp, ClickTime),
          DeviceName, AccountName, RecipientEmailAddress, SenderFromAddress,
          Subject, Url, UrlDomain, ActionType,
          FileName, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFileName
| order by ClickTime desc
// UrlClickEvents has no clean Sentinel-native equivalent. The detection
// pivots to: Office Send→Receive proximity to SecurityEvent 4688 of a
// non-browser child process. Lower fidelity than the Defender version.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let SuspectMailUsers = OfficeActivity
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where OfficeWorkload == "Exchange"
    | where Operation =~ "Receive"
    | summarize Subject = any(Subject), Sender = any(Sender)
                by MailboxOwnerUPN, MessageId, EmailTime = bin(TimeGenerated, 1m);
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
| where EventID == 4688
| where ParentProcessName has_any ("\chrome.exe","\msedge.exe",
                                     "\firefox.exe","\outlook.exe","\brave.exe")
| where NewProcessName has_any ("\powershell.exe","\pwsh.exe","\cmd.exe",
                                  "\mshta.exe","\rundll32.exe","\regsvr32.exe",
                                  "\wscript.exe","\cscript.exe","\bitsadmin.exe",
                                  "\certutil.exe","\curl.exe","\wget.exe")
| join kind=inner SuspectMailUsers on $left.Account == $right.MailboxOwnerUPN
| where TimeGenerated between (EmailTime .. EmailTime + 60s)
| project TimeGenerated, EmailTime, Computer, Account, ParentProcessName,
          NewProcessName, CommandLine, Sender, Subject
| order by TimeGenerated desc

| tstats `summariesonly` earliest(_time) AS click_time
    from datamodel=Web

    by Web.src, Web.user, Web.dest, Web.url
| `drop_dm_object_name(Web)`

    [| tstats `summariesonly` earliest(_time) AS exec_time
         values(Processes.process) AS exec_cmd, values(Processes.process_name) AS exec_proc
         from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
         where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",

| where delta_sec >= 0 AND delta_sec <= 60

// Sentinel doesn't have an attachment-hash table. Best approximation:

| tstats `summariesonly` count
    from datamodel=Email.All_Email
    where All_Email.file_name!="-"
    by All_Email.src_user, All_Email.recipient, All_Email.file_name, All_Email.subject
| rename All_Email.recipient as user
| join type=inner user
    [| tstats `summariesonly` count
        from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
        where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("OUTLOOK.EXE","winword.exe","excel.exe","powerpnt.exe")
          AND Processes.process_name IN ("cmd.exe","powershell.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe","mshta.exe","rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe")
        by Processes.dest, Processes.user, Processes.parent_process_name, Processes.process_name, Processes.process
     | rename Processes.user as user]
| tstats summariesonly=false count
    from datamodel=Email.All_Email
    where All_Email.file_name!="-"
    by All_Email.src_user, All_Email.recipient, All_Email.file_name, All_Email.subject
| rename All_Email.recipient as user
| join type=inner user
    [| tstats summariesonly=false count
        from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
        where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("OUTLOOK.EXE","winword.exe","excel.exe","powerpnt.exe")
          AND Processes.process_name IN ("cmd.exe","powershell.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe","mshta.exe","rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe")
        by Processes.dest, Processes.user, Processes.parent_process_name, Processes.process_name, Processes.process
     | rename Processes.user as user]
Office app spawning script/LOLBin child process Exploitation High
Classic macro/exploit pattern — Office app launching cmd/powershell/wmic/regsvr32.
ATT&CKT1059.001 T1059.005 T1218
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes DeviceProcessEvents
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where AccountName !endswith "$"
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("winword.exe","excel.exe","powerpnt.exe","outlook.exe","onenote.exe","mspub.exe","visio.exe")
| where FileName in~ ("cmd.exe","powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe","mshta.exe","rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wmic.exe","bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, InitiatingProcessFileName, FileName, ProcessCommandLine
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where EventID == 4688
| where Account !endswith "$"
| where ParentProcessName endswith "\winword.exe"
   or ParentProcessName endswith "\excel.exe"
   or ParentProcessName endswith "\powerpnt.exe"
   or ParentProcessName endswith "\outlook.exe"
   or ParentProcessName endswith "\onenote.exe"
   or ParentProcessName endswith "\mspub.exe"
   or ParentProcessName endswith "\visio.exe"
| where NewProcessName endswith "\cmd.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\powershell.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\pwsh.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\wscript.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\cscript.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\mshta.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\rundll32.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\regsvr32.exe"
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, Account, ParentProcessName,
          NewProcessName, CommandLine
| order by TimeGenerated desc

title: Office Application Spawning Script Host
id: 7c8b2e10-4d4f-4a8c-9c1f-bf6e2c4a8d07
status: experimental
description: |
    Word/Excel/Outlook/OneNote spawning powershell, cmd, wscript,
    cscript, mshta, rundll32, regsvr32 — classic macro / embedded-
    object payload signature.
references:
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1059/
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1566/001/
author: Clankerusecase
date: 2026/05/02
tags:
    - attack.t1059
    - attack.t1566.001
    - attack.execution
logsource:
    category: process_creation
    product: windows
detection:
    selection_parent:
        ParentImage|endswith:
            - '\winword.exe'
            - '\excel.exe'
            - '\powerpnt.exe'
            - '\outlook.exe'
            - '\onenote.exe'
            - '\mspub.exe'
            - '\visio.exe'
    selection_child:
        Image|endswith:
            - '\cmd.exe'
            - '\powershell.exe'
            - '\pwsh.exe'
            - '\wscript.exe'
            - '\cscript.exe'
            - '\mshta.exe'
            - '\rundll32.exe'
            - '\regsvr32.exe'
    condition: selection_parent and selection_child
falsepositives:
    - Legitimate automation macros in trusted internal documents
level: high
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
    where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("winword.exe","excel.exe","powerpnt.exe","outlook.exe","onenote.exe","mspub.exe","visio.exe")
      AND Processes.process_name IN ("cmd.exe","powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe","mshta.exe","rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wmic.exe","bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe")
    by Processes.dest, Processes.user, Processes.parent_process_name, Processes.process_name, Processes.process
| `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
| `security_content_ctime(firstTime)` | `security_content_ctime(lastTime)`
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
    where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("winword.exe","excel.exe","powerpnt.exe","outlook.exe","onenote.exe","mspub.exe","visio.exe")
      AND Processes.process_name IN ("cmd.exe","powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe","mshta.exe","rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wmic.exe","bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe")
    by Processes.dest, Processes.user, Processes.parent_process_name, Processes.process_name, Processes.process
| `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
| `security_content_ctime(firstTime)` | `security_content_ctime(lastTime)`
Network connections to article IPs / domains Command & Control High
Outbound traffic to attacker infrastructure named in the article.
ATT&CKT1071
Data sourcesNetwork_Traffic.All_Traffic Web Network_Resolution.DNS DeviceNetworkEvents
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where RemoteIP in ("78.135.93.123", "79.133.57.141", "178.156.177.192", "191.101.131.250", "195.160.221.203", "191.96.224.87", "191.96.225.241", "191.96.78.172", "191.96.78.28", "191.96.79.133", "191.96.79.179", "191.96.79.41", "200.9.155.153") or RemoteUrl has_any ("arbsniper.com")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, RemoteIP, RemotePort, RemoteUrl,
          InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine
let BadIPs     = dynamic(["78.135.93.123", "79.133.57.141", "178.156.177.192", "191.101.131.250", "195.160.221.203", "191.96.224.87", "191.96.225.241", "191.96.78.172", "191.96.78.28", "191.96.79.133", "191.96.79.179", "191.96.79.41", "200.9.155.153"]);
let BadDomains = dynamic(["arbsniper.com"]);
ImNetworkSession
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where DstIpAddr in (BadIPs)
   or Url has_any (BadDomains)
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, DstIpAddr, DstPortNumber, Url, NetworkProtocol
| order by TimeGenerated desc

title: Outbound Connection to Article-Named IP / Domain
id: 7c8b2e10-4d4f-4a8c-9c1f-bf6e2c4a8d0f
status: experimental
description: |
    Replace `__IP_LIST__` / `__DOMAIN_LIST__` placeholders with
    article-specific destinations. For dynamic IOC management, use a
    watchlist or external feed.
references:
    - https://attack.mitre.org/tactics/TA0011/
author: Clankerusecase
date: 2026/05/02
tags:
    - attack.command-and-control
logsource:
    category: network_connection
    product: windows
detection:
    selection_ip:
        DestinationIp:
            - '__IP_PLACEHOLDER_1__'
            - '__IP_PLACEHOLDER_2__'
    selection_domain:
        DestinationHostname:
            - '__DOMAIN_PLACEHOLDER_1__'
            - '__DOMAIN_PLACEHOLDER_2__'
    condition: selection_ip or selection_domain
falsepositives:
    - None on a true-positive IOC match
level: critical
NETWORK
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Network_Traffic.All_Traffic
    where All_Traffic.dest IN ("78.135.93.123", "79.133.57.141", "178.156.177.192", "191.101.131.250", "195.160.221.203", "191.96.224.87", "191.96.225.241", "191.96.78.172", "191.96.78.28", "191.96.79.133", "191.96.79.179", "191.96.79.41", "200.9.155.153")
    by All_Traffic.src, All_Traffic.dest, All_Traffic.dest_port
| `drop_dm_object_name(All_Traffic)`
| append
    [| tstats `summariesonly` count from datamodel=Web
        where Web.dest IN ("arbsniper.com")
        by Web.src, Web.dest, Web.url, Web.user
     | `drop_dm_object_name(Web)`]
| append
    [| tstats `summariesonly` count from datamodel=Network_Resolution.DNS
        where DNS.query IN ("arbsniper.com")
        by DNS.src, DNS.query, DNS.answer
     | `drop_dm_object_name(DNS)`]
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Network_Traffic.All_Traffic
    where All_Traffic.dest IN ("78.135.93.123", "79.133.57.141", "178.156.177.192", "191.101.131.250", "195.160.221.203", "191.96.224.87", "191.96.225.241", "191.96.78.172", "191.96.78.28", "191.96.79.133", "191.96.79.179", "191.96.79.41", "200.9.155.153")
    by All_Traffic.src, All_Traffic.dest, All_Traffic.dest_port
| `drop_dm_object_name(All_Traffic)`
| append
    [| tstats summariesonly=false count from datamodel=Web
        where Web.dest IN ("arbsniper.com")
        by Web.src, Web.dest, Web.url, Web.user
     | `drop_dm_object_name(Web)`]
| append
    [| tstats summariesonly=false count from datamodel=Network_Resolution.DNS
        where DNS.query IN ("arbsniper.com")
        by DNS.src, DNS.query, DNS.answer
     | `drop_dm_object_name(DNS)`]

status: experimental
description: |

    at scale.

Detected
Reconnaissance. Attacker researches the target — OSINT, scanning, enumeration.
Weaponization. Coupling exploit code with deliverable payload (e.g. weaponized PDF/Office doc, trojanized installer).
Delivery. Transmitting the weapon (phishing email, USB, watering hole, drive-by, malicious ad). → [LLM] DNS/HTTP traffic to Ghost Stadium FIFA typosquat domains (2026 World Cup fraud) · [LLM] Browser navigation to FIFA-themed look-alike hostname (typosquat pattern hunt) · Phishing-link click correlated to endpoint execution · Email attachment opened from external sender
Exploitation. Triggering the exploit — vulnerability/macro/trust abuse to execute code. → Office app spawning script/LOLBin child process
Installation. Establishing persistence on the host — backdoor, service, scheduled task, registry key. → File hash IOCs — endpoint file/process match
Command & Control. Beacon to attacker infrastructure for control and tasking. → [LLM] Outbound connection to Ghost Stadium FIFA fraud staging IPs · Network connections to article IPs / domains
Actions on Objectives. Lateral movement, credential dumping, data theft, ransomware, sabotage. → [LLM] Risky AAD sign-in after user contact with FIFA typosquat phishing portal
[LLM] DNS/HTTP traffic to Ghost Stadium FIFA typosquat domains (2026 World Cup fraud) Delivery High
Hunts for endpoint resolution or HTTP requests to the eight FIFA look-alike domains called out in the FBI 2026 World Cup PSA and Group-IB's Ghost Stadium reporting. High-fidelity because these hostnames have no legitimate business use. Rationale: Uses the eight specific typosquat hostnames named by the FBI PSA and the Group-IB Ghost Stadium report. Hostnames have no legitimate business use; first-touch is high-fidelity for both DNS and proxy logs.
ATT&CKT1566.002 T1189 T1583.001
Data sourcesWeb Network_Resolution
let TyposquatDomains = dynamic(["fiffa.com","jobs-fifa.com","fifa-hiring.com","filfa.org","wvvw-fifa.com","ww-fifa.com","fifa-hr.com","fifa-careerhub.com"]);
let NetHits = DeviceNetworkEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(14d)
    | where RemoteUrl has_any (TyposquatDomains)
    | project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountUpn=InitiatingProcessAccountUpn, InitiatingProcessFileName, RemoteUrl, RemoteIP, Source="DeviceNetworkEvents";
let ClickHits = UrlClickEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(14d)
    | where Url has_any (TyposquatDomains)
    | project Timestamp, DeviceName="", AccountUpn, InitiatingProcessFileName="", RemoteUrl=Url, RemoteIP="", Source="UrlClickEvents";
union NetHits, ClickHits
| order by Timestamp desc
let TyposquatDomains = dynamic(["fiffa.com","jobs-fifa.com","fifa-hiring.com","filfa.org","wvvw-fifa.com","ww-fifa.com","fifa-hr.com","fifa-careerhub.com"]);
union
(DnsEvents | where TimeGenerated > ago(14d) | where Name has_any (TyposquatDomains) | project TimeGenerated, Computer, ClientIP, Host=Name, Source="DNS"),
(CommonSecurityLog | where TimeGenerated > ago(14d) | where RequestURL has_any (TyposquatDomains) or DestinationHostName has_any (TyposquatDomains) | project TimeGenerated, Computer=SourceHostName, ClientIP=SourceIP, Host=coalesce(DestinationHostName,RequestURL), Source="Proxy"),
(W3CIISLog | where TimeGenerated > ago(14d) | where csReferer has_any (TyposquatDomains) | project TimeGenerated, Computer, ClientIP=cIP, Host=csReferer, Source="IIS-Referer")
| order by TimeGenerated desc
title: FIFA Typosquat Domain Lookup (Ghost Stadium 2026 World Cup Fraud)
id: 7a4b9e6e-1c2f-4b9d-8e5a-d4d2f5e3b6a1
description: Detects DNS resolution or HTTP traffic to FIFA typosquat domains associated with the FBI 2026 World Cup PSA and Group-IB's Ghost Stadium campaign.
references:
  - https://www.bleepingcomputer.com/news/security/fbi-warns-of-fake-fifa-websites-running-world-cup-fraud-schemes/
author: SOC Detection Engineering
date: 2026/05/28
tags:
  - attack.initial_access
  - attack.t1566.002
  - attack.t1189
  - attack.t1583.001
logsource:
  category: dns
detection:
  selection:
    query|contains:
      - 'fiffa.com'
      - 'jobs-fifa.com'
      - 'fifa-hiring.com'
      - 'filfa.org'
      - 'wvvw-fifa.com'
      - 'ww-fifa.com'
      - 'fifa-hr.com'
      - 'fifa-careerhub.com'
  condition: selection
falsepositives:
  - Threat-intel analysts pivoting on IOCs
  - Email-security sandbox detonation
level: high
(@network.destination.domain:(fiffa.com OR jobs-fifa.com OR fifa-hiring.com OR filfa.org OR wvvw-fifa.com OR ww-fifa.com OR fifa-hr.com OR fifa-careerhub.com) OR @http.url_details.host:(fiffa.com OR jobs-fifa.com OR fifa-hiring.com OR filfa.org OR wvvw-fifa.com OR ww-fifa.com OR fifa-hr.com OR fifa-careerhub.com) OR @dns.question.name:(fiffa.com OR jobs-fifa.com OR fifa-hiring.com OR filfa.org OR wvvw-fifa.com OR ww-fifa.com OR fifa-hr.com OR fifa-careerhub.com))
#event_simpleName=DnsRequest DomainName=/^(fiffa\.com|jobs-fifa\.com|fifa-hiring\.com|filfa\.org|wvvw-fifa\.com|ww-fifa\.com|fifa-hr\.com|fifa-careerhub\.com)$/i
| groupBy([aid, ComputerName, DomainName, ContextImageFileName], function=count())

| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime values(Web.url) as urls values(Web.http_referrer) as referrers from datamodel=Web where (Web.dest IN ("fiffa.com","jobs-fifa.com","fifa-hiring.com","filfa.org","wvvw-fifa.com","ww-fifa.com","fifa-hr.com","fifa-careerhub.com") OR Web.url="*fiffa.com*" OR Web.url="*jobs-fifa.com*" OR Web.url="*fifa-hiring.com*" OR Web.url="*filfa.org*" OR Web.url="*wvvw-fifa.com*" OR Web.url="*ww-fifa.com*" OR Web.url="*fifa-hr.com*" OR Web.url="*fifa-careerhub.com*") by Web.src, Web.user, Web.dest | `drop_dm_object_name(Web)` | convert ctime(firstTime) ctime(lastTime)
[LLM] Outbound connection to Ghost Stadium FIFA fraud staging IPs Command & Control High
Alerts when any internal host establishes an outbound connection to the eight staging IPs that host the cloned FIFA ticketing/employment/merchandise portals. Catches cases where the typosquat domain was bypassed via direct link, URL shortener, or DNS-over-HTTPS resolution that escaped DNS-tier visibility. Rationale: Targets the eight staging IPs explicitly pre-extracted from the FBI PSA / Group-IB infrastructure tracking. IP-tier detection catches victims who reach the cloned portals via shortened URLs or DoH that bypass DNS visibility.
ATT&CKT1071.001 T1583.003
Data sourcesNetwork_Traffic
let StagingIPs = dynamic(["148.178.18.23","148.178.18.60","154.86.0.33","207.56.1.93","66.112.212.25","148.178.16.48","148.178.16.5","104.225.235.49"]);
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(30d)
| where RemoteIP in (StagingIPs)
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountUpn=InitiatingProcessAccountUpn, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, RemoteIP, RemotePort, RemoteUrl, Protocol
| order by Timestamp desc
let StagingIPs = dynamic(["148.178.18.23","148.178.18.60","154.86.0.33","207.56.1.93","66.112.212.25","148.178.16.48","148.178.16.5","104.225.235.49"]);
CommonSecurityLog
| where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
| where DestinationIP in (StagingIPs) or SourceIP in (StagingIPs)
| project TimeGenerated, DeviceVendor, DeviceProduct, SourceIP, SourceUserName, DestinationIP, DestinationPort, RequestURL, DestinationHostName, DeviceAction
| order by TimeGenerated desc
title: Outbound Connection to Ghost Stadium FIFA Fraud Staging IPs
id: c2e1f4a8-7d3b-4c2e-9f1a-3b8e6c4d2a5f
description: Detects outbound network connections to the eight staging IPs hosting cloned FIFA ticketing/employment/merch portals (FBI PSA May 2026, Group-IB Ghost Stadium).
references:
  - https://www.bleepingcomputer.com/news/security/fbi-warns-of-fake-fifa-websites-running-world-cup-fraud-schemes/

date: 2026/05/28

  - attack.t1071.001
  - attack.t1583.003
logsource:
  category: network_connection
  product: windows
detection:
  selection:
    DestinationIp:
      - '148.178.18.23'
      - '148.178.18.60'
      - '154.86.0.33'
      - '207.56.1.93'
      - '66.112.212.25'
      - '148.178.16.48'
      - '148.178.16.5'
      - '104.225.235.49'
  condition: selection

level: high
(@network.destination.ip:(148.178.18.23 OR 148.178.18.60 OR 154.86.0.33 OR 207.56.1.93 OR 66.112.212.25 OR 148.178.16.48 OR 148.178.16.5 OR 104.225.235.49) OR @DestinationIp:(148.178.18.23 OR 148.178.18.60 OR 154.86.0.33 OR 207.56.1.93 OR 66.112.212.25 OR 148.178.16.48 OR 148.178.16.5 OR 104.225.235.49))
#event_simpleName=NetworkConnectIP4 RemoteAddressIP4=/^(148\.178\.18\.23|148\.178\.18\.60|154\.86\.0\.33|207\.56\.1\.93|66\.112\.212\.25|148\.178\.16\.48|148\.178\.16\.5|104\.225\.235\.49)$/
| groupBy([aid, ComputerName, RemoteAddressIP4, RemotePort, ContextImageFileName, ContextProcessId], function=count())
# log group: /aws/vpc/flowlogs
fields @timestamp, srcAddr, dstAddr, dstPort, protocol, bytes, action, accountId, interfaceId
| filter dstAddr in ["148.178.18.23","148.178.18.60","154.86.0.33","207.56.1.93","66.112.212.25","148.178.16.48","148.178.16.5","104.225.235.49"]
      and action = "ACCEPT"
| stats count(*) as flows, sum(bytes) as totalBytes by srcAddr, dstAddr, dstPort
| sort flows desc

| tstats summariesonly=t count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime values(All_Traffic.dest_port) as ports values(All_Traffic.app) as apps from datamodel=Network_Traffic where All_Traffic.dest IN ("148.178.18.23","148.178.18.60","154.86.0.33","207.56.1.93","66.112.212.25","148.178.16.48","148.178.16.5","104.225.235.49") by All_Traffic.src, All_Traffic.user, All_Traffic.dest | `drop_dm_object_name(All_Traffic)` | convert ctime(firstTime) ctime(lastTime)
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime values(All_Traffic.dest_port) as ports values(All_Traffic.app) as apps from datamodel=Network_Traffic where All_Traffic.dest IN ("148.178.18.23","148.178.18.60","154.86.0.33","207.56.1.93","66.112.212.25","148.178.16.48","148.178.16.5","104.225.235.49") by All_Traffic.src, All_Traffic.user, All_Traffic.dest | `drop_dm_object_name(All_Traffic)` | convert ctime(firstTime) ctime(lastTime)
[LLM] Browser navigation to FIFA-themed look-alike hostname (typosquat pattern hunt) Delivery Medium
Hunting query that surfaces browser traffic to any domain matching the FIFA typosquat pattern family (extra/missing letters, hyphenated subbrands like -hiring/-hr/-careerhub/-ticket, doubled-W prefixes) excluding the legitimate fifa.com/fifa.org. Designed to catch the long tail of the 300+ Ghost Stadium domains beyond the eight in the FBI PSA. Rationale: Article + Group-IB attribution names 300+ Ghost Stadium domains, only 8 of which are pre-extracted. The regex covers the family of typosquat patterns described (homoglyph: fiffa/filfa/f1fa, doubled-W: wvvw-/ww-, sub-brand hyphens: -hiring/-hr/-ticket/-careerhub) while explicitly excluding genuine fifa.com/fifa.org.
ATT&CKT1566.002 T1583.001 T1036.005
Data sourcesWeb
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(30d)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe","brave.exe","opera.exe")
| where isnotempty(RemoteUrl)
| extend Hostname = tolower(tostring(parse_url(RemoteUrl)["Host"]))
| where Hostname matches regex @"(fiff[ai]|filfa|f1fa|fifaa|wvvw-?fifa|ww-?fifa|fifa-?(hiring|hr|ticket|tickets|careers?|careerhub|jobs|hospitality|online|com|worldcup|world-cup|2026|store|merch|panini))"
| where Hostname != "fifa.com" and Hostname != "fifa.org" and Hostname !endswith ".fifa.com" and Hostname !endswith ".fifa.org"
| summarize HitCount=count(), FirstSeen=min(Timestamp), LastSeen=max(Timestamp), Devices=dcount(DeviceName), Users=dcount(InitiatingProcessAccountUpn), SampleUrls=make_set(RemoteUrl, 5) by Hostname
| order by FirstSeen desc
let LookalikeRegex = @"(?i)(fiff[ai]|filfa|f1fa|fifaa|wvvw-?fifa|ww-?fifa|fifa-?(hiring|hr|ticket|tickets|careers?|careerhub|jobs|hospitality|online|com|worldcup|world-cup|2026|store|merch|panini))";
union
(CommonSecurityLog | where TimeGenerated > ago(30d) | where DestinationHostName matches regex LookalikeRegex or RequestURL matches regex LookalikeRegex | extend Host=tolower(DestinationHostName) | where Host != "fifa.com" and Host != "fifa.org" and Host !endswith ".fifa.com" and Host !endswith ".fifa.org" | project TimeGenerated, SourceIP, SourceUserName, Host, RequestURL, Source="Proxy"),
(DnsEvents | where TimeGenerated > ago(30d) | where Name matches regex LookalikeRegex | extend Host=tolower(Name) | where Host != "fifa.com" and Host != "fifa.org" and Host !endswith ".fifa.com" and Host !endswith ".fifa.org" | project TimeGenerated, SourceIP=ClientIP, SourceUserName="", Host, RequestURL="", Source="DNS")
| summarize HitCount=count(), FirstSeen=min(TimeGenerated), LastSeen=max(TimeGenerated), Sources=dcount(SourceIP) by Host
| order by FirstSeen desc
(@http.url_details.host:*fifa* OR @network.destination.domain:*fifa* OR @dns.question.name:*fifa*) AND -@http.url_details.host:(fifa.com OR www.fifa.com OR fifa.org OR www.fifa.org) AND -@network.destination.domain:(fifa.com OR www.fifa.com OR fifa.org OR www.fifa.org) AND -@dns.question.name:(fifa.com OR www.fifa.com OR fifa.org OR www.fifa.org)
#event_simpleName=DnsRequest
| regex("(fiff[ai]|filfa|f1fa|fifaa|wvvw-?fifa|ww-?fifa|fifa-?(hiring|hr|ticket|tickets|careers?|careerhub|jobs|hospitality|online|com|worldcup|world-cup|2026|store|merch|panini))", field=DomainName, flags="i")
| DomainName!=/^(www\.)?fifa\.(com|org)$/i
| groupBy([DomainName], function={ count() | dcount(field=aid, as=hosts) | min(_time, as=firstSeen) })
WEB

[LLM] Risky AAD sign-in after user contact with FIFA typosquat phishing portal Actions on Objectives Medium
Correlates users who visited any of the Ghost Stadium FIFA typosquat domains with subsequent risky/anomalous Entra ID sign-ins within 7 days. Targets the post-credential-submission account-takeover pivot described in the article ('create fraudulent accounts, commit identity theft'). Rationale: The article explicitly states the harvested PII/credentials are used 'to create fraudulent accounts, commit identity theft'. Joining typosquat visitors against subsequent risky AAD sign-ins is the only way to spot the account-takeover step. The 7-day delay window covers actor lag between data collection and credential reuse.
ATT&CKT1078.004 T1556 T1539
Data sourcesAuthentication Web
let TyposquatDomains = dynamic(["fiffa.com","jobs-fifa.com","fifa-hiring.com","filfa.org","wvvw-fifa.com","ww-fifa.com","fifa-hr.com","fifa-careerhub.com"]);
let Visitors = union
    (DeviceNetworkEvents | where Timestamp > ago(14d) | where RemoteUrl has_any (TyposquatDomains) | where isnotempty(InitiatingProcessAccountUpn) | project VisitTime=Timestamp, AccountUpn=tolower(InitiatingProcessAccountUpn), DeviceName, VisitedHost=RemoteUrl),
    (UrlClickEvents | where Timestamp > ago(14d) | where Url has_any (TyposquatDomains) | where isnotempty(AccountUpn) | project VisitTime=Timestamp, AccountUpn=tolower(AccountUpn), DeviceName="", VisitedHost=Url);
AADSignInEventsBeta

| where RiskLevelDuringSignIn in ("medium","high") or RiskLevelAggregated in ("medium","high") or RiskState in ("atRisk","confirmedCompromised")

| join kind=inner Visitors on AccountUpn
| where Timestamp between (VisitTime .. VisitTime + 7d)
| extend DelayHours = datetime_diff('hour', Timestamp, VisitTime)
| project SignInTime=Timestamp, VisitTime, DelayHours, AccountUpn, IPAddress, Country, City, RiskLevelDuringSignIn, RiskState, Application, VisitedHost, DeviceName

Phishing-link click correlated to endpoint execution Delivery High
User received an external email containing a URL, clicked it, and within 60 seconds the recipient's endpoint spawned a scripting interpreter or network downloader (PowerShell / cmd / mshta / curl / certutil / bitsadmin). This is the high-fidelity shape — a raw "user clicked an emailed URL" query is too noisy to alert on because every Microsoft 365 tenant generates thousands of legitimate clicks per day. The exec-correlation step suppresses the noise to roughly the rate at which a click actually drives onto-host execution, which is the actionable signal. Pair with UC_PHISH_LINK_BYPASS (Safe Links override) and UC_PHISH_LINK_NEWDOMAIN for orthogonal high-fidelity variants.
ATT&CKT1566.002 T1204.001 T1059.001
Data sourcesEmail.All_Email Web Endpoint.Processes EmailEvents EmailUrlInfo UrlClickEvents DeviceProcessEvents
// Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s.
// Far higher fidelity than "every clicked URL" — most legitimate clicks
// never spawn a non-browser child process, so the join eliminates the
// 99% of noise that makes a raw click query unactionable.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let SuspectClicks = UrlClickEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where AccountName !endswith "$"
    | where ActionType in ("ClickAllowed","ClickedThrough")
    | join kind=inner (
        EmailEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
        | where DeliveryAction == "Delivered"
        | where EmailDirection == "Inbound"
        | project NetworkMessageId, Subject, SenderFromAddress, SenderFromDomain,
                  RecipientEmailAddress, EmailTimestamp = Timestamp
      ) on NetworkMessageId
    | join kind=leftouter (
        EmailUrlInfo | project NetworkMessageId, Url, UrlDomain
      ) on NetworkMessageId, Url
    | project ClickTime = Timestamp, AccountUpn, IPAddress, Url, UrlDomain,
              Subject, SenderFromAddress, SenderFromDomain, RecipientEmailAddress,
              ActionType;
// Correlate to a non-browser child process spawned within 60 seconds on
// the recipient's device.
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                         "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
| where FileName in~ ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                        "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe",
                        "bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe","curl.exe","wget.exe")
| join kind=inner SuspectClicks on $left.AccountName == $right.AccountUpn
| where Timestamp between (ClickTime .. ClickTime + 60s)
| project ClickTime, ProcessTime = Timestamp,
          DelaySec = datetime_diff('second', Timestamp, ClickTime),
          DeviceName, AccountName, RecipientEmailAddress, SenderFromAddress,
          Subject, Url, UrlDomain, ActionType,
          FileName, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFileName
| order by ClickTime desc
// UrlClickEvents has no clean Sentinel-native equivalent. The detection
// pivots to: Office Send→Receive proximity to SecurityEvent 4688 of a
// non-browser child process. Lower fidelity than the Defender version.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let SuspectMailUsers = OfficeActivity
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where OfficeWorkload == "Exchange"
    | where Operation =~ "Receive"
    | summarize Subject = any(Subject), Sender = any(Sender)
                by MailboxOwnerUPN, MessageId, EmailTime = bin(TimeGenerated, 1m);
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
| where EventID == 4688
| where ParentProcessName has_any ("\chrome.exe","\msedge.exe",
                                     "\firefox.exe","\outlook.exe","\brave.exe")
| where NewProcessName has_any ("\powershell.exe","\pwsh.exe","\cmd.exe",
                                  "\mshta.exe","\rundll32.exe","\regsvr32.exe",
                                  "\wscript.exe","\cscript.exe","\bitsadmin.exe",
                                  "\certutil.exe","\curl.exe","\wget.exe")
| join kind=inner SuspectMailUsers on $left.Account == $right.MailboxOwnerUPN
| where TimeGenerated between (EmailTime .. EmailTime + 60s)
| project TimeGenerated, EmailTime, Computer, Account, ParentProcessName,
          NewProcessName, CommandLine, Sender, Subject
| order by TimeGenerated desc
WEB

| tstats `summariesonly` earliest(_time) AS click_time
    from datamodel=Web
    where Web.action="allowed"
    by Web.src, Web.user, Web.dest, Web.url
| `drop_dm_object_name(Web)`
| rename user AS recipient, dest AS clicked_domain, url AS clicked_url
| join type=inner recipient
    [| tstats `summariesonly` count
         from datamodel=Email.All_Email
         where All_Email.action="delivered" AND All_Email.url!="-"
         by All_Email.recipient, All_Email.src_user, All_Email.url, All_Email.subject
     | `drop_dm_object_name(All_Email)`
     | rex field=url "https?://(?<email_domain>[^/]+)"
     | rename recipient AS recipient]
| join type=inner src
    [| tstats `summariesonly` earliest(_time) AS exec_time
         values(Processes.process) AS exec_cmd, values(Processes.process_name) AS exec_proc
         from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
         where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                                   "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
           AND Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                                            "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe",
                                            "cscript.exe","bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe",
                                            "curl.exe","wget.exe")
         by Processes.dest, Processes.user

     | rename dest AS src]

| table click_time, exec_time, delta_sec, recipient, src, src_user, subject,

Email attachment opened from external sender Delivery High
Attachment delivery + execution by recipient — most common malware initial access.
ATT&CKT1566.001 T1204.002
Data sourcesEmail.All_Email Endpoint.Processes EmailAttachmentInfo DeviceProcessEvents
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let MalAttachments = EmailAttachmentInfo
    | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where AccountName !endswith "$"
    | project NetworkMessageId, RecipientEmailAddress,
              AttachmentFileName = FileName, AttachmentSHA256 = SHA256;
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("OUTLOOK.EXE","winword.exe","excel.exe","powerpnt.exe")
| where FileName in~ ("cmd.exe","powershell.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe",
                      "mshta.exe","rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe")
| join kind=inner MalAttachments on $left.AccountUpn == $right.RecipientEmailAddress
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, FileName, ProcessCommandLine,
          InitiatingProcessFileName, AttachmentFileName, AttachmentSHA256
// Sentinel doesn't have an attachment-hash table. Best approximation:
// OfficeActivity Send/Receive activity + correlate to host process spawn.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let MailWithAttach = OfficeActivity
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where OfficeWorkload == "Exchange"
    | where Operation in~ ("Send","Receive")
    | where isnotempty(MessageId)
    | project EmailTime = TimeGenerated, MailboxOwnerUPN, Sender,
              Recipients, Subject, MessageId;
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
| where EventID == 4688
| where ParentProcessName endswith "OUTLOOK.EXE"
| where NewProcessName endswith "\cmd.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\powershell.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\wscript.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\cscript.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\mshta.exe"
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, Account, NewProcessName, CommandLine,
          ParentProcessName
| order by TimeGenerated desc

File hash IOCs — endpoint file/process match Installation High
Match SHA256/SHA1/MD5 named in the article against EDR file/process telemetry.
ATT&CKT1027
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem Endpoint.Processes DeviceFileEvents DeviceProcessEvents
// Pre-filter each table BEFORE the union — the engine cannot push
// predicates across `union`, and DeviceFileEvents lacks ProcessCommandLine
// (Initiating only) so column-projection has to differ per side.
union
    ( DeviceFileEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(7d)
        | where InitiatingProcessAccountName !endswith "$"
        | where SHA256 in~ ("3b8bb7631b39f455d31544b55ba97b49ab1888c1", "84ecdca915f1af822ccc8a04479f5179104f353c", "9bd164dd3f50d196c7dff4f6c1b0f1345ac96d9a") or SHA1 in~ ("3b8bb7631b39f455d31544b55ba97b49ab1888c1", "84ecdca915f1af822ccc8a04479f5179104f353c", "9bd164dd3f50d196c7dff4f6c1b0f1345ac96d9a") or MD5 in~ ("3b8bb7631b39f455d31544b55ba97b49ab1888c1", "84ecdca915f1af822ccc8a04479f5179104f353c", "9bd164dd3f50d196c7dff4f6c1b0f1345ac96d9a")
        | project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, FileName, FolderPath, SHA256,
                  Cmd = InitiatingProcessCommandLine, Source = "DeviceFileEvents" ),
    ( DeviceProcessEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(7d)
        | where AccountName !endswith "$"
        | where SHA256 in~ ("3b8bb7631b39f455d31544b55ba97b49ab1888c1", "84ecdca915f1af822ccc8a04479f5179104f353c", "9bd164dd3f50d196c7dff4f6c1b0f1345ac96d9a") or SHA1 in~ ("3b8bb7631b39f455d31544b55ba97b49ab1888c1", "84ecdca915f1af822ccc8a04479f5179104f353c", "9bd164dd3f50d196c7dff4f6c1b0f1345ac96d9a") or MD5 in~ ("3b8bb7631b39f455d31544b55ba97b49ab1888c1", "84ecdca915f1af822ccc8a04479f5179104f353c", "9bd164dd3f50d196c7dff4f6c1b0f1345ac96d9a")
        | project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, FileName, FolderPath, SHA256,
                  Cmd = ProcessCommandLine, Source = "DeviceProcessEvents" )
| order by Timestamp desc

// Pre-filter both ASIM tables before the union — same pattern as the
// Defender version so the engine can push hash predicates per-side.
let BadHashes = dynamic(["3b8bb7631b39f455d31544b55ba97b49ab1888c1", "84ecdca915f1af822ccc8a04479f5179104f353c", "9bd164dd3f50d196c7dff4f6c1b0f1345ac96d9a"]);
union
    ( ImFileEvent
        | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
        | where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
        | where TargetFileSHA256 in~ (BadHashes)
           or TargetFileSHA1 in~ (BadHashes)
           or TargetFileMD5 in~ (BadHashes)
        | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, EventType,
                  TargetFileName, TargetFilePath, TargetFileSHA256,
                  Cmd = ActingProcessName, Source = "ImFileEvent" ),
    ( ImProcessCreate
        | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
        | where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
        | where SHA256 in~ (BadHashes) or SHA1 in~ (BadHashes) or MD5 in~ (BadHashes)
        | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, EventType = TargetProcessName,
                  TargetFileName = TargetProcessName, TargetFilePath = TargetProcessName,
                  TargetFileSHA256 = SHA256,
                  Cmd = TargetProcessCommandLine, Source = "ImProcessCreate" )
| order by TimeGenerated desc

Cyber Security News
2026-05-28 11 use cases 4 techniques 5 kill-chain phases detected

A new kind of cyberattack is changing how defenders must think about intrusion detection. Reconnaissance. Attacker researches the target — OSINT, scanning, enumeration. → Asset exposure — vulnerability matches article CVE(s)
Weaponization. Coupling exploit code with deliverable payload (e.g. weaponized PDF/Office doc, trojanized installer).
Delivery. Transmitting the weapon (phishing email, USB, watering hole, drive-by, malicious ad). → Phishing-link click correlated to endpoint execution · Email attachment opened from external sender
Exploitation. Triggering the exploit — vulnerability/macro/trust abuse to execute code. → [LLM] marimo notebook Python process spawning interactive shell (CVE-2026-39987 post-exploit) · Office app spawning script/LOLBin child process · Fake CAPTCHA / clipboard-injected PowerShell (ClickFix / FakeCaptcha)
Installation. Establishing persistence on the host — backdoor, service, scheduled task, registry key.
Command & Control. Beacon to attacker infrastructure for control and tasking. → [LLM] Burst AWS API calls fanned across Cloudflare Workers egress (104.28.0.0/16) for one principal · Network connections to article IPs / domains

Lateral movement, credential dumping, data theft, ransomware, sabotage. → [LLM] AWS Secrets Manager retrieval from Cloudflare Workers egress pool · [LLM] SSH authentication to bastion from Cloudflare Workers CIDR (104.28.0.0/16) · [LLM] PostgreSQL HEREDOC credential-table dump invoked from compromised host
[LLM] marimo notebook Python process spawning interactive shell (CVE-2026-39987 post-exploit) Exploitation High
Detects post-exploitation of CVE-2026-39987 where the marimo notebook server's Python process spawns an interactive shell via the abused /terminal/ws WebSocket endpoint. The shell child of a marimo-bearing Python parent is the on-host fingerprint of the one-WebSocket-request RCE Sysdig documented. Rationale: Article names marimo + CVE-2026-39987 + /terminal/ws as the entry. On-host the abused terminal feature surfaces as a Python(marimo) → bash child; pairing that parent with the credential-file enumeration strings (.aws/credentials, .pgpass) the article calls out makes this fire on the actual intrusion shape, not generic Python-spawns-shell noise.
ATT&CKT1190 T1059.004
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("python","python3","uvicorn") or InitiatingProcessCommandLine has "marimo"
| where FileName in~ ("bash","sh","dash","zsh","ksh")
| where InitiatingProcessCommandLine has "marimo" or ProcessCommandLine has_any ("id","whoami","/.aws/credentials","/.pgpass","env","find /","ls /")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, FileName, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessParentFileName
| order by Timestamp desc
ImProcessCreate
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where ParentProcessName in~ ("python","python3","uvicorn") or ParentProcessCommandLine has "marimo"
| where ActingProcessName in~ ("bash","sh","dash","zsh")
| where ParentProcessCommandLine has "marimo" or ActingProcessCommandLine has_any ("id","whoami","/.aws/credentials","/.pgpass","env","find /")
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, ParentProcessCommandLine, ActingProcessName, ActingProcessCommandLine
title: marimo Notebook Python Process Spawning Interactive Shell (CVE-2026-39987)
id: a1b2c3d4-e5f6-4789-abcd-ef1234567890

| ImageFileName=/\/(bash|sh|dash|zsh)$/i
| CommandLine=/(marimo|\.aws\/credentials|\.pgpass|whoami|find\s+\/)/i
| groupBy([aid, ComputerName, UserName, ParentImageFileName, ImageFileName, CommandLine], function=count())
