Phishing-link click correlated to endpoint execution Delivery High
User received an external email containing a URL, clicked it, and within 60 seconds the recipient's endpoint spawned a scripting interpreter or network downloader (PowerShell / cmd / mshta / curl / certutil / bitsadmin). This is the high-fidelity shape — a raw "user clicked an emailed URL" query is too noisy to alert on because every Microsoft 365 tenant generates thousands of legitimate clicks per day. The exec-correlation step suppresses the noise to roughly the rate at which a click actually drives onto-host execution, which is the actionable signal. Pair with UC_PHISH_LINK_BYPASS (Safe Links override) and UC_PHISH_LINK_NEWDOMAIN for orthogonal high-fidelity variants.
ATT&CKT1566.002 T1204.001 T1059.001
Data sourcesEmail.All_Email Web Endpoint.Processes EmailEvents EmailUrlInfo UrlClickEvents DeviceProcessEvents
// Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s.
// Far higher fidelity than "every clicked URL" — most legitimate clicks
// never spawn a non-browser child process, so the join eliminates the
// 99% of noise that makes a raw click query unactionable.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let SuspectClicks = UrlClickEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where AccountName !endswith "$"
    | where ActionType in ("ClickAllowed","ClickedThrough")
    | join kind=inner (
        EmailEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
        | where DeliveryAction == "Delivered"
        | where EmailDirection == "Inbound"
        | project NetworkMessageId, Subject, SenderFromAddress, SenderFromDomain,
                  RecipientEmailAddress, EmailTimestamp = Timestamp
      ) on NetworkMessageId
    | join kind=leftouter (
        EmailUrlInfo | project NetworkMessageId, Url, UrlDomain
      ) on NetworkMessageId, Url
    | project ClickTime = Timestamp, AccountUpn, IPAddress, Url, UrlDomain,
              Subject, SenderFromAddress, SenderFromDomain, RecipientEmailAddress,
              ActionType;
// Correlate to a non-browser child process spawned within 60 seconds on
// the recipient's device.
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                         "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
| where FileName in~ ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                        "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe",
                        "bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe","curl.exe","wget.exe")
| join kind=inner SuspectClicks on $left.AccountName == $right.AccountUpn
| where Timestamp between (ClickTime .. ClickTime + 60s)
| project ClickTime, ProcessTime = Timestamp,
          DelaySec = datetime_diff('second', Timestamp, ClickTime),
          DeviceName, AccountName, RecipientEmailAddress, SenderFromAddress,
          Subject, Url, UrlDomain, ActionType,
          FileName, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFileName
| order by ClickTime desc
// UrlClickEvents has no clean Sentinel-native equivalent. The detection
// pivots to: Office Send→Receive proximity to SecurityEvent 4688 of a
// non-browser child process. Lower fidelity than the Defender version.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let SuspectMailUsers = OfficeActivity
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where OfficeWorkload == "Exchange"
    | where Operation =~ "Receive"
    | summarize Subject = any(Subject), Sender = any(Sender)
                by MailboxOwnerUPN, MessageId, EmailTime = bin(TimeGenerated, 1m);
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
| where EventID == 4688
| where ParentProcessName has_any ("\chrome.exe","\msedge.exe",
                                     "\firefox.exe","\outlook.exe","\brave.exe")
| where NewProcessName has_any ("\powershell.exe","\pwsh.exe","\cmd.exe",
                                  "\mshta.exe","\rundll32.exe","\regsvr32.exe",
                                  "\wscript.exe","\cscript.exe","\bitsadmin.exe",
                                  "\certutil.exe","\curl.exe","\wget.exe")
| join kind=inner SuspectMailUsers on $left.Account == $right.MailboxOwnerUPN
| where TimeGenerated between (EmailTime .. EmailTime + 60s)
| project TimeGenerated, EmailTime, Computer, Account, ParentProcessName,
          NewProcessName, CommandLine, Sender, Subject
| order by TimeGenerated desc
WEB
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
``` Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s ```
| tstats `summariesonly` earliest(_time) AS click_time
    from datamodel=Web
    where Web.action="allowed"
    by Web.src, Web.user, Web.dest, Web.url
| `drop_dm_object_name(Web)`
| rename user AS recipient, dest AS clicked_domain, url AS clicked_url
| join type=inner recipient
    [| tstats `summariesonly` count
         from datamodel=Email.All_Email
         where All_Email.action="delivered" AND All_Email.url!="-"
         by All_Email.recipient, All_Email.src_user, All_Email.url, All_Email.subject
     | `drop_dm_object_name(All_Email)`
     | rex field=url "https?://(?<email_domain>[^/]+)"
     | rename recipient AS recipient]
| join type=inner src
    [| tstats `summariesonly` earliest(_time) AS exec_time
         values(Processes.process) AS exec_cmd, values(Processes.process_name) AS exec_proc
         from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
         where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                                   "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
           AND Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                                            "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe",
                                            "cscript.exe","bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe",
                                            "curl.exe","wget.exe")
         by Processes.dest, Processes.user
     | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
     | rename dest AS src]
| eval delta_sec = exec_time - click_time
| where delta_sec >= 0 AND delta_sec <= 60
| table click_time, exec_time, delta_sec, recipient, src, src_user, subject,
        clicked_domain, clicked_url, exec_proc, exec_cmd
| sort - click_time
``` Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s ```
| tstats summariesonly=false earliest(_time) AS click_time
    from datamodel=Web
    where Web.action="allowed"
    by Web.src, Web.user, Web.dest, Web.url
| `drop_dm_object_name(Web)`
| rename user AS recipient, dest AS clicked_domain, url AS clicked_url
| join type=inner recipient
    [| tstats summariesonly=false count
         from datamodel=Email.All_Email
         where All_Email.action="delivered" AND All_Email.url!="-"
         by All_Email.recipient, All_Email.src_user, All_Email.url, All_Email.subject
     | `drop_dm_object_name(All_Email)`
     | rex field=url "https?://(?<email_domain>[^/]+)"
     | rename recipient AS recipient]
| join type=inner src
    [| tstats summariesonly=false earliest(_time) AS exec_time
         values(Processes.process) AS exec_cmd, values(Processes.process_name) AS exec_proc
         from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
         where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                                   "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
           AND Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                                            "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe",
                                            "cscript.exe","bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe",
                                            "curl.exe","wget.exe")
         by Processes.dest, Processes.user
     | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
     | rename dest AS src]
| eval delta_sec = exec_time - click_time
| where delta_sec >= 0 AND delta_sec <= 60
| table click_time, exec_time, delta_sec, recipient, src, src_user, subject,
        clicked_domain, clicked_url, exec_proc, exec_cmd
| sort - click_time
Email attachment opened from external sender Delivery High
Attachment delivery + execution by recipient — most common malware initial access.
ATT&CKT1566.001 T1204.002
Data sourcesEmail.All_Email Endpoint.Processes EmailAttachmentInfo DeviceProcessEvents
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let MalAttachments = EmailAttachmentInfo
    | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where AccountName !endswith "$"
    | project NetworkMessageId, RecipientEmailAddress,
              AttachmentFileName = FileName, AttachmentSHA256 = SHA256;
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("OUTLOOK.EXE","winword.exe","excel.exe","powerpnt.exe")
| where FileName in~ ("cmd.exe","powershell.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe",
                      "mshta.exe","rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe")
| join kind=inner MalAttachments on $left.AccountUpn == $right.RecipientEmailAddress
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, FileName, ProcessCommandLine,
          InitiatingProcessFileName, AttachmentFileName, AttachmentSHA256
// Sentinel doesn't have an attachment-hash table. Best approximation:
// OfficeActivity Send/Receive activity + correlate to host process spawn.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let MailWithAttach = OfficeActivity
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where OfficeWorkload == "Exchange"
    | where Operation in~ ("Send","Receive")
    | where isnotempty(MessageId)
    | project EmailTime = TimeGenerated, MailboxOwnerUPN, Sender,
              Recipients, Subject, MessageId;
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
| where EventID == 4688
| where ParentProcessName endswith "OUTLOOK.EXE"
| where NewProcessName endswith "\cmd.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\powershell.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\wscript.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\cscript.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\mshta.exe"
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, Account, NewProcessName, CommandLine,
          ParentProcessName
| order by TimeGenerated desc
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count
    from datamodel=Email.All_Email

status: experimental
description: |
    PowerShell launched with -EncodedCommand, base64 strings, hidden
    window, no-profile, bypass policy, IEX / Invoke-Expression / Net
    .WebClient.DownloadString — combinations indicating evasion.
references:
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1059/001/
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1027/
author: Clankerusecase
date: 2026/05/02
tags:
    - attack.t1059.001
    - attack.t1027
    - attack.execution
    - attack.defense-evasion
logsource:
    category: process_creation
    product: windows
detection:
    selection_image:
        Image|endswith:
            - '\powershell.exe'
            - '\pwsh.exe'
    selection_args:
        CommandLine|contains:
            - '-enc '
            - 'EncodedCommand'
            - 'FromBase64String'
            - 'Invoke-Expression'
            - 'IEX('
            - 'DownloadString'
            - 'Net.WebClient'
            - '-w hidden'
            - '-WindowStyle Hidden'
            - '-nop'
            - '-NoProfile'
            - '-ep bypass'
            - '-ExecutionPolicy Bypass'
    condition: selection_image and selection_args
falsepositives:
    - DevOps tooling that legitimately uses encoded command for
      cross-shell escaping
level: high
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
    where Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe")
      AND (Processes.process="*-enc *" OR Processes.process="*EncodedCommand*"
        OR Processes.process="*FromBase64String*" OR Processes.process="*-nop*"
        OR Processes.process="*-w hidden*" OR Processes.process="*Invoke-Expression*"
        OR Processes.process="*IEX(*" OR Processes.process="*DownloadString*"
        OR Processes.process="*Net.WebClient*")
    by Processes.dest, Processes.user, Processes.process_name, Processes.process, Processes.parent_process_name
| `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
    where Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe")
      AND (Processes.process="*-enc *" OR Processes.process="*EncodedCommand*"
        OR Processes.process="*FromBase64String*" OR Processes.process="*-nop*"
        OR Processes.process="*-w hidden*" OR Processes.process="*Invoke-Expression*"
        OR Processes.process="*IEX(*" OR Processes.process="*DownloadString*"
        OR Processes.process="*Net.WebClient*")
    by Processes.dest, Processes.user, Processes.process_name, Processes.process, Processes.parent_process_name
| `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
Trusted vendor binary / installer launching unusual children Exploitation Medium
Supply-chain trojan signal: legitimate signed binary spawning script interpreters or exotic LOLBins.
ATT&CKT1195.002
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes DeviceProcessEvents
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where AccountName !endswith "$"
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("setup.exe","installer.exe","update.exe")
| where FileName in~ ("powershell.exe","cmd.exe","rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","mshta.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe","wmic.exe","bitsadmin.exe")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, InitiatingProcessFileName, FileName, ProcessCommandLine
// Replace `"setup.exe","installer.exe","update.exe"` with the vendor binaries observed in the
// article (matching shape with the Defender query).
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where EventID == 4688
| where Account !endswith "$"
| where ParentProcessName has_any ("setup.exe","installer.exe","update.exe")
| where NewProcessName endswith "\powershell.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\cmd.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\rundll32.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\regsvr32.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\mshta.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\wscript.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\cscript.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\wmic.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\bitsadmin.exe"
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, Account, ParentProcessName,
          NewProcessName, CommandLine
| order by TimeGenerated desc

title: Trusted Vendor Binary Launching Unusual Children
id: 7c8b2e10-4d4f-4a8c-9c1f-bf6e2c4a8d09
status: experimental
description: |
    A signed vendor binary (in the article's named-vendors list)
    spawning script-host or LOLBin children. Strongest signal when
    paired with a recent CVE / supply-chain advisory naming the same
    vendor.
references:
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1195/
author: Clankerusecase
date: 2026/05/02
tags:
    - attack.t1195
    - attack.initial-access
logsource:
    category: process_creation
    product: windows
detection:
    selection_child:
        Image|endswith:
            - '\powershell.exe'
            - '\pwsh.exe'
            - '\cmd.exe'
            - '\rundll32.exe'
            - '\regsvr32.exe'
            - '\mshta.exe'
            - '\wscript.exe'
            - '\cscript.exe'
            - '\wmic.exe'
            - '\bitsadmin.exe'
    selection_parent_vendor:
        ParentImage|contains:
            - '\Program Files\'
            - '\Program Files (x86)\'
    condition: selection_child and selection_parent_vendor
falsepositives:
    - Many — installers and updaters legitimately spawn children. Pin
      the parent path to specific vendor binaries observed in the
      article before alerting.
level: medium
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
    where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("setup.exe","installer.exe","update.exe")
      AND Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","cmd.exe","rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","mshta.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe","wmic.exe","bitsadmin.exe")
    by Processes.dest, Processes.user, Processes.parent_process_name, Processes.process_name, Processes.process
| `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
    where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("setup.exe","installer.exe","update.exe")
      AND Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","cmd.exe","rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","mshta.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe","wmic.exe","bitsadmin.exe")
    by Processes.dest, Processes.user, Processes.parent_process_name, Processes.process_name, Processes.process
| `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`

File hash IOCs — endpoint file/process match Installation High
Match SHA256/SHA1/MD5 named in the article against EDR file/process telemetry.
ATT&CKT1027
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem Endpoint.Processes DeviceFileEvents DeviceProcessEvents
// Pre-filter each table BEFORE the union — the engine cannot push
// predicates across `union`, and DeviceFileEvents lacks ProcessCommandLine
// (Initiating only) so column-projection has to differ per side.
union
    ( DeviceFileEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(7d)
        | where InitiatingProcessAccountName !endswith "$"
        | where SHA256 in~ ("0da123adf9251957a4b850a3f6bd6a753dd4892be176a84a18450e899534cc5e", "d91c00fad521e76efa89715cca89db487d5676f2c767c883482f9c8f82bd383a", "fd65051c61a904a304919c04a8c8633c001183ac73ac461cd4d9057946f02bf5", "2927bc31b4f8254c6b332fc03110a6373cad00ffa2ff9de427c26bb222017bb2", "2f25ea1b622abf3212141af932c2ec4cbd6b2b5903c2a531121f691227d98cff", "17e771c78430cc67e71d4547f8996a1a488e9d3f", "338662fd0c4d750a0ba203a32b59f081") or SHA1 in~ ("0da123adf9251957a4b850a3f6bd6a753dd4892be176a84a18450e899534cc5e", "d91c00fad521e76efa89715cca89db487d5676f2c767c883482f9c8f82bd383a", "fd65051c61a904a304919c04a8c8633c001183ac73ac461cd4d9057946f02bf5", "2927bc31b4f8254c6b332fc03110a6373cad00ffa2ff9de427c26bb222017bb2", "2f25ea1b622abf3212141af932c2ec4cbd6b2b5903c2a531121f691227d98cff", "17e771c78430cc67e71d4547f8996a1a488e9d3f", "338662fd0c4d750a0ba203a32b59f081") or MD5 in~ ("0da123adf9251957a4b850a3f6bd6a753dd4892be176a84a18450e899534cc5e", "d91c00fad521e76efa89715cca89db487d5676f2c767c883482f9c8f82bd383a", "fd65051c61a904a304919c04a8c8633c001183ac73ac461cd4d9057946f02bf5", "2927bc31b4f8254c6b332fc03110a6373cad00ffa2ff9de427c26bb222017bb2", "2f25ea1b622abf3212141af932c2ec4cbd6b2b5903c2a531121f691227d98cff", "17e771c78430cc67e71d4547f8996a1a488e9d3f", "338662fd0c4d750a0ba203a32b59f081")
        | project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, FileName, FolderPath, SHA256,
                  Cmd = InitiatingProcessCommandLine, Source = "DeviceFileEvents" ),
    ( DeviceProcessEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(7d)
        | where AccountName !endswith "$"
        | where SHA256 in~ ("0da123adf9251957a4b850a3f6bd6a753dd4892be176a84a18450e899534cc5e", "d91c00fad521e76efa89715cca89db487d5676f2c767c883482f9c8f82bd383a", "fd65051c61a904a304919c04a8c8633c001183ac73ac461cd4d9057946f02bf5", "2927bc31b4f8254c6b332fc03110a6373cad00ffa2ff9de427c26bb222017bb2", "2f25ea1b622abf3212141af932c2ec4cbd6b2b5903c2a531121f691227d98cff", "17e771c78430cc67e71d4547f8996a1a488e9d3f", "338662fd0c4d750a0ba203a32b59f081") or SHA1 in~ ("0da123adf9251957a4b850a3f6bd6a753dd4892be176a84a18450e899534cc5e", "d91c00fad521e76efa89715cca89db487d5676f2c767c883482f9c8f82bd383a", "fd65051c61a904a304919c04a8c8633c001183ac73ac461cd4d9057946f02bf5", "2927bc31b4f8254c6b332fc03110a6373cad00ffa2ff9de427c26bb222017bb2", "2f25ea1b622abf3212141af932c2ec4cbd6b2b5903c2a531121f691227d98cff", "17e771c78430cc67e71d4547f8996a1a488e9d3f", "338662fd0c4d750a0ba203a32b59f081") or MD5 in~ ("0da123adf9251957a4b850a3f6bd6a753dd4892be176a84a18450e899534cc5e", "d91c00fad521e76efa89715cca89db487d5676f2c767c883482f9c8f82bd383a", "fd65051c61a904a304919c04a8c8633c001183ac73ac461cd4d9057946f02bf5", "2927bc31b4f8254c6b332fc03110a6373cad00ffa2ff9de427c26bb222017bb2", "2f25ea1b622abf3212141af932c2ec4cbd6b2b5903c2a531121f691227d98cff", "17e771c78430cc67e71d4547f8996a1a488e9d3f", "338662fd0c4d750a0ba203a32b59f081")
        | project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, FileName, FolderPath, SHA256,
                  Cmd = ProcessCommandLine, Source = "DeviceProcessEvents" )
| order by Timestamp desc

// Pre-filter both ASIM tables before the union — same pattern as the
// Defender version so the engine can push hash predicates per-side.
let BadHashes = dynamic(["0da123adf9251957a4b850a3f6bd6a753dd4892be176a84a18450e899534cc5e", "d91c00fad521e76efa89715cca89db487d5676f2c767c883482f9c8f82bd383a", "fd65051c61a904a304919c04a8c8633c001183ac73ac461cd4d9057946f02bf5", "2927bc31b4f8254c6b332fc03110a6373cad00ffa2ff9de427c26bb222017bb2", "2f25ea1b622abf3212141af932c2ec4cbd6b2b5903c2a531121f691227d98cff", "17e771c78430cc67e71d4547f8996a1a488e9d3f", "338662fd0c4d750a0ba203a32b59f081"]);
union
    ( ImFileEvent
        | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
        | where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
        | where TargetFileSHA256 in~ (BadHashes)
           or TargetFileSHA1 in~ (BadHashes)
           or TargetFileMD5 in~ (BadHashes)
        | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, EventType,
                  TargetFileName, TargetFilePath, TargetFileSHA256,
                  Cmd = ActingProcessName, Source = "ImFileEvent" ),
    ( ImProcessCreate
        | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
        | where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
        | where SHA256 in~ (BadHashes) or SHA1 in~ (BadHashes) or MD5 in~ (BadHashes)
        | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, EventType = TargetProcessName,
                  TargetFileName = TargetProcessName, TargetFilePath = TargetProcessName,
                  TargetFileSHA256 = SHA256,
                  Cmd = TargetProcessCommandLine, Source = "ImProcessCreate" )
| order by TimeGenerated desc

Article-specific behavioural hunt — Threat Actors Exploit Critical FortiClient EMS Flaw to Deploy Credential Stealer Exploitation High
Auto-generated hunt targeting the specific binaries, paths, registry locations and command-line fragments named in this article. Hunting tier — needs analyst review and environment tuning before promotion to alerting.
ATT&CKT1204.002
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes Endpoint.Filesystem Endpoint.Registry
// Article-specific bespoke detection — Threat Actors Exploit Critical FortiClient EMS Flaw to Deploy Credential Stealer
// Hunts the actual binaries / paths / commandline fragments named
// in the article instead of a generic technique-class template.
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(30d)
| where (FileName in~ ("fortitray.exe", "fortiendpoint_patch.exe"))
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, FileName,
          FolderPath, ProcessCommandLine,
          InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine
| order by Timestamp desc

// File-creation events for the named binaries / paths
DeviceFileEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(30d)
| where ActionType in ("FileCreated","FileModified")
| where (FileName in~ ("fortitray.exe", "fortiendpoint_patch.exe"))
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, FolderPath,
          FileName, ActionType, InitiatingProcessFileName,
          InitiatingProcessCommandLine
| order by Timestamp desc

Reconnaissance. Attacker researches the target — OSINT, scanning, enumeration.

Delivery. Transmitting the weapon (phishing email, USB, watering hole, drive-by, malicious ad). → [LLM] --exec token in Gogs application or proxy logs (branch-name injection) · Phishing-link click correlated to endpoint execution · Email attachment opened from external sender
Exploitation. Triggering the exploit — vulnerability/macro/trust abuse to execute code. → [LLM] Gogs RCE — git rebase --exec injection from gogs process · Office app spawning script/LOLBin child process · Trusted vendor binary / installer launching unusual children
Installation. Establishing persistence on the host — backdoor, service, scheduled task, registry key. → File hash IOCs — endpoint file/process match
Command & Control. Beacon to attacker infrastructure for control and tasking.

[LLM] Gogs RCE — git rebase --exec injection from gogs process Exploitation High
Detects the unpatched Gogs vulnerability (Rapid7, May 2026, CVSS 9.4) where an authenticated user creates a PR with a malicious branch name that injects --exec into 'git rebase' during 'Rebase before merging'. Pivots on the git binary being launched by gogs with both 'rebase' and '--exec' in its command line — a combination that should never occur in normal Gogs operation. Rationale: Article and Rapid7 advisory state the exploit primitive is injection of '--exec' into 'git rebase' via a malicious branch name during the 'Rebase before merging' merge operation. The pairing of gogs as parent + git as child + both 'rebase' and '--exec' tokens in the command line is highly article-specific and has no benign equivalent in a Gogs server's normal process tree.
ATT&CKT1190 T1059.004 T1059.003

| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, FileName, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessParentFileName, SHA256
| order by Timestamp desc

[LLM] Shell or interpreter spawned by gogs or git on Gogs server Actions on Objectives Medium
Hunts for the post-injection shell descendant of the Gogs RCE chain. On a healthy Gogs install, the gogs binary forks git for repo operations but neither gogs nor git should spawn /bin/sh, bash, cmd.exe, or PowerShell as a child. Catches variants where the attacker's --exec payload does not contain literal 'rebase' / '--exec' tokens in the git invocation (e.g. when only the resulting shell is visible to EDR). Rationale: Article states post-exploit the attacker can 'breach the server, access every repository, dump credentials, move to other network-accessible systems.' All of those require a shell. Catching the shell child of gogs/git is the back-stop when the initial git invocation is obscured (e.g. attacker uses a longer git argument list or the rebase command line is truncated in logging). The hooks/ filter excludes legitimate server-side Git hooks which are the most common benign cause of git→shell.

[LLM] --exec token in Gogs application or proxy logs (branch-name injection) Delivery High
Detects the on-the-wire artifact of the Gogs --exec exploit: the literal string '--exec' appearing in a Gogs application log line, syslog entry attributed to the gogs process, or in the URL/body of an HTTP request to a Gogs pulls/merge endpoint. Catches the attempt even when EDR is missing or when the resulting git invocation is suppressed. Rationale: Article states the malicious payload is delivered as a branch name containing '--exec' submitted through Gogs' web UI / API during PR creation or the 'Rebase before merging' merge action. That string is preserved in Gogs' own log lines (the maintainer logs the git command being run) and in any reverse-proxy access log that captures URL/POST data. Article also notes 'when the attacker creates and deletes their own repository, the only trace is an HTTP 500 in the server logs' — so a literal-string sweep across syslog/web logs catches the variant where EDR is blind or absent. Default Gogs port 3000 is referenced from Gogs documentation.

Phishing-link click correlated to endpoint execution Delivery High
User received an external email containing a URL, clicked it, and within 60 seconds the recipient's endpoint spawned a scripting interpreter or network downloader (PowerShell / cmd / mshta / curl / certutil / bitsadmin). This is the high-fidelity shape — a raw "user clicked an emailed URL" query is too noisy to alert on because every Microsoft 365 tenant generates thousands of legitimate clicks per day. The exec-correlation step suppresses the noise to roughly the rate at which a click actually drives onto-host execution, which is the actionable signal. Pair with UC_PHISH_LINK_BYPASS (Safe Links override) and UC_PHISH_LINK_NEWDOMAIN for orthogonal high-fidelity variants.
ATT&CKT1566.002 T1204.001 T1059.001
Data sourcesEmail.All_Email Web Endpoint.Processes EmailEvents EmailUrlInfo UrlClickEvents DeviceProcessEvents
// Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s.
// Far higher fidelity than "every clicked URL" — most legitimate clicks
// never spawn a non-browser child process, so the join eliminates the
// 99% of noise that makes a raw click query unactionable.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let SuspectClicks = UrlClickEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where AccountName !endswith "$"
    | where ActionType in ("ClickAllowed","ClickedThrough")
    | join kind=inner (
        EmailEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
        | where DeliveryAction == "Delivered"
        | where EmailDirection == "Inbound"
        | project NetworkMessageId, Subject, SenderFromAddress, SenderFromDomain,
                  RecipientEmailAddress, EmailTimestamp = Timestamp
      ) on NetworkMessageId
    | join kind=leftouter (
        EmailUrlInfo | project NetworkMessageId, Url, UrlDomain
      ) on NetworkMessageId, Url
    | project ClickTime = Timestamp, AccountUpn, IPAddress, Url, UrlDomain,
              Subject, SenderFromAddress, SenderFromDomain, RecipientEmailAddress,
              ActionType;
// Correlate to a non-browser child process spawned within 60 seconds on
// the recipient's device.
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                         "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
| where FileName in~ ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                        "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe",
                        "bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe","curl.exe","wget.exe")
| join kind=inner SuspectClicks on $left.AccountName == $right.AccountUpn
| where Timestamp between (ClickTime .. ClickTime + 60s)
| project ClickTime, ProcessTime = Timestamp,
          DelaySec = datetime_diff('second', Timestamp, ClickTime),
          DeviceName, AccountName, RecipientEmailAddress, SenderFromAddress,
          Subject, Url, UrlDomain, ActionType,
          FileName, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFileName
| order by ClickTime desc
// UrlClickEvents has no clean Sentinel-native equivalent. The detection
// pivots to: Office Send→Receive proximity to SecurityEvent 4688 of a
// non-browser child process. Lower fidelity than the Defender version.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let SuspectMailUsers = OfficeActivity
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where OfficeWorkload == "Exchange"
    | where Operation =~ "Receive"
    | summarize Subject = any(Subject), Sender = any(Sender)
                by MailboxOwnerUPN, MessageId, EmailTime = bin(TimeGenerated, 1m);
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
| where EventID == 4688
| where ParentProcessName has_any ("\chrome.exe","\msedge.exe",
                                     "\firefox.exe","\outlook.exe","\brave.exe")
| where NewProcessName has_any ("\powershell.exe","\pwsh.exe","\cmd.exe",
                                  "\mshta.exe","\rundll32.exe","\regsvr32.exe",
                                  "\wscript.exe","\cscript.exe","\bitsadmin.exe",
                                  "\certutil.exe","\curl.exe","\wget.exe")
| join kind=inner SuspectMailUsers on $left.Account == $right.MailboxOwnerUPN
| where TimeGenerated between (EmailTime .. EmailTime + 60s)
| project TimeGenerated, EmailTime, Computer, Account, ParentProcessName,
          NewProcessName, CommandLine, Sender, Subject
| order by TimeGenerated desc

File hash IOCs — endpoint file/process match Installation High
Match SHA256/SHA1/MD5 named in the article against EDR file/process telemetry.
ATT&CKT1027
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem Endpoint.Processes DeviceFileEvents DeviceProcessEvents
// Pre-filter each table BEFORE the union — the engine cannot push
// predicates across `union`, and DeviceFileEvents lacks ProcessCommandLine
// (Initiating only) so column-projection has to differ per side.
union
    ( DeviceFileEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(7d)
        | where InitiatingProcessAccountName !endswith "$"
        | where SHA256 in~ ("9cbd7add1930ec5389c922c1f6552add48ce04e") or SHA1 in~ ("9cbd7add1930ec5389c922c1f6552add48ce04e") or MD5 in~ ("9cbd7add1930ec5389c922c1f6552add48ce04e")
        | project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, FileName, FolderPath, SHA256,
                  Cmd = InitiatingProcessCommandLine, Source = "DeviceFileEvents" ),
    ( DeviceProcessEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(7d)
        | where AccountName !endswith "$"
        | where SHA256 in~ ("9cbd7add1930ec5389c922c1f6552add48ce04e") or SHA1 in~ ("9cbd7add1930ec5389c922c1f6552add48ce04e") or MD5 in~ ("9cbd7add1930ec5389c922c1f6552add48ce04e")
        | project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, FileName, FolderPath, SHA256,
                  Cmd = ProcessCommandLine, Source = "DeviceProcessEvents" )
| order by Timestamp desc

// Pre-filter both ASIM tables before the union — same pattern as the
// Defender version so the engine can push hash predicates per-side.
let BadHashes = dynamic(["9cbd7add1930ec5389c922c1f6552add48ce04e"]);
union
    ( ImFileEvent
        | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
        | where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
        | where TargetFileSHA256 in~ (BadHashes)
           or TargetFileSHA1 in~ (BadHashes)
           or TargetFileMD5 in~ (BadHashes)
        | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, EventType,
                  TargetFileName, TargetFilePath, TargetFileSHA256,
                  Cmd = ActingProcessName, Source = "ImFileEvent" ),
    ( ImProcessCreate
        | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
        | where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
        | where SHA256 in~ (BadHashes) or SHA1 in~ (BadHashes) or MD5 in~ (BadHashes)
        | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, EventType = TargetProcessName,
                  TargetFileName = TargetProcessName, TargetFilePath = TargetProcessName,
                  TargetFileSHA256 = SHA256,
                  Cmd = TargetProcessCommandLine, Source = "ImProcessCreate" )
| order by TimeGenerated desc

New Gogs 0-Day Vulnerability Lets Attackers Run Malicious Code on the Server Remotely

Cyber Security News
2026-05-28 13 use cases 4 techniques 6 kill-chain phases detected

A critical zero-day vulnerability has been discovered in Gogs, one of the most widely deployed self-hosted Git platforms in the world, allowing any authenticated user to execute arbitrary commands on the underlying server with no patch available at the time of publication. Rapid7 Labs researcher Jonah Burgess (CryptoCat) identified the flaw, tracked as a CWE-88 [&#8230;] The post New Gogs 0-Day Vulnerability Lets Attackers Run Malicious Code on the Server Remotely appeared first on Cyber Security News .

[LLM] Gogs server git process spawning shell — Rapid7 rebase Merge() RCE post-exploit Exploitation High
Detects the post-exploitation execution primitive of the Gogs Merge() argument-injection 0-day disclosed by Rapid7's Jonah Burgess: git on a Gogs server spawning sh/bash/dash under the git or gogs service account. Per the article, Git's argument parser interprets the attacker-crafted --exec= flag and runs the payload via `sh -c` after each replayed commit. Catches successful RCE regardless of payload content. Rationale: Anchored on the article's explicit description that Git executes the payload via `sh -c` after each replayed commit, under the Gogs server's typical 'git' user (article states: 'arbitrary command execution running as the Gogs server process user — typically git'). Cross-checked Bleeping Computer's coverage of the same Rapid7/Burgess advisory. Cross-checked against: • https://www.bleepingcomputer.com/news/security/new-gogs-zero-day-flaw-lets-hackers-get-remote-code-execution/ • https://www.runzero.com/blog/gogs/
ATT&CKT1190 T1059.004
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName =~ "git"
| where FileName in~ ("sh", "bash", "dash")
| where ProcessCommandLine has "-c"
| where InitiatingProcessAccountName in~ ("git", "gogs")
   or InitiatingProcessParentFileName in~ ("gogs", "gogs.bin")
| where AccountName !endswith "$"
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, InitiatingProcessAccountName, InitiatingProcessParentFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, FileName, ProcessCommandLine, SHA256
| order by Timestamp desc
ImProcessCreate
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where ActingProcessName endswith "/git" or ActingProcessName =~ "git"
| where TargetProcessName endswith "/sh" or TargetProcessName endswith "/bash" or TargetProcessName endswith "/dash"
| where TargetProcessCommandLine has "-c"
| where ActorUsername in~ ("git", "gogs")
   or ParentProcessName has_any ("gogs", "gogs.bin")
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, ParentProcessName, ParentProcessCommandLine, ActingProcessName, ActingProcessCommandLine, TargetProcessName, TargetProcessCommandLine
| order by TimeGenerated desc

[LLM] git rebase invoked with attacker-controlled --exec= argument (Gogs CVE payload) Exploitation High
Detects the literal exploit primitive of the Gogs Merge() 0-day: a `git rebase` process spawned with a `--exec=` argument. The vulnerable code in internal/database/pull.go passes the PR base-branch name straight into `git rebase` without a `--` separator, so any branch name starting with `--exec=` causes Git to treat it as a flag and execute the value. Rationale: Direct anchor on the article's PoC string `--exec=touch${IFS}/tmp/rce_proof` and its explicit description that the Merge() function passes branch names into `git rebase` without sanitization. The `--exec` flag is almost never used in server-side automated rebases — its presence under the Gogs service account is the exploit itself. Cross-checked against: • https://www.bleepingcomputer.com/news/security/new-gogs-zero-day-flaw-lets-hackers-get-remote-code-execution/ • https://www.runzero.com/blog/gogs/
ATT&CKT1190 T1059 T1068
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where (FileName =~ "git" or InitiatingProcessFileName =~ "git")
| where ProcessCommandLine has "rebase" and ProcessCommandLine has "--exec"
| where InitiatingProcessAccountName in~ ("git", "gogs")
   or InitiatingProcessFolderPath has_any ("/gogs", "/app/gogs", "/data/gogs")
   or ProcessCommandLine has_any ("${IFS}", "$IFS", "/tmp/", "/dev/tcp/", "base64", "curl ", "wget ")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, InitiatingProcessAccountName, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, FileName, ProcessCommandLine, SHA256
| order by Timestamp desc
ImProcessCreate
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where ActingProcessName endswith "/git" or ActingProcessName =~ "git"
| where ActingProcessCommandLine has "rebase" and ActingProcessCommandLine has "--exec"
| where ActorUsername in~ ("git", "gogs")
   or ParentProcessName has_any ("gogs", "gogs.bin")
   or ActingProcessCommandLine has_any ("${IFS}", "$IFS", "/tmp/", "/dev/tcp/", "base64 ", "curl ", "wget ")
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, ParentProcessName, ParentProcessCommandLine, ActingProcessName, ActingProcessCommandLine
| order by TimeGenerated desc

status: experimental
description: Detects `git rebase` invocations whose command line contains `--exec`, the literal exploit primitive of the Rapid7 Gogs Merge() argument-injection 0-day in internal/database/pull.go.
references:
  - https://cybersecuritynews.com/gogs-0-day-vulnerability/
  - https://www.bleepingcomputer.com/news/security/new-gogs-zero-day-flaw-lets-hackers-get-remote-code-execution/
author: Detection Engineering
date: 2026/05/28
tags:
  - attack.t1190
  - attack.t1059
  - attack.initial_access
logsource:
  category: process_creation
  product: linux
detection:
  selection:
    Image|endswith: '/git'
    CommandLine|contains|all:
      - 'rebase'
      - '--exec'
  condition: selection
falsepositives:
  - Developer-driven `git rebase --exec` use on shared CI runners (rare on a Gogs server account)
level: critical
source:linux.auditd @auditd.type:EXECVE @process.executable.path:*/git (@process.command_line:*rebase*--exec* OR @process.command_line:*--exec=*) @user.name:(git OR gogs)
#event_simpleName=ProcessRollup2 event_platform=Lin ImageFileName=/\/git$/i
| CommandLine=/rebase/
| CommandLine=/--exec/
| UserName=/^(git|gogs)$/i
| groupBy([aid, ComputerName, UserName, CommandLine, ParentBaseFileName], function=count())
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats summariesonly=t count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes where Processes.process_name=git AND Processes.process="*rebase*" AND Processes.process="*--exec*" by host Processes.user Processes.parent_process_name Processes.process_name Processes.process
| `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
| convert ctime(firstTime) ctime(lastTime)
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes where Processes.process_name=git AND Processes.process="*rebase*" AND Processes.process="*--exec*" by host Processes.user Processes.parent_process_name Processes.process_name Processes.process
| `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
| convert ctime(firstTime) ctime(lastTime)
[LLM] Gogs server log signature — failed --exec rebase exit status 128 Exploitation High
Detects the application-layer error string Rapid7 explicitly calls out as the defender's IOC: Gogs server logs containing `git checkout '--exec=<...>': exit status 128`. Surfaces both successful exploitation and failed/recon attempts where the payload errored before code execution — useful for catching scanning waves and Metasploit shotgun runs. Rationale: Direct quote from the article: 'Defenders should monitor Gogs server logs for ERROR-level entries containing patterns like git checkout \'--exec=<...>\': exit status 128.' This is the article's own recommended IOC. SPL is non-CIM raw search because Gogs application logs are not normalized into a standard Splunk datamodel; defender_kql and falcon_logscale_query are left empty because Defender/FDR do not natively ingest arbitrary Gogs application logs. Cross-checked against: • https://www.bleepingcomputer.com/news/security/new-gogs-zero-day-flaw-lets-hackers-get-remote-code-execution/
ATT&CKT1190 T1059
Data sources
Syslog
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where ProcessName has "gogs" or SyslogMessage contains "gogs"
| where SyslogMessage contains "git checkout '--exec=" and SyslogMessage contains "exit status 128"
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, HostIP, Facility, SeverityLevel, ProcessName, SyslogMessage
| order by TimeGenerated desc
title: Gogs Server Log - Failed Rebase With --exec Argument (Exit Status 128)

[LLM] Gogs repository ref file created with name starting with -- (weaponized PR branch) Weaponization High
Detects the planted-weapon stage of the Gogs Merge() 0-day: a loose ref file under a repo's `.git/refs/heads/` directory whose filename begins with `--`. When an attacker pushes a branch named `--exec=...`, Gogs writes that ref to disk before the merge button is ever clicked, so this fires even on dormant weaponization across the entire fleet. Rationale: Anchored on the article's instruction: 'Administrators should also audit repository branch listings for names beginning with --'. The loose-ref file on disk is the only durable, queryable artifact of a weaponized PR branch — it persists even if the attacker never clicks merge, giving SOCs a passive sweep across all Gogs fleet hosts. Cross-checked with the Bleeping Computer write-up confirming the branch-name vector. Cross-checked against: • https://www.bleepingcomputer.com/news/security/new-gogs-zero-day-flaw-lets-hackers-get-remote-code-execution/ • https://www.runzero.com/blog/gogs/
ATT&CKT1190 T1608

Data sourcesNetwork_Traffic.All_Traffic DeviceNetworkEvents
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(1d)
| where RemoteIPType == "Public" and ActionType == "ConnectionSuccess"
| project DeviceName, RemoteIP, RemotePort, Timestamp

| order by conn_count desc

Phishing-link click correlated to endpoint execution Delivery High
User received an external email containing a URL, clicked it, and within 60 seconds the recipient's endpoint spawned a scripting interpreter or network downloader (PowerShell / cmd / mshta / curl / certutil / bitsadmin). This is the high-fidelity shape — a raw "user clicked an emailed URL" query is too noisy to alert on because every Microsoft 365 tenant generates thousands of legitimate clicks per day. The exec-correlation step suppresses the noise to roughly the rate at which a click actually drives onto-host execution, which is the actionable signal. Pair with UC_PHISH_LINK_BYPASS (Safe Links override) and UC_PHISH_LINK_NEWDOMAIN for orthogonal high-fidelity variants.
ATT&CKT1566.002 T1204.001 T1059.001
Data sourcesEmail.All_Email Web Endpoint.Processes EmailEvents EmailUrlInfo UrlClickEvents DeviceProcessEvents
// Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s.
// Far higher fidelity than "every clicked URL" — most legitimate clicks
// never spawn a non-browser child process, so the join eliminates the
// 99% of noise that makes a raw click query unactionable.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let SuspectClicks = UrlClickEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where AccountName !endswith "$"
    | where ActionType in ("ClickAllowed","ClickedThrough")
    | join kind=inner (
        EmailEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
        | where DeliveryAction == "Delivered"
        | where EmailDirection == "Inbound"
        | project NetworkMessageId, Subject, SenderFromAddress, SenderFromDomain,
                  RecipientEmailAddress, EmailTimestamp = Timestamp
      ) on NetworkMessageId
    | join kind=leftouter (
        EmailUrlInfo | project NetworkMessageId, Url, UrlDomain
      ) on NetworkMessageId, Url
    | project ClickTime = Timestamp, AccountUpn, IPAddress, Url, UrlDomain,
              Subject, SenderFromAddress, SenderFromDomain, RecipientEmailAddress,
              ActionType;
// Correlate to a non-browser child process spawned within 60 seconds on
// the recipient's device.
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                         "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
| where FileName in~ ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                        "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe",
                        "bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe","curl.exe","wget.exe")
| join kind=inner SuspectClicks on $left.AccountName == $right.AccountUpn
| where Timestamp between (ClickTime .. ClickTime + 60s)
| project ClickTime, ProcessTime = Timestamp,
          DelaySec = datetime_diff('second', Timestamp, ClickTime),
          DeviceName, AccountName, RecipientEmailAddress, SenderFromAddress,
          Subject, Url, UrlDomain, ActionType,
          FileName, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFileName
| order by ClickTime desc
// UrlClickEvents has no clean Sentinel-native equivalent. The detection
// pivots to: Office Send→Receive proximity to SecurityEvent 4688 of a
// non-browser child process. Lower fidelity than the Defender version.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let SuspectMailUsers = OfficeActivity
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where OfficeWorkload == "Exchange"
    | where Operation =~ "Receive"
    | summarize Subject = any(Subject), Sender = any(Sender)
                by MailboxOwnerUPN, MessageId, EmailTime = bin(TimeGenerated, 1m);
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
| where EventID == 4688
| where ParentProcessName has_any ("\chrome.exe","\msedge.exe",
                                     "\firefox.exe","\outlook.exe","\brave.exe")
| where NewProcessName has_any ("\powershell.exe","\pwsh.exe","\cmd.exe",
                                  "\mshta.exe","\rundll32.exe","\regsvr32.exe",
                                  "\wscript.exe","\cscript.exe","\bitsadmin.exe",
                                  "\certutil.exe","\curl.exe","\wget.exe")
| join kind=inner SuspectMailUsers on $left.Account == $right.MailboxOwnerUPN
| where TimeGenerated between (EmailTime .. EmailTime + 60s)
| project TimeGenerated, EmailTime, Computer, Account, ParentProcessName,
          NewProcessName, CommandLine, Sender, Subject
| order by TimeGenerated desc
WEB
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
``` Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s ```
| tstats `summariesonly` earliest(_time) AS click_time
    from datamodel=Web
    where Web.action="allowed"
    by Web.src, Web.user, Web.dest, Web.url
| `drop_dm_object_name(Web)`
| rename user AS recipient, dest AS clicked_domain, url AS clicked_url
| join type=inner recipient
    [| tstats `summariesonly` count
         from datamodel=Email.All_Email
         where All_Email.action="delivered" AND All_Email.url!="-"
         by All_Email.recipient, All_Email.src_user, All_Email.url, All_Email.subject
     | `drop_dm_object_name(All_Email)`
     | rex field=url "https?://(?<email_domain>[^/]+)"
     | rename recipient AS recipient]
| join type=inner src
    [| tstats `summariesonly` earliest(_time) AS exec_time
         values(Processes.process) AS exec_cmd, values(Processes.process_name) AS exec_proc
         from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
         where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                                   "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
           AND Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                                            "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe",
                                            "cscript.exe","bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe",
                                            "curl.exe","wget.exe")
         by Processes.dest, Processes.user
     | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
     | rename dest AS src]
| eval delta_sec = exec_time - click_time
| where delta_sec >= 0 AND delta_sec <= 60
| table click_time, exec_time, delta_sec, recipient, src, src_user, subject,
        clicked_domain, clicked_url, exec_proc, exec_cmd
| sort - click_time

    [| tstats summariesonly=false earliest(_time) AS exec_time

Email attachment opened from external sender Delivery High
Attachment delivery + execution by recipient — most common malware initial access.
ATT&CKT1566.001 T1204.002
Data sourcesEmail.All_Email Endpoint.Processes EmailAttachmentInfo DeviceProcessEvents
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let MalAttachments = EmailAttachmentInfo
    | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where AccountName !endswith "$"
    | project NetworkMessageId, RecipientEmailAddress,
              AttachmentFileName = FileName, AttachmentSHA256 = SHA256;
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("OUTLOOK.EXE","winword.exe","excel.exe","powerpnt.exe")
| where FileName in~ ("cmd.exe","powershell.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe",
                      "mshta.exe","rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe")
| join kind=inner MalAttachments on $left.AccountUpn == $right.RecipientEmailAddress
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, FileName, ProcessCommandLine,
          InitiatingProcessFileName, AttachmentFileName, AttachmentSHA256
// Sentinel doesn't have an attachment-hash table. Best approximation:
// OfficeActivity Send/Receive activity + correlate to host process spawn.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let MailWithAttach = OfficeActivity
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where OfficeWorkload == "Exchange"
    | where Operation in~ ("Send","Receive")
    | where isnotempty(MessageId)
    | project EmailTime = TimeGenerated, MailboxOwnerUPN, Sender,
              Recipients, Subject, MessageId;
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
| where EventID == 4688
| where ParentProcessName endswith "OUTLOOK.EXE"
| where NewProcessName endswith "\cmd.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\powershell.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\wscript.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\cscript.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\mshta.exe"
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, Account, NewProcessName, CommandLine,
          ParentProcessName
| order by TimeGenerated desc

title: Office Application Spawning Script Host
id: 7c8b2e10-4d4f-4a8c-9c1f-bf6e2c4a8d07
status: experimental
description: |
    Word/Excel/Outlook/OneNote spawning powershell, cmd, wscript,
    cscript, mshta, rundll32, regsvr32 — classic macro / embedded-
    object payload signature.
references:
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1059/
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1566/001/
author: Clankerusecase
date: 2026/05/02
tags:
    - attack.t1059
    - attack.t1566.001
    - attack.execution
logsource:
    category: process_creation
    product: windows
detection:
    selection_parent:
        ParentImage|endswith:
            - '\winword.exe'
            - '\excel.exe'
            - '\powerpnt.exe'
            - '\outlook.exe'
            - '\onenote.exe'
            - '\mspub.exe'
            - '\visio.exe'
    selection_child:
        Image|endswith:

Hackers Deploy VIP Keylogger Through Phishing Emails Masquerading as Business Documents

Cyber Security News
2026-05-28 15 use cases 6 techniques 6 kill-chain phases detected

Hackers are using deceptive phishing emails dressed up as routine business documents to spread a dangerous malware strain known as VIP Keylogger. The campaign has been active for months, with attackers showing absolutely no signs of slowing down. VIP Keylogger is part of a broader wave of information-stealing malware that has taken over the threat [&#8230;] The post Hackers Deploy VIP Keylogger Through Phishing Emails Masquerading as Business Documents appeared first on Cyber Security News .

Weaponization. Coupling exploit code with deliverable payload (e.g. weaponized PDF/Office doc, trojanized installer).
Delivery. Transmitting the weapon (phishing email, USB, watering hole, drive-by, malicious ad). → [LLM] VIP Keylogger steganographic PNG payload download from vault88x.secure-efficient2.su · Phishing-link click correlated to endpoint execution · Email attachment opened from external sender
Exploitation. Triggering the exploit — vulnerability/macro/trust abuse to execute code. → Office app spawning script/LOLBin child process · Fake CAPTCHA / clipboard-injected PowerShell (ClickFix / FakeCaptcha) · PowerShell encoded / obfuscated command · Article-specific behavioural hunt — Hackers Deploy VIP Keylogger Through Phishing Emails Masquerading as Business Do
Installation. Establishing persistence on the host — backdoor, service, scheduled task, registry key. → [LLM] VIP Keylogger persistence via UserInitMprLogonScript registry value · [LLM] VIP Keylogger PowerShell stager hidden in INTERNAL_DB_CACHE environment variable · [LLM] VIP Keylogger loader chain: script-host parent spawning PowerShell that reads environment variables · File hash IOCs — endpoint file/process match
Command & Control. Beacon to attacker infrastructure for control and tasking. → [LLM] aspnet_compiler.exe making outbound public network connections (VIP Keylogger injection target) · Beaconing — periodic outbound to small set of destinations · Network connections to article IPs / domains
Actions on Objectives. Lateral movement, credential dumping, data theft, ransomware, sabotage. → [LLM] VIP Keylogger sandbox / geolocation reconnaissance via reallyfreegeoip and checkip.dyndns from non-browser process
[LLM] VIP Keylogger persistence via UserInitMprLogonScript registry value Installation High
Detects creation or modification of the rarely-used UserInitMprLogonScript registry value, which VIP Keylogger abuses to invoke its PowerShell stager at every user logon. Legitimate use is essentially limited to a small set of enterprise logon-script GPOs and is extremely rare on non-server endpoints. Rationale: The article calls out UserInitMprLogonScript by name as the persistence anchor (STRT explicit recommendation). The key is rarely written outside GPO-pushed logon scripts, making this a high-fidelity, near-zero-FP alert. Cross-checked against: • https://cybersecuritynews.com/hackers-deploy-vip-keylogger-through-phishing-emails/
ATT&CKT1547.004 T1112
Data sourcesEndpoint.Registry
DeviceRegistryEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where ActionType in ("RegistryValueSet","RegistryKeyCreated")
| where RegistryValueName =~ "UserInitMprLogonScript"
| where isnotempty(RegistryValueData)
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, InitiatingProcessAccountName, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessParentFileName, RegistryKey, RegistryValueName, RegistryValueData
| order by Timestamp desc
ImRegistryEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where RegistryValue =~ "UserInitMprLogonScript"
| where isnotempty(RegistryValueData)
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, ActingProcessName, ActingProcessCommandLine, RegistryKey, RegistryValue, RegistryValueData
| order by TimeGenerated desc

[LLM] VIP Keylogger PowerShell stager hidden in INTERNAL_DB_CACHE environment variable Installation High
Hunts for the article-specific registry environment variable INTERNAL_DB_CACHE used by VIP Keylogger to stash an AES-encrypted PowerShell stager, plus any process command-line that subsequently reads it. The string is unique enough to act as a tripwire on its own. Rationale: INTERNAL_DB_CACHE is a unique string named explicitly in the article as the staging variable for the PowerShell stager. Searching it across both registry writes and command-line reads catches both the persistence write and the execution-time read. Cross-checked against: • https://cybersecuritynews.com/hackers-deploy-vip-keylogger-through-phishing-emails/
ATT&CKT1112 T1140 T1027
Data sourcesEndpoint.Registry Endpoint.Processes
union
(DeviceRegistryEvents
  | where Timestamp > ago(14d)
  | where RegistryValueName =~ "INTERNAL_DB_CACHE" or RegistryKey has @"\Environment\INTERNAL_DB_CACHE"
  | project Timestamp, DeviceName, Channel="Registry", Process=InitiatingProcessFileName, Cmd=InitiatingProcessCommandLine, Parent=InitiatingProcessParentFileName, Detail=strcat(RegistryKey, "\\", RegistryValueName), Payload=substring(RegistryValueData, 0, 256)),
(DeviceProcessEvents
  | where Timestamp > ago(14d)
  | where ProcessCommandLine has "INTERNAL_DB_CACHE"
  | project Timestamp, DeviceName, Channel="Process", Process=FileName, Cmd=ProcessCommandLine, Parent=InitiatingProcessFileName, Detail=InitiatingProcessCommandLine, Payload="")
| order by Timestamp desc
union isfuzzy=true
(ImRegistryEvent
  | where TimeGenerated > ago(14d)
  | where RegistryValue =~ "INTERNAL_DB_CACHE" or RegistryKey has @"\Environment\INTERNAL_DB_CACHE"
  | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, Channel="Registry", Process=ActingProcessName, Cmd=ActingProcessCommandLine, Detail=strcat(RegistryKey, "\\", RegistryValue), Payload=substring(RegistryValueData, 0, 256)),
(SecurityEvent
  | where TimeGenerated > ago(14d)
  | where EventID == 4688
  | where CommandLine has "INTERNAL_DB_CACHE"
  | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname=Computer, Channel="Process", Process=NewProcessName, Cmd=CommandLine, Detail=ParentProcessName, Payload="")
| order by TimeGenerated desc

[LLM] aspnet_compiler.exe making outbound public network connections (VIP Keylogger injection target) Command & Control High
aspnet_compiler.exe is a build-time ASP.NET pre-compilation utility that legitimately has no need to make external network connections. VIP Keylogger injects its final payload into aspnet_compiler.exe; surfacing any public network traffic from that process is high-signal. Rationale: Article explicitly names aspnet_compiler.exe as the injection target. The binary has no legitimate need to reach the public internet (it pre-compiles local ASP.NET sites), so any outbound public connection is essentially TP — particularly to api.telegram.org or vault88x.secure-efficient2.su. Cross-checked against: • https://cybersecuritynews.com/hackers-deploy-vip-keylogger-through-phishing-emails/
ATT&CKT1055.012 T1071.001
Data sourcesNetwork_Traffic.All_Traffic
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName =~ "aspnet_compiler.exe"
| where RemoteIPType == "Public"
| where not(RemoteUrl has_any ("microsoft.com","windowsupdate.com","digicert.com","verisign.com"))
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, InitiatingProcessFolderPath, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessParentFileName, RemoteIP, RemoteUrl, RemotePort, Protocol
| order by Timestamp desc
WindowsEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where Provider == "Microsoft-Windows-Sysmon" and EventID == 3
| extend Image = tostring(EventData.Image), DestinationIp = tostring(EventData.DestinationIp), DestinationHostname = tostring(EventData.DestinationHostname), DestinationPort = tostring(EventData.DestinationPort), DestinationIsIpv6 = tostring(EventData.DestinationIsIpv6), User = tostring(EventData.User)
| where Image endswith "\\aspnet_compiler.exe"
| where not(DestinationHostname has_any ("microsoft.com","windowsupdate.com"))
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, User, Image, DestinationIp, DestinationHostname, DestinationPort
| order by TimeGenerated desc

[LLM] VIP Keylogger steganographic PNG payload download from vault88x.secure-efficient2.su Delivery High
Hunts for HTTP(S) fetches of the named steganography PNGs (MSI_105759.png, img_085027.png) or any traffic to the staging host vault88x.secure-efficient2.su. The PNGs carry AES-encoded payload components decoded in-memory by the PowerShell stager. Rationale: vault88x.secure-efficient2.su, MSI_105759.png, and img_085027.png are unique article-cited indicators. The .su TLD plus an oddly-prefixed hostname plus PNG payloads is a tight fingerprint with effectively zero benign overlap. Cross-checked against: • https://cybersecuritynews.com/hackers-deploy-vip-keylogger-through-phishing-emails/
ATT&CKT1105 T1027.003 T1071.001
Data sourcesWeb.Web Network_Traffic.All_Traffic
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(30d)
| where RemoteUrl has_any ("vault88x.secure-efficient2.su","secure-efficient2.su","MSI_105759.png","img_085027.png")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessParentFileName, RemoteIP, RemoteUrl, RemotePort
| order by Timestamp desc
union isfuzzy=true
(CommonSecurityLog
  | where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
  | where RequestURL has_any ("vault88x.secure-efficient2.su","secure-efficient2.su","MSI_105759.png","img_085027.png") or DestinationHostName has "secure-efficient2.su"
  | project TimeGenerated, SourceIP, SourceUserName, DestinationHostName, RequestURL, DeviceProduct, DeviceVendor),
(DnsEvents
  | where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
  | where Name has "secure-efficient2.su"
  | project TimeGenerated, Computer, ClientIP, Name, QueryType, ResultCode)
| order by TimeGenerated desc

[LLM] VIP Keylogger loader chain: script-host parent spawning PowerShell that reads environment variables Installation High
Detects the VIP Keylogger execution pattern where wscript.exe / cscript.exe / cmd.exe (invoked on a .vbs/.js/.bat attachment) spawns PowerShell that reads its stager from a registry/environment variable. This is the bridge between the document-themed lure and the encoded stager. Rationale: Combines the article's three diagnostic elements: (1) script-host parent invoking a .vbs/.js/.bat, (2) PowerShell child, (3) command-line referencing an environment variable read (or the literal INTERNAL_DB_CACHE name). Each alone is noisy; together they isolate the VIP Keylogger loader chain. Cross-checked against: • https://cybersecuritynews.com/hackers-deploy-vip-keylogger-through-phishing-emails/
ATT&CKT1059.001 T1059.005 T1059.007 T1204.002
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(14d)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("wscript.exe","cscript.exe","cmd.exe")
| where FileName in~ ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe")
| where ProcessCommandLine has_any ("$env:","[Environment]::GetEnvironmentVariable","gci env:","Get-ChildItem env:","INTERNAL_DB_CACHE")
| where InitiatingProcessCommandLine has_any (".vbs",".js",".bat",".vbe",".jse")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, InitiatingProcessParentFileName, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, FileName, ProcessCommandLine, SHA256
| order by Timestamp desc
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(14d)
| where EventID == 4688
| extend ParentName = tostring(split(ParentProcessName, "\\")[-1]), ChildName = tostring(split(NewProcessName, "\\")[-1])
| where tolower(ParentName) in ("wscript.exe","cscript.exe","cmd.exe")
| where tolower(ChildName) in ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe")
| where CommandLine has_any ("$env:","[Environment]::GetEnvironmentVariable","gci env:","Get-ChildItem env:","INTERNAL_DB_CACHE")
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, SubjectUserName, ParentProcessName, NewProcessName, CommandLine
| order by TimeGenerated desc
title: Script Host Spawning PowerShell Reading Environment Variable (VIP Keylogger)
id: 2f9c4a18-8d62-4b3f-91c2-3e1a5f0d8e72
description: VIP Keylogger loader pattern - wscript/cscript/cmd invokes PowerShell that reads its stager from a registry environment variable (INTERNAL_DB_CACHE).
references:
  - https://cybersecuritynews.com/hackers-deploy-vip-keylogger-through-phishing-emails/
author: SOC Detection Engineering
date: 2026/05/28
tags:

  - attack.t1059.005
  - attack.t1059.007
  - attack.t1204.002
logsource:
  category: process_creation
  product: windows
detection:
  selection_parent:
    ParentImage|endswith:
      - '\wscript.exe'
      - '\cscript.exe'
      - '\cmd.exe'
  selection_child:
    Image|endswith:
      - '\powershell.exe'
      - '\pwsh.exe'
  selection_env:
    CommandLine|contains:
      - '$env:'
      - '[Environment]::GetEnvironmentVariable'
      - 'gci env:'
      - 'Get-ChildItem env:'
      - 'INTERNAL_DB_CACHE'
  condition: selection_parent and selection_child and selection_env
level: high
source:windows.sysmon @EventID:1 (@ParentImage:*\\wscript.exe OR @ParentImage:*\\cscript.exe OR @ParentImage:*\\cmd.exe OR @ParentImage:*\\WScript.exe OR @ParentImage:*\\CScript.exe) (@Image:*\\powershell.exe OR @Image:*\\pwsh.exe OR @Image:*\\PowerShell.exe) (@CommandLine:*$env:* OR @CommandLine:*GetEnvironmentVariable* OR @CommandLine:*INTERNAL_DB_CACHE*)
#event_simpleName=ProcessRollup2 ParentBaseFileName=/(wscript|cscript|cmd)\.exe$/i ImageFileName=/(powershell|pwsh)\.exe$/i
| regex("(\\$env:|GetEnvironmentVariable|Get-ChildItem env:|gci env:|INTERNAL_DB_CACHE)", field=CommandLine)
| groupBy([aid, ComputerName, UserName, ParentBaseFileName, ImageFileName, CommandLine], function=count())
ENDPOINT

| tstats summariesonly=true count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime values(Processes.process) as process values(Processes.parent_process) as parent_process from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("wscript.exe","cscript.exe","cmd.exe") AND Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe") AND (Processes.process="*$env:*" OR Processes.process="*[Environment]::GetEnvironmentVariable*" OR Processes.process="*gci env:*" OR Processes.process="*Get-ChildItem env:*" OR Processes.process="*INTERNAL_DB_CACHE*") AND (Processes.parent_process="*.vbs*" OR Processes.parent_process="*.js*" OR Processes.parent_process="*.bat*") by Processes.dest Processes.user Processes.parent_process_name Processes.process_name | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)` | convert ctime(firstTime) ctime(lastTime)
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime values(Processes.process) as process values(Processes.parent_process) as parent_process from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("wscript.exe","cscript.exe","cmd.exe") AND Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe") AND (Processes.process="*$env:*" OR Processes.process="*[Environment]::GetEnvironmentVariable*" OR Processes.process="*gci env:*" OR Processes.process="*Get-ChildItem env:*" OR Processes.process="*INTERNAL_DB_CACHE*") AND (Processes.parent_process="*.vbs*" OR Processes.parent_process="*.js*" OR Processes.parent_process="*.bat*") by Processes.dest Processes.user Processes.parent_process_name Processes.process_name | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)` | convert ctime(firstTime) ctime(lastTime)
[LLM] VIP Keylogger sandbox / geolocation reconnaissance via reallyfreegeoip and checkip.dyndns from non-browser process Actions on Objectives High
Surfaces requests to reallyfreegeoip.org/xml/ or checkip.dyndns.org made by interpreters or LOLBins rather than browsers. VIP Keylogger uses these endpoints for IP-based sandbox detection and host geolocation before fully unpacking. Rationale: Both URLs are explicitly cited as VIP Keylogger sandbox/geolocation checks. Real users hit these only via browsers (and rarely even then); a script interpreter or aspnet_compiler.exe resolving them is a near-pure TP. Cross-checked against: • https://cybersecuritynews.com/hackers-deploy-vip-keylogger-through-phishing-emails/
ATT&CKT1016 T1016.001 T1497.001
Data sourcesWeb.Web Network_Traffic.All_Traffic
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where RemoteUrl has_any ("reallyfreegeoip.org/xml","checkip.dyndns.org") or RemoteUrl endswith "reallyfreegeoip.org" or RemoteUrl endswith "checkip.dyndns.org"
| where not(InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe","iexplore.exe","brave.exe","opera.exe","safari.exe"))
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessParentFileName, RemoteIP, RemoteUrl, RemotePort
| order by Timestamp desc
union isfuzzy=true
(DnsEvents
  | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
  | where Name has_any ("reallyfreegeoip.org","checkip.dyndns.org")
  | project TimeGenerated, Computer, ClientIP, Name, QueryType),
(CommonSecurityLog
  | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
  | where RequestURL has_any ("reallyfreegeoip.org/xml","checkip.dyndns.org") or DestinationHostName in~ ("reallyfreegeoip.org","checkip.dyndns.org")
  | where not(RequestClientApplication has_any ("Chrome","Edg/","Firefox","Safari"))
  | project TimeGenerated, SourceIP, SourceUserName, DestinationHostName, RequestURL, RequestClientApplication)
| order by TimeGenerated desc

Beaconing — periodic outbound to small set of destinations Command & Control Medium
C2 channel detection via inter-beacon-time stddev / fan-out to single dest.
ATT&CKT1071.001 T1071.004
Data sourcesNetwork_Traffic.All_Traffic DeviceNetworkEvents
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(1d)
| where RemoteIPType == "Public" and ActionType == "ConnectionSuccess"
| project DeviceName, RemoteIP, RemotePort, Timestamp
| sort by DeviceName asc, RemoteIP asc, RemotePort asc, Timestamp asc
| extend prev_dev = prev(DeviceName, 1), prev_ip = prev(RemoteIP, 1),
         prev_port = prev(RemotePort, 1), prev_ts = prev(Timestamp, 1)
| where DeviceName == prev_dev and RemoteIP == prev_ip and RemotePort == prev_port
| extend delta_sec = datetime_diff('second', Timestamp, prev_ts)
| summarize conn_count = count(), avg_delta = avg(delta_sec), stdev_delta = stdev(delta_sec)
    by DeviceName, RemoteIP, RemotePort
| where conn_count > 30 and avg_delta between (30.0 .. 600.0) and stdev_delta < 5.0
| order by conn_count desc
ImNetworkSession
| where TimeGenerated > ago(2h)
| where DvcAction != "Block"
| where ipv4_is_private(DstIpAddr) == false
| summarize ConnCount = count(),
            DistinctMinutes = dcount(bin(TimeGenerated, 1m))
            by DvcHostname, DstIpAddr, DstPortNumber
| where ConnCount > 50 and DistinctMinutes > 30   // sustained, not bursty

Phishing-link click correlated to endpoint execution Delivery High
User received an external email containing a URL, clicked it, and within 60 seconds the recipient's endpoint spawned a scripting interpreter or network downloader (PowerShell / cmd / mshta / curl / certutil / bitsadmin). This is the high-fidelity shape — a raw "user clicked an emailed URL" query is too noisy to alert on because every Microsoft 365 tenant generates thousands of legitimate clicks per day. The exec-correlation step suppresses the noise to roughly the rate at which a click actually drives onto-host execution, which is the actionable signal. Pair with UC_PHISH_LINK_BYPASS (Safe Links override) and UC_PHISH_LINK_NEWDOMAIN for orthogonal high-fidelity variants.
ATT&CKT1566.002 T1204.001 T1059.001
Data sourcesEmail.All_Email Web Endpoint.Processes EmailEvents EmailUrlInfo UrlClickEvents DeviceProcessEvents
// Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s.
// Far higher fidelity than "every clicked URL" — most legitimate clicks
// never spawn a non-browser child process, so the join eliminates the
// 99% of noise that makes a raw click query unactionable.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let SuspectClicks = UrlClickEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where AccountName !endswith "$"
    | where ActionType in ("ClickAllowed","ClickedThrough")
    | join kind=inner (
        EmailEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
        | where DeliveryAction == "Delivered"
        | where EmailDirection == "Inbound"
        | project NetworkMessageId, Subject, SenderFromAddress, SenderFromDomain,
                  RecipientEmailAddress, EmailTimestamp = Timestamp
      ) on NetworkMessageId
    | join kind=leftouter (
        EmailUrlInfo | project NetworkMessageId, Url, UrlDomain
      ) on NetworkMessageId, Url
    | project ClickTime = Timestamp, AccountUpn, IPAddress, Url, UrlDomain,
              Subject, SenderFromAddress, SenderFromDomain, RecipientEmailAddress,
              ActionType;
// Correlate to a non-browser child process spawned within 60 seconds on
// the recipient's device.
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                         "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
| where FileName in~ ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                        "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe",
                        "bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe","curl.exe","wget.exe")
| join kind=inner SuspectClicks on $left.AccountName == $right.AccountUpn
| where Timestamp between (ClickTime .. ClickTime + 60s)
| project ClickTime, ProcessTime = Timestamp,
          DelaySec = datetime_diff('second', Timestamp, ClickTime),
          DeviceName, AccountName, RecipientEmailAddress, SenderFromAddress,
          Subject, Url, UrlDomain, ActionType,
          FileName, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFileName
| order by ClickTime desc
// UrlClickEvents has no clean Sentinel-native equivalent. The detection
// pivots to: Office Send→Receive proximity to SecurityEvent 4688 of a
// non-browser child process. Lower fidelity than the Defender version.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let SuspectMailUsers = OfficeActivity
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where OfficeWorkload == "Exchange"
    | where Operation =~ "Receive"
    | summarize Subject = any(Subject), Sender = any(Sender)
                by MailboxOwnerUPN, MessageId, EmailTime = bin(TimeGenerated, 1m);
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
| where EventID == 4688
| where ParentProcessName has_any ("\chrome.exe","\msedge.exe",
                                     "\firefox.exe","\outlook.exe","\brave.exe")
| where NewProcessName has_any ("\powershell.exe","\pwsh.exe","\cmd.exe",
                                  "\mshta.exe","\rundll32.exe","\regsvr32.exe",
                                  "\wscript.exe","\cscript.exe","\bitsadmin.exe",
                                  "\certutil.exe","\curl.exe","\wget.exe")
| join kind=inner SuspectMailUsers on $left.Account == $right.MailboxOwnerUPN
| where TimeGenerated between (EmailTime .. EmailTime + 60s)
| project TimeGenerated, EmailTime, Computer, Account, ParentProcessName,
          NewProcessName, CommandLine, Sender, Subject
| order by TimeGenerated desc
WEB
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
``` Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s ```
| tstats `summariesonly` earliest(_time) AS click_time
    from datamodel=Web
    where Web.action="allowed"
    by Web.src, Web.user, Web.dest, Web.url
| `drop_dm_object_name(Web)`
| rename user AS recipient, dest AS clicked_domain, url AS clicked_url
| join type=inner recipient
    [| tstats `summariesonly` count
         from datamodel=Email.All_Email
         where All_Email.action="delivered" AND All_Email.url!="-"
         by All_Email.recipient, All_Email.src_user, All_Email.url, All_Email.subject
     | `drop_dm_object_name(All_Email)`
     | rex field=url "https?://(?<email_domain>[^/]+)"
     | rename recipient AS recipient]
| join type=inner src
    [| tstats `summariesonly` earliest(_time) AS exec_time
         values(Processes.process) AS exec_cmd, values(Processes.process_name) AS exec_proc
         from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
         where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                                   "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
           AND Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                                            "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe",
                                            "cscript.exe","bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe",
                                            "curl.exe","wget.exe")
         by Processes.dest, Processes.user
     | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
     | rename dest AS src]
| eval delta_sec = exec_time - click_time
| where delta_sec >= 0 AND delta_sec <= 60
| table click_time, exec_time, delta_sec, recipient, src, src_user, subject,
        clicked_domain, clicked_url, exec_proc, exec_cmd
| sort - click_time
