[LLM] Mini Shai-Hulud npm worm exfil to filev2.getsession.org Actions on Objectives High
Detects outbound traffic to filev2.getsession.org — the Session decentralised-network endpoint the Mini Shai-Hulud / Sha1-Hulud npm worm uses to exfil harvested GitHub, npm, cloud, Kubernetes, Vault, Docker and SSH credentials. Scopes to Node.js / package-manager process context so it doesn't fire on a real user running the Session messenger. Rationale: Article lists filev2.getsession.org in the IOC bundle. Cross-checked with Wiz (Mini Shai-Hulud), Socket (Tanstack packages), BleepingComputer and StepSecurity — all confirm Session's decentralized P2P file API as the exfil channel; gating on Node/npm/yarn/pnpm/bun parent process distinguishes worm exfil from a real user's Session messenger traffic. Cross-checked against: • https://www.wiz.io/blog/mini-shai-hulud-strikes-again-tanstack-more-npm-packages-compromised • https://socket.dev/blog/tanstack-npm-packages-compromised-mini-shai-hulud-supply-chain-attack • https://www.stepsecurity.io/blog/mini-shai-hulud-is-back-a-self-spreading-supply-chain-attack-hits-the-npm-ecosystem • https://www.bleepingcomputer.com/news/security/new-shai-hulud-malware-wave-compromises-600-npm-packages/

[LLM] Shai-Hulud worm GitHub Action workflow file dropped under .github/workflows Installation High
Detects file creation of shai-hulud-workflow.yml / shai-hulud.yaml / discussion.yaml under any .github/workflows/ directory on a developer host. The Shai-Hulud and Shai-Hulud 2.0 worms write this workflow then push it to a fresh branch so a PUSH-triggered Action exfiltrates harvested secrets. Rationale: Article references Mini Shai-Hulud and the postinstall credential-theft chain. Workflow filename triplet (shai-hulud-workflow.yml / shai-hulud.yaml / discussion.yaml) confirmed by Unit 42, Wiz, Datadog Security Labs and their public IOC repo. File-creation telemetry catches the worm during install-time, well before its GitHub push step. Cross-checked against: • https://unit42.paloaltonetworks.com/npm-supply-chain-attack/ • https://www.wiz.io/blog/shai-hulud-npm-supply-chain-attack • https://securitylabs.datadoghq.com/articles/shai-hulud-2.0-npm-worm/ • https://github.com/DataDog/indicators-of-compromise/tree/main/shai-hulud-2.0 • https://research.jfrog.com/post/shai-hulud-here-we-go-again/
ATT&CKT1195.002 T1546 T1567.002

| where ActionType in ("FileCreated","FileModified","FileRenamed")

| project Timestamp, DeviceName, InitiatingProcessAccountName, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessParentFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, FolderPath, FileName, SHA256
| order by Timestamp desc

[LLM] postmark-mcp BCC exfil to giftshop.club Actions on Objectives High
Hunts for outbound DNS/HTTPS to giftshop.club — the domain hosting phan@giftshop.club, the BCC recipient hard-coded into postmark-mcp v1.0.16 (the first publicly documented malicious npm-distributed MCP server, disclosed by Koi Security). Also catches BCC of organisational email to @giftshop.club via mail-flow telemetry. Rationale: Article lists giftshop.club in the IOC bundle. Koi Security (original disclosure), Snyk, BleepingComputer and the official Postmark advisory all confirm the BCC address phan@giftshop.club embedded in postmark-mcp v1.0.16. Detecting on the domain catches both the BCC mail leg (via Office mail-flow) and any local Node.js process resolving it during MCP server startup. Cross-checked against: • https://www.koi.ai/blog/postmark-mcp-npm-malicious-backdoor-email-theft • https://snyk.io/blog/malicious-mcp-server-on-npm-postmark-mcp-harvests-emails/ • https://postmarkapp.com/blog/information-regarding-malicious-postmark-mcp-package • https://thehackernews.com/2025/09/first-malicious-mcp-server-found.html

    | project TimeGenerated, Host="", Actor=UserId, Indicator=tostring(Recipients), Path="mail";
union Net, Mail
| order by TimeGenerated desc

[LLM] npm/yarn/pnpm postinstall hook spawning credential-harvest tooling Installation Medium
Hunts for package-manager processes (npm/npx/yarn/pnpm/node/bun) spawning TruffleHog, curl/wget reaching the Shai-Hulud or postmark-mcp exfil hosts, or executing setup_bun.js / bun_environment.js — the signature install-time payload chain used by the Mini Shai-Hulud and Shai-Hulud 2.0 worms before EDR has a behavioural signal to bite on. Rationale: Article describes the npm postinstall credential-scraping chain (Mini Shai-Hulud, postmark-mcp). Datadog IOC repo, Wiz, Socket and Sysdig confirm setup_bun.js / bun_environment.js and TruffleHog binary execution from npm contexts as the post-compromise install-time signal — plus the webhook.site / filev2.getsession.org / giftshop.club exfil strings catch curl/wget invocations the worm chains. Cross-checked against: • https://www.wiz.io/blog/mini-shai-hulud-strikes-again-tanstack-more-npm-packages-compromised • https://securitylabs.datadoghq.com/articles/shai-hulud-2.0-npm-worm/ • https://socket.dev/blog/tanstack-npm-packages-compromised-mini-shai-hulud-supply-chain-attack • https://www.sysdig.com/blog/shai-hulud-the-novel-self-replicating-worm-infecting-hundreds-of-npm-packages • https://github.com/DataDog/indicators-of-compromise/tree/main/shai-hulud-2.0
ATT&CKT1059.007 T1195.002 T1552.001 T1546.016
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes
let PkgMgrs = dynamic(["npm.exe","npm.cmd","npx.exe","npx.cmd","yarn.exe","yarn.cmd","pnpm.exe","pnpm.cmd","node.exe","bun.exe","npm","npx","node","yarn","pnpm","bun"]);
let SuspChildren = dynamic(["trufflehog.exe","trufflehog","curl.exe","wget.exe","bun.exe"]);
let SuspStrings = dynamic(["setup_bun.js","bun_environment.js","trufflehog","webhook.site","filev2.getsession.org","giftshop.club"]);
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(30d)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ (PkgMgrs)
   or InitiatingProcessParentFileName in~ (PkgMgrs)
| where FileName in~ (SuspChildren)
   or ProcessCommandLine has_any (SuspStrings)
   or InitiatingProcessCommandLine has_any (SuspStrings)
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, InitiatingProcessParentFileName, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, FileName, ProcessCommandLine, SHA256
| order by Timestamp desc
let PkgMgrs = dynamic(["npm.exe","npx.exe","yarn.exe","pnpm.exe","node.exe","bun.exe","npm","npx","node","yarn","pnpm","bun"]);
let SuspChildren = dynamic(["trufflehog.exe","trufflehog","curl.exe","wget.exe","bun.exe"]);
let SuspStrings = dynamic(["setup_bun.js","bun_environment.js","trufflehog","webhook.site","filev2.getsession.org","giftshop.club"]);
ImProcessCreate
| where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
| where ParentProcessName has_any (PkgMgrs) or ActingProcessName has_any (PkgMgrs)
| where TargetProcessName has_any (SuspChildren) or TargetProcessCommandLine has_any (SuspStrings) or ActingProcessCommandLine has_any (SuspStrings)
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, ParentProcessName, ParentProcessCommandLine, ActingProcessName, TargetProcessName, TargetProcessCommandLine
| order by TimeGenerated desc
title: Package-Manager Postinstall Hook Spawning Credential-Harvest Tooling
id: a1c7f4b3-8e6c-4f39-9a5b-4c9d0e1f6234
description: npm/npx/yarn/pnpm/node/bun spawning trufflehog, or executing setup_bun.js / bun_environment.js, or reaching Shai-Hulud / postmark-mcp exfil hosts — the install-time payload chain documented across the Mini Shai-Hulud and Shai-Hulud 2.0 npm worm waves.
references:
  - https://www.wiz.io/blog/mini-shai-hulud-strikes-again-tanstack-more-npm-packages-compromised
  - https://securitylabs.datadoghq.com/articles/shai-hulud-2.0-npm-worm/
  - https://socket.dev/blog/tanstack-npm-packages-compromised-mini-shai-hulud-supply-chain-attack
  - https://www.koi.ai/blog/postmark-mcp-npm-malicious-backdoor-email-theft
author: SOC Detection Engineering
date: 2026/05/28
tags:
  - attack.execution
  - attack.t1059.007
  - attack.t1195.002
  - attack.t1552.001
logsource:
  category: process_creation
detection:
  parent_pkg_mgr:
    ParentImage|endswith:
      - '\npm.exe'
      - '\npx.exe'
      - '\node.exe'
      - '\yarn.exe'
      - '\pnpm.exe'
      - '\bun.exe'
      - '/npm'
      - '/npx'
      - '/node'
      - '/yarn'
      - '/pnpm'
      - '/bun'
  child_susp_tool:
    Image|endswith:
      - '\trufflehog.exe'
      - '\trufflehog'
      - '/trufflehog'
      - '\bun.exe'
  child_susp_cmd:
    CommandLine|contains:
      - 'setup_bun.js'
      - 'bun_environment.js'
      - 'trufflehog'
      - 'webhook.site'
      - 'filev2.getsession.org'
      - 'giftshop.club'
  condition: parent_pkg_mgr and (child_susp_tool or child_susp_cmd)
falsepositives:
  - CI/CD pipelines that legitimately run trufflehog secret scanning inside npm scripts
  - Developers manually invoking trufflehog from a Node tool wrapper
level: high
source:windows.sysmon @EventID:1 @ParentImage:(*\npm.exe OR *\Npm.exe OR *\npx.exe OR *\node.exe OR *\Node.exe OR *\yarn.exe OR *\pnpm.exe OR *\bun.exe) (@Image:(*\trufflehog.exe OR *\TruffleHog.exe OR *\curl.exe OR *\wget.exe OR *\bun.exe) OR @CommandLine:(*setup_bun.js* OR *bun_environment.js* OR *trufflehog* OR *TruffleHog* OR *webhook.site* OR *filev2.getsession.org* OR *giftshop.club*))
#event_simpleName=ProcessRollup2 ParentBaseFileName=/^(npm|npx|node|yarn|pnpm|bun)(\.exe)?$/i
| ImageFileName=/(trufflehog|curl|wget|bun)(\.exe)?$/i OR CommandLine=/(setup_bun\.js|bun_environment\.js|trufflehog|webhook\.site|filev2\.getsession\.org|giftshop\.club)/i
| groupBy([aid, ComputerName, ParentBaseFileName, ImageFileName, CommandLine], function=count())
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats summariesonly=true count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes where (Processes.parent_process_name IN ("npm.exe","npx.exe","node.exe","yarn.exe","pnpm.exe","bun.exe","npm","npx","node","yarn","pnpm","bun")) AND (Processes.process_name IN ("trufflehog.exe","trufflehog","curl.exe","wget.exe","bun.exe") OR Processes.process="*setup_bun.js*" OR Processes.process="*bun_environment.js*" OR Processes.process="*trufflehog*" OR Processes.process="*webhook.site*" OR Processes.process="*filev2.getsession.org*" OR Processes.process="*giftshop.club*") by host Processes.user Processes.parent_process_name Processes.parent_process Processes.process_name Processes.process | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)` | `security_content_ctime(firstTime)` | `security_content_ctime(lastTime)`

Beaconing — periodic outbound to small set of destinations Command & Control Medium
C2 channel detection via inter-beacon-time stddev / fan-out to single dest.
ATT&CKT1071.001 T1071.004
Data sourcesNetwork_Traffic.All_Traffic DeviceNetworkEvents
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(1d)
| where RemoteIPType == "Public" and ActionType == "ConnectionSuccess"
| project DeviceName, RemoteIP, RemotePort, Timestamp
| sort by DeviceName asc, RemoteIP asc, RemotePort asc, Timestamp asc
| extend prev_dev = prev(DeviceName, 1), prev_ip = prev(RemoteIP, 1),
         prev_port = prev(RemotePort, 1), prev_ts = prev(Timestamp, 1)
| where DeviceName == prev_dev and RemoteIP == prev_ip and RemotePort == prev_port
| extend delta_sec = datetime_diff('second', Timestamp, prev_ts)
| summarize conn_count = count(), avg_delta = avg(delta_sec), stdev_delta = stdev(delta_sec)
    by DeviceName, RemoteIP, RemotePort
| where conn_count > 30 and avg_delta between (30.0 .. 600.0) and stdev_delta < 5.0
| order by conn_count desc
ImNetworkSession
| where TimeGenerated > ago(2h)
| where DvcAction != "Block"
| where ipv4_is_private(DstIpAddr) == false
| summarize ConnCount = count(),
            DistinctMinutes = dcount(bin(TimeGenerated, 1m))
            by DvcHostname, DstIpAddr, DstPortNumber
| where ConnCount > 50 and DistinctMinutes > 30   // sustained, not bursty
| order by ConnCount desc
NETWORK
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count, values(All_Traffic.dest_port) AS ports
    from datamodel=Network_Traffic.All_Traffic
    where All_Traffic.action="allowed" AND All_Traffic.dest_category!="internal"
    by _time span=10s, All_Traffic.src, All_Traffic.dest
| `drop_dm_object_name(All_Traffic)`
| streamstats current=f last(_time) AS prev_time by src, dest
| eval delta = _time - prev_time
| stats avg(delta) AS avg_delta stdev(delta) AS sd_delta count by src, dest
| where count > 30 AND sd_delta < 5 AND avg_delta>=30 AND avg_delta<=600
| sort - count
| tstats summariesonly=false count, values(All_Traffic.dest_port) AS ports
    from datamodel=Network_Traffic.All_Traffic
    where All_Traffic.action="allowed" AND All_Traffic.dest_category!="internal"
    by _time span=10s, All_Traffic.src, All_Traffic.dest
| `drop_dm_object_name(All_Traffic)`
| streamstats current=f last(_time) AS prev_time by src, dest
| eval delta = _time - prev_time
| stats avg(delta) AS avg_delta stdev(delta) AS sd_delta count by src, dest
| where count > 30 AND sd_delta < 5 AND avg_delta>=30 AND avg_delta<=600
| sort - count

Phishing-link click correlated to endpoint execution Delivery High
User received an external email containing a URL, clicked it, and within 60 seconds the recipient's endpoint spawned a scripting interpreter or network downloader (PowerShell / cmd / mshta / curl / certutil / bitsadmin). This is the high-fidelity shape — a raw "user clicked an emailed URL" query is too noisy to alert on because every Microsoft 365 tenant generates thousands of legitimate clicks per day. The exec-correlation step suppresses the noise to roughly the rate at which a click actually drives onto-host execution, which is the actionable signal. Pair with UC_PHISH_LINK_BYPASS (Safe Links override) and UC_PHISH_LINK_NEWDOMAIN for orthogonal high-fidelity variants.
ATT&CKT1566.002 T1204.001 T1059.001
Data sourcesEmail.All_Email Web Endpoint.Processes EmailEvents EmailUrlInfo UrlClickEvents DeviceProcessEvents
// Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s.
// Far higher fidelity than "every clicked URL" — most legitimate clicks
// never spawn a non-browser child process, so the join eliminates the
// 99% of noise that makes a raw click query unactionable.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let SuspectClicks = UrlClickEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where AccountName !endswith "$"
    | where ActionType in ("ClickAllowed","ClickedThrough")
    | join kind=inner (
        EmailEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
        | where DeliveryAction == "Delivered"
        | where EmailDirection == "Inbound"
        | project NetworkMessageId, Subject, SenderFromAddress, SenderFromDomain,
                  RecipientEmailAddress, EmailTimestamp = Timestamp
      ) on NetworkMessageId
    | join kind=leftouter (
        EmailUrlInfo | project NetworkMessageId, Url, UrlDomain
      ) on NetworkMessageId, Url
    | project ClickTime = Timestamp, AccountUpn, IPAddress, Url, UrlDomain,
              Subject, SenderFromAddress, SenderFromDomain, RecipientEmailAddress,
              ActionType;
// Correlate to a non-browser child process spawned within 60 seconds on
// the recipient's device.
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                         "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
| where FileName in~ ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                        "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe",
                        "bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe","curl.exe","wget.exe")
| join kind=inner SuspectClicks on $left.AccountName == $right.AccountUpn
| where Timestamp between (ClickTime .. ClickTime + 60s)
| project ClickTime, ProcessTime = Timestamp,
          DelaySec = datetime_diff('second', Timestamp, ClickTime),
          DeviceName, AccountName, RecipientEmailAddress, SenderFromAddress,
          Subject, Url, UrlDomain, ActionType,
          FileName, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFileName
| order by ClickTime desc
// UrlClickEvents has no clean Sentinel-native equivalent. The detection
// pivots to: Office Send→Receive proximity to SecurityEvent 4688 of a
// non-browser child process. Lower fidelity than the Defender version.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let SuspectMailUsers = OfficeActivity
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where OfficeWorkload == "Exchange"
    | where Operation =~ "Receive"
    | summarize Subject = any(Subject), Sender = any(Sender)
                by MailboxOwnerUPN, MessageId, EmailTime = bin(TimeGenerated, 1m);
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
| where EventID == 4688
| where ParentProcessName has_any ("\chrome.exe","\msedge.exe",
                                     "\firefox.exe","\outlook.exe","\brave.exe")
| where NewProcessName has_any ("\powershell.exe","\pwsh.exe","\cmd.exe",
                                  "\mshta.exe","\rundll32.exe","\regsvr32.exe",
                                  "\wscript.exe","\cscript.exe","\bitsadmin.exe",
                                  "\certutil.exe","\curl.exe","\wget.exe")
| join kind=inner SuspectMailUsers on $left.Account == $right.MailboxOwnerUPN
| where TimeGenerated between (EmailTime .. EmailTime + 60s)
| project TimeGenerated, EmailTime, Computer, Account, ParentProcessName,
          NewProcessName, CommandLine, Sender, Subject
| order by TimeGenerated desc
WEB
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
``` Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s ```
| tstats `summariesonly` earliest(_time) AS click_time
    from datamodel=Web
    where Web.action="allowed"
    by Web.src, Web.user, Web.dest, Web.url
| `drop_dm_object_name(Web)`
| rename user AS recipient, dest AS clicked_domain, url AS clicked_url
| join type=inner recipient
    [| tstats `summariesonly` count
         from datamodel=Email.All_Email
         where All_Email.action="delivered" AND All_Email.url!="-"
         by All_Email.recipient, All_Email.src_user, All_Email.url, All_Email.subject
     | `drop_dm_object_name(All_Email)`
     | rex field=url "https?://(?<email_domain>[^/]+)"
     | rename recipient AS recipient]
| join type=inner src
    [| tstats `summariesonly` earliest(_time) AS exec_time
         values(Processes.process) AS exec_cmd, values(Processes.process_name) AS exec_proc
         from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
         where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                                   "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
           AND Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                                            "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe",
                                            "cscript.exe","bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe",
                                            "curl.exe","wget.exe")
         by Processes.dest, Processes.user
     | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
     | rename dest AS src]
| eval delta_sec = exec_time - click_time
| where delta_sec >= 0 AND delta_sec <= 60
| table click_time, exec_time, delta_sec, recipient, src, src_user, subject,
        clicked_domain, clicked_url, exec_proc, exec_cmd
| sort - click_time

Email attachment opened from external sender Delivery High
Attachment delivery + execution by recipient — most common malware initial access.
ATT&CKT1566.001 T1204.002
Data sourcesEmail.All_Email Endpoint.Processes EmailAttachmentInfo DeviceProcessEvents
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let MalAttachments = EmailAttachmentInfo
    | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where AccountName !endswith "$"
    | project NetworkMessageId, RecipientEmailAddress,
              AttachmentFileName = FileName, AttachmentSHA256 = SHA256;
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("OUTLOOK.EXE","winword.exe","excel.exe","powerpnt.exe")
| where FileName in~ ("cmd.exe","powershell.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe",
                      "mshta.exe","rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe")
| join kind=inner MalAttachments on $left.AccountUpn == $right.RecipientEmailAddress
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, FileName, ProcessCommandLine,
          InitiatingProcessFileName, AttachmentFileName, AttachmentSHA256
// Sentinel doesn't have an attachment-hash table. Best approximation:
// OfficeActivity Send/Receive activity + correlate to host process spawn.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let MailWithAttach = OfficeActivity
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where OfficeWorkload == "Exchange"
    | where Operation in~ ("Send","Receive")
    | where isnotempty(MessageId)
    | project EmailTime = TimeGenerated, MailboxOwnerUPN, Sender,
              Recipients, Subject, MessageId;
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
| where EventID == 4688
| where ParentProcessName endswith "OUTLOOK.EXE"
| where NewProcessName endswith "\cmd.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\powershell.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\wscript.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\cscript.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\mshta.exe"
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, Account, NewProcessName, CommandLine,
          ParentProcessName
| order by TimeGenerated desc

    from datamodel=Email.All_Email

        by Processes.dest, Processes.user, Processes.parent_process_name, Processes.process_name, Processes.process

    by All_Email.src_user, All_Email.recipient, All_Email.file_name, All_Email.subject

title: Office Application Spawning Script Host

    by Processes.dest, Processes.user, Processes.parent_process_name, Processes.process_name, Processes.process

    from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
    where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("winword.exe","excel.exe","powerpnt.exe","outlook.exe","onenote.exe","mspub.exe","visio.exe")

OAuth consent / suspicious app grant Actions on Objectives High
Cloud identity abuse: app gets high-priv scopes, often via consent phishing.
ATT&CKT1528 T1098.001
Data sourcesAuthentication.Authentication CloudAppEvents
CloudAppEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where ActionType in ("Consent to application.","Add OAuth2PermissionGrant.","Add delegated permission grant.")
| project Timestamp, AccountObjectId, AccountDisplayName, ActivityType,
          ActivityObjects, IPAddress, UserAgent
// Entra ID directory audit — user / admin consent to a third-party app.
AuditLogs
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where OperationName has "Consent to application"
| where Result =~ "success"
| extend AppName = tostring(parse_json(tostring(TargetResources))[0].displayName),
         AppId   = tostring(parse_json(tostring(TargetResources))[0].id),
         User    = tostring(parse_json(tostring(InitiatedBy)).user.userPrincipalName)
| project TimeGenerated, OperationName, User, AppName, AppId, Result
| order by TimeGenerated desc

Trusted vendor binary / installer launching unusual children Exploitation Medium

Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes DeviceProcessEvents
DeviceProcessEvents

| where ParentProcessName has_any ("setup.exe","installer.exe","update.exe")
| where NewProcessName endswith "\powershell.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\cmd.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\rundll32.exe"

   or NewProcessName endswith "\mshta.exe"

File hash IOCs — endpoint file/process match Installation High
Match SHA256/SHA1/MD5 named in the article against EDR file/process telemetry.
ATT&CKT1027
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem Endpoint.Processes DeviceFileEvents DeviceProcessEvents
// Pre-filter each table BEFORE the union — the engine cannot push
// predicates across `union`, and DeviceFileEvents lacks ProcessCommandLine
// (Initiating only) so column-projection has to differ per side.
union
    ( DeviceFileEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(7d)
        | where InitiatingProcessAccountName !endswith "$"
        | where SHA256 in~ ("ab4fcadaec49c03278063dd269ea5eef82d24f2124a8e15d7b90f2fa8601266c", "2ec78d556d696e208927cc503d48e4b5eb56b31abc2870c2ed2e98d6be27fc96", "1a4afce34918bdc74ae3f31edaffffaa0ee074d83618f53edfd88137927340b8", "b0cefb66b953e5184b6adb3035e9e267335ac5eabfe1848e07834777b9397b74", "e7347d90653efc565f03733a95e9209d78f9cfa81e31ff2b2dd9d48d75a4b8b1", "558b09d7ad0d1660e2a0fb8a06da81a6f42e06d2", "ba642fe2c7c65e42dd7f6444b83023dc6827e08c") or SHA1 in~ ("ab4fcadaec49c03278063dd269ea5eef82d24f2124a8e15d7b90f2fa8601266c", "2ec78d556d696e208927cc503d48e4b5eb56b31abc2870c2ed2e98d6be27fc96", "1a4afce34918bdc74ae3f31edaffffaa0ee074d83618f53edfd88137927340b8", "b0cefb66b953e5184b6adb3035e9e267335ac5eabfe1848e07834777b9397b74", "e7347d90653efc565f03733a95e9209d78f9cfa81e31ff2b2dd9d48d75a4b8b1", "558b09d7ad0d1660e2a0fb8a06da81a6f42e06d2", "ba642fe2c7c65e42dd7f6444b83023dc6827e08c") or MD5 in~ ("ab4fcadaec49c03278063dd269ea5eef82d24f2124a8e15d7b90f2fa8601266c", "2ec78d556d696e208927cc503d48e4b5eb56b31abc2870c2ed2e98d6be27fc96", "1a4afce34918bdc74ae3f31edaffffaa0ee074d83618f53edfd88137927340b8", "b0cefb66b953e5184b6adb3035e9e267335ac5eabfe1848e07834777b9397b74", "e7347d90653efc565f03733a95e9209d78f9cfa81e31ff2b2dd9d48d75a4b8b1", "558b09d7ad0d1660e2a0fb8a06da81a6f42e06d2", "ba642fe2c7c65e42dd7f6444b83023dc6827e08c")
        | project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, FileName, FolderPath, SHA256,
                  Cmd = InitiatingProcessCommandLine, Source = "DeviceFileEvents" ),
    ( DeviceProcessEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(7d)
        | where AccountName !endswith "$"
        | where SHA256 in~ ("ab4fcadaec49c03278063dd269ea5eef82d24f2124a8e15d7b90f2fa8601266c", "2ec78d556d696e208927cc503d48e4b5eb56b31abc2870c2ed2e98d6be27fc96", "1a4afce34918bdc74ae3f31edaffffaa0ee074d83618f53edfd88137927340b8", "b0cefb66b953e5184b6adb3035e9e267335ac5eabfe1848e07834777b9397b74", "e7347d90653efc565f03733a95e9209d78f9cfa81e31ff2b2dd9d48d75a4b8b1", "558b09d7ad0d1660e2a0fb8a06da81a6f42e06d2", "ba642fe2c7c65e42dd7f6444b83023dc6827e08c") or SHA1 in~ ("ab4fcadaec49c03278063dd269ea5eef82d24f2124a8e15d7b90f2fa8601266c", "2ec78d556d696e208927cc503d48e4b5eb56b31abc2870c2ed2e98d6be27fc96", "1a4afce34918bdc74ae3f31edaffffaa0ee074d83618f53edfd88137927340b8", "b0cefb66b953e5184b6adb3035e9e267335ac5eabfe1848e07834777b9397b74", "e7347d90653efc565f03733a95e9209d78f9cfa81e31ff2b2dd9d48d75a4b8b1", "558b09d7ad0d1660e2a0fb8a06da81a6f42e06d2", "ba642fe2c7c65e42dd7f6444b83023dc6827e08c") or MD5 in~ ("ab4fcadaec49c03278063dd269ea5eef82d24f2124a8e15d7b90f2fa8601266c", "2ec78d556d696e208927cc503d48e4b5eb56b31abc2870c2ed2e98d6be27fc96", "1a4afce34918bdc74ae3f31edaffffaa0ee074d83618f53edfd88137927340b8", "b0cefb66b953e5184b6adb3035e9e267335ac5eabfe1848e07834777b9397b74", "e7347d90653efc565f03733a95e9209d78f9cfa81e31ff2b2dd9d48d75a4b8b1", "558b09d7ad0d1660e2a0fb8a06da81a6f42e06d2", "ba642fe2c7c65e42dd7f6444b83023dc6827e08c")
        | project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, FileName, FolderPath, SHA256,
                  Cmd = ProcessCommandLine, Source = "DeviceProcessEvents" )
| order by Timestamp desc

// Pre-filter both ASIM tables before the union — same pattern as the
// Defender version so the engine can push hash predicates per-side.
let BadHashes = dynamic(["ab4fcadaec49c03278063dd269ea5eef82d24f2124a8e15d7b90f2fa8601266c", "2ec78d556d696e208927cc503d48e4b5eb56b31abc2870c2ed2e98d6be27fc96", "1a4afce34918bdc74ae3f31edaffffaa0ee074d83618f53edfd88137927340b8", "b0cefb66b953e5184b6adb3035e9e267335ac5eabfe1848e07834777b9397b74", "e7347d90653efc565f03733a95e9209d78f9cfa81e31ff2b2dd9d48d75a4b8b1", "558b09d7ad0d1660e2a0fb8a06da81a6f42e06d2", "ba642fe2c7c65e42dd7f6444b83023dc6827e08c"]);
union
    ( ImFileEvent
        | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
        | where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
        | where TargetFileSHA256 in~ (BadHashes)
           or TargetFileSHA1 in~ (BadHashes)
           or TargetFileMD5 in~ (BadHashes)
        | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, EventType,
                  TargetFileName, TargetFilePath, TargetFileSHA256,
                  Cmd = ActingProcessName, Source = "ImFileEvent" ),
    ( ImProcessCreate
        | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
        | where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
        | where SHA256 in~ (BadHashes) or SHA1 in~ (BadHashes) or MD5 in~ (BadHashes)
        | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, EventType = TargetProcessName,
                  TargetFileName = TargetProcessName, TargetFilePath = TargetProcessName,
                  TargetFileSHA256 = SHA256,
                  Cmd = TargetProcessCommandLine, Source = "ImProcessCreate" )
| order by TimeGenerated desc

Carnival Cruise confirms data breach affecting nearly 6 million people

BleepingComputer
2026-05-28 7 use cases 2 techniques 5 kill-chain phases detected

Carnival Corporation, the world's largest cruise line operator, has confirmed a data breach affecting nearly 6 million people claimed by the ShinyHunters extortion gang in April 2026. [...]

Actions on Objectives
Detected
Reconnaissance. Attacker researches the target — OSINT, scanning, enumeration.
Weaponization. Coupling exploit code with deliverable payload (e.g. weaponized PDF/Office doc, trojanized installer).
Delivery. Transmitting the weapon (phishing email, USB, watering hole, drive-by, malicious ad). → [LLM] Helpdesk-impersonation pattern: AAD MFA method registration immediately followed by sign-in from new geo
Exploitation. Triggering the exploit — vulnerability/macro/trust abuse to execute code.
Installation. Establishing persistence on the host — backdoor, service, scheduled task, registry key. → [LLM] User consent to non-corporate OAuth app requesting Salesforce or mail-read scope
Command & Control. Beacon to attacker infrastructure for control and tasking. → Network connections to article IPs / domains
Actions on Objectives. Lateral movement, credential dumping, data theft, ransomware, sabotage. → [LLM] Bulk Salesforce record export / report download by single user (UNC6040 data-theft TTP) · Ransomware-style mass file rename / extension change · LSASS process access / dump (credential theft) · Remote service execution — PsExec / SMB lateral movement
[LLM] Bulk Salesforce record export / report download by single user (UNC6040 data-theft TTP) Actions on Objectives Medium
Detects a single Salesforce user account performing an abnormal volume of report exports, mass-transfers, list-view exports, or Bulk API jobs in a short window — the core data-theft action ShinyHunters/UNC6040 performs after social-engineering an employee, as seen in the Salesloft Drift and Salesforce Aura campaigns the article references. Rationale: Article names ShinyHunters and references their Salesloft Drift / Salesforce Aura campaigns; the public Mandiant write-ups on UNC6040 (Mandiant blog 2025) describe the post-access action as bulk report/Bulk-API exfil. Hunting on Salesforce ReportExport / BulkApi / MassTransfer event types in CloudAppEvents (MCAS Salesforce connector) is the highest-fidelity behaviour pivot for this campaign. Sentinel KQL left blank because Sentinel's standard schema in this tenant has no Salesforce table; operators on Sentinel should onboard the Salesforce connector before deploying this UC. Cross-checked against: • https://cloud.google.com/blog/topics/threat-intelligence/voice-phishing-data-extortion • https://www.haveibeenpwned.com/PwnedWebsites#Carnival
ATT&CKT1567 T1530 T1213
Data sourcesAuthentication.Authentication Change.Account_Management
CloudAppEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where Application =~ "Salesforce"
| where ActionType has_any ("ReportExport", "MassTransfer", "BulkApi", "BulkApi2", "DataExport", "ListViewExport", "ReportRunAsync", "ContentDistributionDownload")
| summarize EventCount = count(), DistinctObjects = dcount(ObjectName), SampleActions = make_set(ActionType, 10), FirstSeen = min(Timestamp), LastSeen = max(Timestamp), SrcIPs = make_set(IPAddress, 5), Geos = make_set(CountryCode, 5) by bin(Timestamp, 1h), AccountObjectId, AccountDisplayName
| where EventCount > 50 or DistinctObjects > 20
| order by EventCount desc
source:salesforce @evt.name:(ReportExport OR MassTransfer OR BulkApi OR BulkApi2 OR ListViewEvent OR ContentDistribution OR ApiTotalUsage)
APPLICATION
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
`summariesonly` | tstats count from datamodel=Authentication where Authentication.app="salesforce" Authentication.action="success" by Authentication.user Authentication.src _time span=1h | join type=outer Authentication.user [ search index=salesforce sourcetype=salesforce:eventlogfile EVENT_TYPE IN ("ReportExport","MassTransfer","BulkApi","BulkApi2","ListViewEvent","ContentDistribution","ContentDocumentLink","ApiTotalUsage") | rename USER_ID as user | stats sum(ROWS_PROCESSED) as RowsExported dc(EVENT_TYPE) as DistinctActions values(EVENT_TYPE) as ActionTypes by user ] | where RowsExported > 5000 OR DistinctActions >= 3 | sort - RowsExported
summariesonly=false | tstats count from datamodel=Authentication where Authentication.app="salesforce" Authentication.action="success" by Authentication.user Authentication.src _time span=1h | join type=outer Authentication.user [ search index=salesforce sourcetype=salesforce:eventlogfile EVENT_TYPE IN ("ReportExport","MassTransfer","BulkApi","BulkApi2","ListViewEvent","ContentDistribution","ContentDocumentLink","ApiTotalUsage") | rename USER_ID as user | stats sum(ROWS_PROCESSED) as RowsExported dc(EVENT_TYPE) as DistinctActions values(EVENT_TYPE) as ActionTypes by user ] | where RowsExported > 5000 OR DistinctActions >= 3 | sort - RowsExported
[LLM] User consent to non-corporate OAuth app requesting Salesforce or mail-read scope Installation High
Detects an Entra ID user granting consent to a third-party OAuth application requesting high-privilege Mail / Files / offline_access / Salesforce-API scopes — the persistence + token-theft pivot ShinyHunters has used in the Salesloft Drift campaign and against other Salesforce customers, where a malicious OAuth app retains access even after the social-engineered user's password is reset. Rationale: Cross-checked Mandiant's UNC6040/UNC6395 reporting on the Salesloft Drift campaign — the persistence vector after vishing the employee is consent-phishing of a malicious OAuth app, which survives password reset. The article explicitly ties Carnival's incident to the ShinyHunters Salesforce campaigns, making consent-to-non-Microsoft apps with mail/offline scopes the highest-leverage detection. Mail.Read / offline_access combo is the documented ShinyHunters scope set. Cross-checked against: • https://cloud.google.com/blog/topics/threat-intelligence/voice-phishing-data-extortion • https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1528/
ATT&CKT1528 T1550.001 T1098.003
Data sourcesChange.Account_Management Authentication.Authentication
CloudAppEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(30d)
| where ActionType in~ ("Consent to application", "Add OAuth2PermissionGrant", "Add delegated permission grant", "Add app role assignment grant to user")
| extend Raw = tostring(RawEventData)
| where Raw has_any ("Mail.Read", "Mail.ReadWrite", "offline_access", "Files.Read.All", "Sites.Read.All", "full_access", "refresh_token")
| extend AppName = tostring(parse_json(Raw).Target[0].Name)
| where isnotempty(AppName)
| where AppName !startswith "Microsoft" and AppName !has "Carnival"
| project Timestamp, AccountDisplayName, AccountObjectId, IPAddress, CountryCode, ActionType, AppName, Raw
| order by Timestamp desc
AuditLogs
| where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
| where OperationName has_any ("Consent to application", "Add OAuth2PermissionGrant", "Add delegated permission grant", "Add app role assignment grant to user")
| extend RawProps = tostring(TargetResources)
| where RawProps has_any ("Mail.Read", "Mail.ReadWrite", "offline_access", "Files.Read.All", "Sites.Read.All", "full_access", "refresh_token")
| extend AppName = tostring(parse_json(tostring(TargetResources))[0].displayName)
| extend Initiator = tostring(parse_json(tostring(InitiatedBy)).user.userPrincipalName)
| extend InitiatorIP = tostring(parse_json(tostring(InitiatedBy)).user.ipAddress)
| where AppName !startswith "Microsoft" and AppName !has "Carnival"
| project TimeGenerated, OperationName, Initiator, InitiatorIP, AppName, Result, RawProps
| order by TimeGenerated desc
title: Risky OAuth Consent to Non-Corporate App with Mail/Salesforce Scope
id: 7d3e9c11-2a4b-4c8f-9e6d-3f5a8b1c7d20
description: Detects an Entra ID user granting consent to a third-party OAuth app requesting Mail.Read, offline_access, Files.Read.All or Salesforce API scopes - ShinyHunters persistence pattern in the Salesloft Drift / Salesforce Aura campaigns.
references:
  - https://www.bleepingcomputer.com/news/security/carnival-cruise-confirms-data-breach-affecting-nearly-6-million-people/
  - https://cloud.google.com/blog/topics/threat-intelligence/voice-phishing-data-extortion
author: thn-detections
date: 2026/05/28
tags:
  - attack.t1528
  - attack.t1550.001
logsource:
  product: azure
  service: auditlogs
detection:
  selection:
    OperationName:
      - 'Consent to application'
      - 'Add OAuth2PermissionGrant'
      - 'Add delegated permission grant'
      - 'Add app role assignment grant to user'
    TargetResources|contains:
      - 'Mail.Read'
      - 'Mail.ReadWrite'
      - 'offline_access'
      - 'Files.Read.All'
      - 'Sites.Read.All'
      - 'full_access'
      - 'refresh_token'
  filter_ms:
    TargetResources|contains: 'Microsoft'
  condition: selection and not filter_ms
level: high
source:azure.activeDirectory @evt.name:("Consent to application" OR "Add OAuth2PermissionGrant" OR "Add delegated permission grant") (@properties.targetResources:*Mail.Read* OR @properties.targetResources:*offline_access* OR @properties.targetResources:*Files.Read.All* OR @properties.targetResources:*Sites.Read.All*)
CLOUD
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
`summariesonly` | tstats count from datamodel=Change where Change.action="created" Change.object_category="oauth_application" by Change.user Change.object Change.object_attrs _time | rename Change.user as user Change.object as AppDisplayName Change.object_attrs as Scopes | search Scopes IN ("*Mail.Read*","*Mail.ReadWrite*","*offline_access*","*Files.Read.All*","*Sites.Read.All*","*full*","*api*","*refresh_token*") AppDisplayName!="Microsoft*" AppDisplayName!="Carnival*" | sort - _time
summariesonly=false | tstats count from datamodel=Change where Change.action="created" Change.object_category="oauth_application" by Change.user Change.object Change.object_attrs _time | rename Change.user as user Change.object as AppDisplayName Change.object_attrs as Scopes | search Scopes IN ("*Mail.Read*","*Mail.ReadWrite*","*offline_access*","*Files.Read.All*","*Sites.Read.All*","*full*","*api*","*refresh_token*") AppDisplayName!="Microsoft*" AppDisplayName!="Carnival*" | sort - _time
[LLM] Helpdesk-impersonation pattern: AAD MFA method registration immediately followed by sign-in from new geo Delivery Medium
Detects a user's MFA authentication method being added/registered immediately followed by a successful sign-in from a previously-unseen country — the specific vishing-the-helpdesk pattern that gives ShinyHunters initial access (per the Carnival notification: 'unauthorized actor used social engineering to deceive an employee'). Rationale: Carnival notification states 'unauthorized actor used social engineering to deceive an employee' — this maps directly to the documented ShinyHunters / Scattered-Spider helpdesk-vishing pattern (call helpdesk → reset MFA → sign in). The temporal correlation between MFA registration / password reset and a first-seen-geo sign-in is the highest-fidelity behavioural signature for that specific vector. Cross-checked Mandiant's UNC6040 vishing write-up. Cross-checked against: • https://cloud.google.com/blog/topics/threat-intelligence/voice-phishing-data-extortion
ATT&CKT1556.006 T1078.004 T1098.005
Data sourcesAuthentication.Authentication Change.Account_Management
let MFAEvents = CloudAppEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where ActionType in~ ("Update user", "Register security info", "User registered security info", "Admin registered security info on behalf of user", "Reset user password", "Reset password (by admin)")
| extend Raw = tostring(RawEventData)
| where Raw has_any ("StrongAuthenticationMethod", "authenticatorAppMethod", "phoneAuthenticationMethod", "PhoneNumber")
| project MFATime = Timestamp, AccountObjectId, MFAAction = ActionType, MFAIP = IPAddress;
AADSignInEventsBeta
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where ErrorCode == 0
| where IsInteractive == true
| join kind=inner MFAEvents on AccountObjectId
| where Timestamp between (MFATime .. MFATime + 1h)
| extend MinutesAfterMFAChange = datetime_diff('minute', Timestamp, MFATime)
| join kind=leftanti (AADSignInEventsBeta | where Timestamp between (ago(90d) .. ago(7d)) | distinct AccountObjectId, Country) on AccountObjectId, Country
| project MFATime, SignInTime = Timestamp, MinutesAfterMFAChange, AccountUpn, MFAAction, MFAIP, SignInIP = IPAddress, Country, City, IPAddress, UserAgent
| order by SignInTime desc
let MFAEvents = AuditLogs
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where OperationName in~ ("Update user", "User registered security info", "Admin registered security info", "Reset user password", "Reset password (by admin)", "User started security info registration")
| extend Raw = tostring(TargetResources)
| where Raw has_any ("StrongAuthenticationMethod", "authenticatorAppMethod", "phoneAuthenticationMethod", "PhoneNumber")
| extend AccountObjectId = tostring(parse_json(tostring(TargetResources))[0].id)
| project MFATime = TimeGenerated, AccountObjectId, MFAAction = OperationName;
SigninLogs
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where ResultType == 0
| where IsInteractive == true
| extend AccountObjectId = UserId
| join kind=inner MFAEvents on AccountObjectId
| where TimeGenerated between (MFATime .. MFATime + 1h)
| extend Country = tostring(parse_json(tostring(Location)).countryOrRegion)
| join kind=leftanti (SigninLogs | where TimeGenerated between (ago(90d) .. ago(7d)) | extend Country = tostring(parse_json(tostring(Location)).countryOrRegion) | distinct UserId, Country) on $left.AccountObjectId == $right.UserId, Country
| extend MinutesAfterMFAChange = datetime_diff('minute', TimeGenerated, MFATime)
| project MFATime, SignInTime = TimeGenerated, MinutesAfterMFAChange, UserPrincipalName, MFAAction, IPAddress, Country, AppDisplayName, UserAgent
| order by SignInTime desc
source:azure.activeDirectory @evt.name:("User registered security info" OR "Admin registered security info" OR "Update user") @properties.targetResources:(*StrongAuthentication* OR *phoneAuthenticationMethod* OR *authenticatorAppMethod*)
CLOUD
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
`summariesonly` | tstats min(_time) as MfaTime from datamodel=Change where Change.action="modified" Change.object_category="user" (Change.object_attrs="*StrongAuthenticationMethod*" OR Change.object_attrs="*authenticationPhoneMethod*" OR Change.object_attrs="Update user*") by Change.user | rename Change.user as user | join type=inner user [ tstats min(_time) as LoginTime from datamodel=Authentication where Authentication.action="success" by Authentication.user Authentication.src Authentication.src_country | rename Authentication.user as user Authentication.src as src Authentication.src_country as country ] | where LoginTime > MfaTime AND LoginTime < MfaTime + 3600 | table user MfaTime LoginTime src country
summariesonly=false | tstats min(_time) as MfaTime from datamodel=Change where Change.action="modified" Change.object_category="user" (Change.object_attrs="*StrongAuthenticationMethod*" OR Change.object_attrs="*authenticationPhoneMethod*" OR Change.object_attrs="Update user*") by Change.user | rename Change.user as user | join type=inner user [ tstats min(_time) as LoginTime from datamodel=Authentication where Authentication.action="success" by Authentication.user Authentication.src Authentication.src_country | rename Authentication.user as user Authentication.src as src Authentication.src_country as country ] | where LoginTime > MfaTime AND LoginTime < MfaTime + 3600 | table user MfaTime LoginTime src country
Ransomware-style mass file rename / extension change Actions on Objectives Medium
Threshold detection: many files renamed in short window, often with new extension.
ATT&CKT1486
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem DeviceFileEvents
DeviceFileEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(1d)
| where InitiatingProcessAccountName !endswith "$"
| where ActionType in ("FileRenamed","FileModified")
| summarize files = dcount(FileName) by DeviceName, InitiatingProcessAccountName, bin(Timestamp, 1m)
| where files > 200    // empirical: > 200 unique-file renames in 1m by one account on one host
                       //            is well above the P99 of legitimate bulk-tooling
| order by files desc

ImFileEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(1d)
| where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
| where EventType in ("FileRenamed","FileModified")
| summarize files = dcount(TargetFileName)
            by DvcHostname, ActorUsername, ActingProcessName, bin(TimeGenerated, 1m)
| where files > 200    // P99 of legit bulk-tooling per-minute rename volume
| order by files desc
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count, dc(Filesystem.file_name) AS files
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Filesystem
    where Filesystem.action IN ("modified","renamed")
    by Filesystem.dest, Filesystem.user, _time span=1m
| `drop_dm_object_name(Filesystem)`
| where files > 200
| sort - files
| tstats summariesonly=false count, dc(Filesystem.file_name) AS files
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Filesystem
    where Filesystem.action IN ("modified","renamed")
    by Filesystem.dest, Filesystem.user, _time span=1m
| `drop_dm_object_name(Filesystem)`
| where files > 200
| sort - files
LSASS process access / dump (credential theft) Actions on Objectives High
Mimikatz, comsvcs.dll MiniDump, or any non-Windows process opening LSASS.
ATT&CKT1003.001 T1003
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes DeviceEvents
DeviceEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where AccountName !endswith "$"
| where ActionType == "OpenProcessApiCall"
| where FileName =~ "lsass.exe"
| where InitiatingProcessFileName !in~ ("MsSense.exe","MsMpEng.exe","csrss.exe",
                                          "svchost.exe","wininit.exe","services.exe",
                                          "lsm.exe","SearchProtocolHost.exe")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, FileName,
          InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine,
          InitiatingProcessFolderPath, AccountName
| order by Timestamp desc
// SecurityEvent EventID 4663 = object access. AccessMask 0x10 / 0x40 / 0x1010
// indicate read access to lsass.exe — credential-dump signature. Audit
// Object Access > Audit File System policy required.
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where EventID == 4663
| where ObjectName endswith "\lsass.exe"
| where Account !endswith "$"
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, Account, ObjectName, ProcessName,
          AccessMask, AccessReason
| order by TimeGenerated desc

2026 World Cup: Discussing The World’s Biggest Game’s Attack Surface

Unit 42 (Palo Alto)
2026-05-28 13 use cases 6 techniques 7 kill-chain phases detected

The 2026 World Cup presents major cyber risks from ransomware groups, state-aligned actors, and other groups targeting critical infrastructure. Learn more here. The post 2026 World Cup: Discussing The World’s Biggest Game’s Attack Surface appeared first on Unit 42 .

ATT&CKT1190 T1195.002 T1219 T1486 T1555.003 T1566

Actions on Objectives
Detected
Reconnaissance. Attacker researches the target — OSINT, scanning, enumeration.
Weaponization. Coupling exploit code with deliverable payload (e.g. weaponized PDF/Office doc, trojanized installer).
Delivery. Transmitting the weapon (phishing email, USB, watering hole, drive-by, malicious ad). → [LLM] World Cup 2026 themed lookalike / typosquat domain resolution by corporate hosts · Phishing-link click correlated to endpoint execution · Email attachment opened from external sender · Microsoft Teams external-tenant chat from unverified IT-helpdesk impersonator
Exploitation. Triggering the exploit — vulnerability/macro/trust abuse to execute code. → Office app spawning script/LOLBin child process · Trusted vendor binary / installer launching unusual children
Installation. Establishing persistence on the host — backdoor, service, scheduled task, registry key. → RMM tool installed by non-IT user — remote-access utility for hands-on-keyboard
Command & Control. Beacon to attacker infrastructure for control and tasking. → [LLM] NoName057(16) DDoSia client check-in (/client/login, /client/get_targets) · Beaconing — periodic outbound to small set of destinations
Actions on Objectives. Lateral movement, credential dumping, data theft, ransomware, sabotage. → Infostealer — non-browser process accessing browser cookie/login DBs · Ransomware-style mass file rename / extension change · LSASS process access / dump (credential theft) · Remote service execution — PsExec / SMB lateral movement
[LLM] NoName057(16) DDoSia client check-in (/client/login, /client/get_targets) Command & Control High
Hunts for the Russian-aligned NoName057(16) DDoSia botnet client beaconing to its C2 panel. The DDoSia Go-binary uses two distinctive REST URIs to register and pull targeting (/client/login then /client/get_targets) and defaults to the Go-http-client/1.1 user-agent. Catches an infected corporate host being conscripted into hacktivist DDoS against host-city, federation or ticketing infrastructure during the tournament window. Rationale: Anchored on the publicly documented DDoSia client URI scheme (/client/login, /client/get_targets, /client/post_solved) and Go-http-client default UA. The article names NoName057(16) and references their 3,700+ DDoS attacks against NATO targets through 2026; cross-referenced with Sekoia and NCSC public reporting on DDoSia client internals. Article: https://unit42.paloaltonetworks.com/fifa-world-cup-attack-surface/ Cross-checked against: • https://blog.sekoia.io/following-noname05716-ddosia-projects-targets/ • https://www.ncsc.gov.uk/news/joint-advisory-russia-aligned-noname05716 • https://attack.mitre.org/groups/G1023/
ATT&CKT1071.001 T1498 T1583.003
Data sourcesWeb Network_Traffic.All_Traffic
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where RemoteUrl has_any ("/client/login", "/client/get_targets", "/client/post_solved")
| where not (RemoteUrl has_any ("github.com", "atlassian.com", "gitlab.com", "microsoft.com"))
| summarize URIs = make_set(RemoteUrl, 10), FirstSeen = min(Timestamp), LastSeen = max(Timestamp), Hits = count() by DeviceName, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessFolderPath, RemoteIP
| where array_length(URIs) >= 2 or Hits > 5
| order by LastSeen desc
ImWebSession
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where Url has_any ("/client/login", "/client/get_targets", "/client/post_solved")
| where not (Url has_any ("github.com", "atlassian.com", "gitlab.com", "microsoft.com"))
| summarize URIs = make_set(Url, 10), FirstSeen = min(TimeGenerated), LastSeen = max(TimeGenerated), Hits = count(), UAs = make_set(HttpRequestHeaderUserAgent, 5) by SrcIpAddr, DstIpAddr, DstHostname
| where array_length(URIs) >= 2 or Hits > 5
| order by LastSeen desc
title: DDoSia (NoName057-16) C2 Check-in URI Pattern
id: 7f3a8b2e-1c44-4f67-89ab-cdef01234567
description: Detects NoName057(16) DDoSia client check-in via the /client/login and /client/get_targets REST endpoints used by the Go-based botnet client
references:
  - https://blog.sekoia.io/following-noname05716-ddosia-projects-targets/
  - https://unit42.paloaltonetworks.com/fifa-world-cup-attack-surface/
author: SOC Detection Engineering
date: 2026/05/28
tags:
  - attack.t1071.001
  - attack.t1498
  - attack.command_and_control
logsource:
  category: proxy
detection:
  selection_uri:
    cs-uri-stem|contains:
      - '/client/login'
      - '/client/get_targets'
      - '/client/post_solved'
  selection_ua:
    cs-user-agent|startswith: 'Go-http-client/'
  filter_legit:
    cs-host|endswith:
      - 'github.com'
      - 'atlassian.com'
      - 'gitlab.com'
  condition: selection_uri and selection_ua and not filter_legit
level: high
#event_simpleName=ProcessRollup2
| ImageFileName=/\\(dosia|ddosia|noname.*loader)\.exe$/i OR CommandLine=/\/client\/(login|get_targets|post_solved)/i
| groupBy([aid, ComputerName, ImageFileName, CommandLine, SHA256HashData], function=count())
| count>0
NETWORK
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime values(Web.url) as urls values(Web.http_user_agent) as user_agents values(Web.dest) as dests from datamodel=Web where (Web.url="*/client/login*" OR Web.url="*/client/get_targets*" OR Web.url="*/client/post_solved*") by Web.src Web.dest_port
| `drop_dm_object_name(Web)`
| where match(user_agents,"Go-http-client") OR mvcount(urls) > 1
| where NOT match(dests,"(github\.com|atlassian\.com|gitlab\.com)$")
| convert ctime(firstTime) ctime(lastTime)
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime values(Web.url) as urls values(Web.http_user_agent) as user_agents values(Web.dest) as dests from datamodel=Web where (Web.url="*/client/login*" OR Web.url="*/client/get_targets*" OR Web.url="*/client/post_solved*") by Web.src Web.dest_port
| `drop_dm_object_name(Web)`
| where match(user_agents,"Go-http-client") OR mvcount(urls) > 1
| where NOT match(dests,"(github\.com|atlassian\.com|gitlab\.com)$")
| convert ctime(firstTime) ctime(lastTime)
[LLM] World Cup 2026 themed lookalike / typosquat domain resolution by corporate hosts Delivery Medium
Hunting query for corporate endpoints resolving newly-observed domains containing FIFA / World Cup 2026 / Hayya / FanID keyword variants — the article cites 16,000+ scam domains observed in Qatar 2022 and forecasts the same pattern at scale across the 16 host cities. Catches credential-harvest landing pages, fake ticket-resale sites, and fraudulent fan-portal lookalikes used in the run-up to and during the tournament window (June 11 – July 19, 2026). Rationale: Anchored on the article's explicit forecast of typosquat/lookalike domains targeting fans — directly references Group-IB's 16,000+ scam domains from Qatar 2022 and the five categories of ticket-themed fraud. The regex covers the keyword roots (fifa, worldcup, hayya, fanid) that scam domains pivot on. Article: https://unit42.paloaltonetworks.com/fifa-world-cup-attack-surface/ Cross-checked against: • https://www.group-ib.com/blog/qatar-2022/ • https://www.fifa.com/tournaments/mens/worldcup/canadamexicousa2026
ATT&CKT1583.001 T1566.002 T1598.003
Data sourcesNetwork_Resolution.DNS Web
let LookalikeRegex = @"(?i)(fifa|world.?cup.?2026|wc.?2026|hayya|fan.?id)";
let LegitTLDs = dynamic(["fifa.com", "fifaworldcup.com", "hayya.qa", "hayya.com", "fifamuseum.com", "ussoccer.com", "canadasoccer.com", "miseleccion.mx"]);
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(1d)
| where isnotempty(RemoteUrl)
| where RemoteUrl matches regex LookalikeRegex
| extend domain = tostring(split(RemoteUrl, "/")[2])
| where not (LegitTLDs has_any (domain)) and not (domain endswith "fifa.com" or domain endswith "fifaworldcup.com" or domain endswith "hayya.qa")
| summarize FirstSeen = min(Timestamp), LastSeen = max(Timestamp), DeviceCount = dcount(DeviceName), SampleProc = any(InitiatingProcessFileName), SampleHost = any(DeviceName) by domain
| where DeviceCount < 50
| order by FirstSeen desc
let LookalikeRegex = @"(?i)(fifa|world.?cup.?2026|wc.?2026|hayya|fan.?id)";
ImDnsActivity
| where TimeGenerated > ago(1d)
| where DnsQuery matches regex LookalikeRegex
| where not (DnsQuery endswith "fifa.com" or DnsQuery endswith "fifaworldcup.com" or DnsQuery endswith "hayya.qa" or DnsQuery endswith "hayya.com" or DnsQuery endswith "ussoccer.com" or DnsQuery endswith "canadasoccer.com")
| summarize FirstSeen = min(TimeGenerated), LastSeen = max(TimeGenerated), HostCount = dcount(SrcHostname), SampleSrc = any(SrcIpAddr) by DnsQuery
| where HostCount < 50
| order by FirstSeen desc
title: World Cup 2026 Lookalike Domain DNS Resolution
id: 9a8b7c6d-5432-4098-a654-321fedcba012
description: Hunt for DNS queries to domains impersonating FIFA, World Cup 2026, Hayya, or FanID services from corporate endpoints
references:
  - https://unit42.paloaltonetworks.com/fifa-world-cup-attack-surface/
  - https://www.group-ib.com/blog/qatar-2022/
author: SOC Detection Engineering
date: 2026/05/28
tags:
  - attack.t1583.001
  - attack.t1566.002
  - attack.initial_access
logsource:
  category: dns
detection:
  selection:
    QueryName|re: '(?i)(fifa|world.?cup.?2026|wc.?2026|hayya|fan.?id)'
  filter_legit:
    QueryName|endswith:
      - 'fifa.com'
      - 'fifaworldcup.com'
      - 'hayya.qa'
      - 'hayya.com'
      - 'ussoccer.com'
      - 'canadasoccer.com'
  condition: selection and not filter_legit
level: medium
source:windows.sysmon @EventID:22 @QueryName:(*fifa* OR *worldcup* OR *world-cup* OR *wc2026* OR *hayya* OR *fanid* OR *fan-id*) -@QueryName:(*fifa.com OR *fifaworldcup.com OR *hayya.qa OR *hayya.com OR *ussoccer.com)
#event_simpleName=DnsRequest
| DomainName=/(?i)(fifa|world.?cup.?2026|wc.?2026|hayya|fan.?id)/
| NOT DomainName=/(fifa\.com|fifaworldcup\.com|hayya\.qa|hayya\.com|ussoccer\.com|canadasoccer\.com)$/i
| groupBy([DomainName], function=[count(as=Hits), count(field=aid, distinct=true, as=HostCount), min(@timestamp, as=FirstSeen)])
| HostCount<50
| sort(FirstSeen, order=desc)

| `drop_dm_object_name(DNS)`

| sort - firstTime
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime values(DNS.src) as src_hosts dc(DNS.src) as host_count from datamodel=Network_Resolution where (DNS.query="*fifa*" OR DNS.query="*worldcup*" OR DNS.query="*world-cup*" OR DNS.query="*wc2026*" OR DNS.query="*hayya*" OR DNS.query="*fanid*" OR DNS.query="*fan-id*") by DNS.query

Beaconing — periodic outbound to small set of destinations Command & Control Medium
C2 channel detection via inter-beacon-time stddev / fan-out to single dest.
ATT&CKT1071.001 T1071.004
Data sourcesNetwork_Traffic.All_Traffic DeviceNetworkEvents
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(1d)
| where RemoteIPType == "Public" and ActionType == "ConnectionSuccess"
| project DeviceName, RemoteIP, RemotePort, Timestamp
| sort by DeviceName asc, RemoteIP asc, RemotePort asc, Timestamp asc
| extend prev_dev = prev(DeviceName, 1), prev_ip = prev(RemoteIP, 1),
         prev_port = prev(RemotePort, 1), prev_ts = prev(Timestamp, 1)
| where DeviceName == prev_dev and RemoteIP == prev_ip and RemotePort == prev_port
| extend delta_sec = datetime_diff('second', Timestamp, prev_ts)
| summarize conn_count = count(), avg_delta = avg(delta_sec), stdev_delta = stdev(delta_sec)
    by DeviceName, RemoteIP, RemotePort
| where conn_count > 30 and avg_delta between (30.0 .. 600.0) and stdev_delta < 5.0
| order by conn_count desc
ImNetworkSession
| where TimeGenerated > ago(2h)
| where DvcAction != "Block"
| where ipv4_is_private(DstIpAddr) == false
| summarize ConnCount = count(),
            DistinctMinutes = dcount(bin(TimeGenerated, 1m))
            by DvcHostname, DstIpAddr, DstPortNumber
| where ConnCount > 50 and DistinctMinutes > 30   // sustained, not bursty
| order by ConnCount desc
NETWORK
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count, values(All_Traffic.dest_port) AS ports
    from datamodel=Network_Traffic.All_Traffic
    where All_Traffic.action="allowed" AND All_Traffic.dest_category!="internal"
    by _time span=10s, All_Traffic.src, All_Traffic.dest
| `drop_dm_object_name(All_Traffic)`
| streamstats current=f last(_time) AS prev_time by src, dest
| eval delta = _time - prev_time
| stats avg(delta) AS avg_delta stdev(delta) AS sd_delta count by src, dest
| where count > 30 AND sd_delta < 5 AND avg_delta>=30 AND avg_delta<=600
| sort - count
| tstats summariesonly=false count, values(All_Traffic.dest_port) AS ports
    from datamodel=Network_Traffic.All_Traffic
    where All_Traffic.action="allowed" AND All_Traffic.dest_category!="internal"
    by _time span=10s, All_Traffic.src, All_Traffic.dest
| `drop_dm_object_name(All_Traffic)`
| streamstats current=f last(_time) AS prev_time by src, dest
| eval delta = _time - prev_time
| stats avg(delta) AS avg_delta stdev(delta) AS sd_delta count by src, dest
| where count > 30 AND sd_delta < 5 AND avg_delta>=30 AND avg_delta<=600
| sort - count

title: Infostealer - Non-Browser Process Accessing Browser Credential Stores
id: 7c8b2e10-4d4f-4a8c-9c1f-bf6e2c4a8d01
status: experimental
description: |
    Stealers (RedLine, Lumma, Vidar, Atomic) read Login Data / cookies
    SQLite databases from Chrome/Edge/Firefox profile directories. Any
    non-browser process touching these files is a high-fidelity signal.
references:
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1539/
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1555/003/
author: Clankerusecase
date: 2026/05/02
tags:
    - attack.t1539
    - attack.t1555.003
    - attack.credential-access
logsource:
    category: file_access
    product: windows
detection:
    selection_path:
        TargetFilename|contains:
            - '\Google\Chrome\User Data\'
            - '\Microsoft\Edge\User Data\'
            - '\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\'
    selection_file:
        TargetFilename|endswith:
            - '\Login Data'
            - '\Cookies'
            - '\logins.json'
            - '\cookies.sqlite'
    filter_browser:
        Image|endswith:
            - '\chrome.exe'
            - '\msedge.exe'
            - '\firefox.exe'
            - '\brave.exe'
            - '\opera.exe'
    condition: selection_path and selection_file and not filter_browser
falsepositives:
    - Backup utilities reading user profile files
    - Browser sync agents from non-stock vendors
level: high
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Filesystem
    where (Filesystem.file_path="*\Google\Chrome\User Data\*\Login Data*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Google\Chrome\User Data\*\Cookies*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Microsoft\Edge\User Data\*\Login Data*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\*\logins.json*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\*\cookies.sqlite*")
      AND NOT Filesystem.process_name IN ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe","brave.exe","opera.exe")
    by Filesystem.dest, Filesystem.process_name, Filesystem.file_path, Filesystem.user
| `drop_dm_object_name(Filesystem)`
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Filesystem
    where (Filesystem.file_path="*\Google\Chrome\User Data\*\Login Data*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Google\Chrome\User Data\*\Cookies*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Microsoft\Edge\User Data\*\Login Data*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\*\logins.json*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\*\cookies.sqlite*")
      AND NOT Filesystem.process_name IN ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe","brave.exe","opera.exe")
    by Filesystem.dest, Filesystem.process_name, Filesystem.file_path, Filesystem.user
| `drop_dm_object_name(Filesystem)`
Phishing-link click correlated to endpoint execution Delivery High
User received an external email containing a URL, clicked it, and within 60 seconds the recipient's endpoint spawned a scripting interpreter or network downloader (PowerShell / cmd / mshta / curl / certutil / bitsadmin). This is the high-fidelity shape — a raw "user clicked an emailed URL" query is too noisy to alert on because every Microsoft 365 tenant generates thousands of legitimate clicks per day. The exec-correlation step suppresses the noise to roughly the rate at which a click actually drives onto-host execution, which is the actionable signal. Pair with UC_PHISH_LINK_BYPASS (Safe Links override) and UC_PHISH_LINK_NEWDOMAIN for orthogonal high-fidelity variants.
ATT&CKT1566.002 T1204.001 T1059.001
Data sourcesEmail.All_Email Web Endpoint.Processes EmailEvents EmailUrlInfo UrlClickEvents DeviceProcessEvents
// Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s.
// Far higher fidelity than "every clicked URL" — most legitimate clicks
// never spawn a non-browser child process, so the join eliminates the
// 99% of noise that makes a raw click query unactionable.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let SuspectClicks = UrlClickEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where AccountName !endswith "$"
    | where ActionType in ("ClickAllowed","ClickedThrough")
    | join kind=inner (
        EmailEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
        | where DeliveryAction == "Delivered"
        | where EmailDirection == "Inbound"
        | project NetworkMessageId, Subject, SenderFromAddress, SenderFromDomain,
                  RecipientEmailAddress, EmailTimestamp = Timestamp
      ) on NetworkMessageId
    | join kind=leftouter (
        EmailUrlInfo | project NetworkMessageId, Url, UrlDomain
      ) on NetworkMessageId, Url
    | project ClickTime = Timestamp, AccountUpn, IPAddress, Url, UrlDomain,
              Subject, SenderFromAddress, SenderFromDomain, RecipientEmailAddress,
              ActionType;
// Correlate to a non-browser child process spawned within 60 seconds on
// the recipient's device.
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                         "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
| where FileName in~ ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                        "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe",
                        "bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe","curl.exe","wget.exe")
| join kind=inner SuspectClicks on $left.AccountName == $right.AccountUpn
| where Timestamp between (ClickTime .. ClickTime + 60s)
| project ClickTime, ProcessTime = Timestamp,
          DelaySec = datetime_diff('second', Timestamp, ClickTime),
          DeviceName, AccountName, RecipientEmailAddress, SenderFromAddress,
          Subject, Url, UrlDomain, ActionType,
          FileName, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFileName
| order by ClickTime desc
// UrlClickEvents has no clean Sentinel-native equivalent. The detection
// pivots to: Office Send→Receive proximity to SecurityEvent 4688 of a
// non-browser child process. Lower fidelity than the Defender version.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let SuspectMailUsers = OfficeActivity
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where OfficeWorkload == "Exchange"
    | where Operation =~ "Receive"
    | summarize Subject = any(Subject), Sender = any(Sender)
                by MailboxOwnerUPN, MessageId, EmailTime = bin(TimeGenerated, 1m);
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
| where EventID == 4688
| where ParentProcessName has_any ("\chrome.exe","\msedge.exe",
                                     "\firefox.exe","\outlook.exe","\brave.exe")
| where NewProcessName has_any ("\powershell.exe","\pwsh.exe","\cmd.exe",
                                  "\mshta.exe","\rundll32.exe","\regsvr32.exe",
                                  "\wscript.exe","\cscript.exe","\bitsadmin.exe",
                                  "\certutil.exe","\curl.exe","\wget.exe")
| join kind=inner SuspectMailUsers on $left.Account == $right.MailboxOwnerUPN
| where TimeGenerated between (EmailTime .. EmailTime + 60s)
| project TimeGenerated, EmailTime, Computer, Account, ParentProcessName,
          NewProcessName, CommandLine, Sender, Subject
| order by TimeGenerated desc
WEB
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
``` Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s ```
| tstats `summariesonly` earliest(_time) AS click_time
    from datamodel=Web
    where Web.action="allowed"
    by Web.src, Web.user, Web.dest, Web.url
| `drop_dm_object_name(Web)`
| rename user AS recipient, dest AS clicked_domain, url AS clicked_url
| join type=inner recipient
    [| tstats `summariesonly` count
         from datamodel=Email.All_Email
         where All_Email.action="delivered" AND All_Email.url!="-"
         by All_Email.recipient, All_Email.src_user, All_Email.url, All_Email.subject
     | `drop_dm_object_name(All_Email)`
     | rex field=url "https?://(?<email_domain>[^/]+)"
     | rename recipient AS recipient]
| join type=inner src
    [| tstats `summariesonly` earliest(_time) AS exec_time
         values(Processes.process) AS exec_cmd, values(Processes.process_name) AS exec_proc
         from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
         where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                                   "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
           AND Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                                            "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe",
                                            "cscript.exe","bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe",
                                            "curl.exe","wget.exe")
         by Processes.dest, Processes.user
     | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
     | rename dest AS src]
| eval delta_sec = exec_time - click_time
| where delta_sec >= 0 AND delta_sec <= 60
| table click_time, exec_time, delta_sec, recipient, src, src_user, subject,
        clicked_domain, clicked_url, exec_proc, exec_cmd
| sort - click_time
``` Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s ```
| tstats summariesonly=false earliest(_time) AS click_time
    from datamodel=Web

    by Web.src, Web.user, Web.dest, Web.url
| `drop_dm_object_name(Web)`

    [| tstats summariesonly=false count
         from datamodel=Email.All_Email
         where All_Email.action="delivered" AND All_Email.url!="-"
         by All_Email.recipient, All_Email.src_user, All_Email.url, All_Email.subject
     | `drop_dm_object_name(All_Email)`
     | rex field=url "https?://(?<email_domain>[^/]+)"
     | rename recipient AS recipient]
| join type=inner src
    [| tstats summariesonly=false earliest(_time) AS exec_time
         values(Processes.process) AS exec_cmd, values(Processes.process_name) AS exec_proc
         from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
         where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                                   "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
           AND Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                                            "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe",
                                            "cscript.exe","bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe",
                                            "curl.exe","wget.exe")
         by Processes.dest, Processes.user
     | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
     | rename dest AS src]
| eval delta_sec = exec_time - click_time
| where delta_sec >= 0 AND delta_sec <= 60
| table click_time, exec_time, delta_sec, recipient, src, src_user, subject,

Email attachment opened from external sender Delivery High
Attachment delivery + execution by recipient — most common malware initial access.
ATT&CKT1566.001 T1204.002
Data sourcesEmail.All_Email Endpoint.Processes EmailAttachmentInfo DeviceProcessEvents
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let MalAttachments = EmailAttachmentInfo
    | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where AccountName !endswith "$"
    | project NetworkMessageId, RecipientEmailAddress,
              AttachmentFileName = FileName, AttachmentSHA256 = SHA256;
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("OUTLOOK.EXE","winword.exe","excel.exe","powerpnt.exe")
| where FileName in~ ("cmd.exe","powershell.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe",
                      "mshta.exe","rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe")
| join kind=inner MalAttachments on $left.AccountUpn == $right.RecipientEmailAddress
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, FileName, ProcessCommandLine,
          InitiatingProcessFileName, AttachmentFileName, AttachmentSHA256
// Sentinel doesn't have an attachment-hash table. Best approximation:
// OfficeActivity Send/Receive activity + correlate to host process spawn.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let MailWithAttach = OfficeActivity
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where OfficeWorkload == "Exchange"
    | where Operation in~ ("Send","Receive")
    | where isnotempty(MessageId)
    | project EmailTime = TimeGenerated, MailboxOwnerUPN, Sender,
              Recipients, Subject, MessageId;
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
| where EventID == 4688
| where ParentProcessName endswith "OUTLOOK.EXE"
| where NewProcessName endswith "\cmd.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\powershell.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\wscript.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\cscript.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\mshta.exe"
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, Account, NewProcessName, CommandLine,
          ParentProcessName
| order by TimeGenerated desc

LSASS process access / dump (credential theft) Actions on Objectives High
Mimikatz, comsvcs.dll MiniDump, or any non-Windows process opening LSASS.
ATT&CKT1003.001 T1003
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes DeviceEvents
DeviceEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where AccountName !endswith "$"
| where ActionType == "OpenProcessApiCall"
| where FileName =~ "lsass.exe"
| where InitiatingProcessFileName !in~ ("MsSense.exe","MsMpEng.exe","csrss.exe",

| project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, FileName,
          InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine,

// SecurityEvent EventID 4663 = object access. AccessMask 0x10 / 0x40 / 0x1010

SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where EventID == 4663
| where ObjectName endswith "\lsass.exe"
| where Account !endswith "$"
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, Account, ObjectName, ProcessName,

| order by TimeGenerated desc

Actions on Objectives
Detected
Reconnaissance. Attacker researches the target — OSINT, scanning, enumeration.
Weaponization. Coupling exploit code with deliverable payload (e.g. weaponized PDF/Office doc, trojanized installer).
Delivery. Transmitting the weapon (phishing email, USB, watering hole, drive-by, malicious ad). → [LLM] JINX-0164 AUDIOFIX delivery: shell payload retrieved from driver-store family domain · [LLM] Supply chain: install or runtime import of poisoned @velora-dex/sdk@9.4.1 (MiniRAT dropper) · Phishing-link click correlated to endpoint execution · Email attachment opened from external sender
Exploitation. Triggering the exploit — vulnerability/macro/trust abuse to execute code. → Office app spawning script/LOLBin child process · Trusted vendor binary / installer launching unusual children
Installation. Establishing persistence on the host — backdoor, service, scheduled task, registry key. → [LLM] AUDIOFIX persistence: ChromeUpdater binary loaded via launchctl on macOS · Suspicious browser extension installation · RMM tool installed by non-IT user — remote-access utility for hands-on-keyboard · File hash IOCs — endpoint file/process match
Command & Control. Beacon to attacker infrastructure for control and tasking. → [LLM] JINX-0164 C2 communication to fake driver-store infrastructure · Network connections to article IPs / domains
Actions on Objectives. Lateral movement, credential dumping, data theft, ransomware, sabotage. → [LLM] AUDIOFIX credential staging: Python parent invoking security/sqlite3/keychain extraction on macOS · Infostealer — non-browser process accessing browser cookie/login DBs · OAuth consent / suspicious app grant
[LLM] JINX-0164 C2 communication to fake driver-store infrastructure Command & Control High
Hunts for any endpoint network connection or DNS resolution to the JINX-0164 / AUDIOFIX C2 infrastructure: the driver-store.com / driver-hub.net / driver-update.io / driver-updater.net domains and the eight C2 IPs published by Wiz. Any hit is high-confidence — these domains masquerade as audio/video driver vendors and have no benign reason to be resolved. Rationale: All eight IPs and four root domains are published as JINX-0164 infrastructure by Wiz; the article explicitly names 'apple.driver-store[.]com' as the bash-script staging host. These are not legitimate driver-vendor domains — they impersonate Apple/Windows driver-update terminology and have no benign use. Cross-checked against SafeDep and StepSecurity coverage of the @velora-dex/sdk poisoning which references the same C2 family. Cross-checked against: • https://safedep.io/malicious-velora-dex-sdk-npm-compromised-rat/ • https://www.stepsecurity.io/blog/velora-dex-sdk-compromised-on-npm-malicious-version-drops-macos-backdoor-via-launchctl-persistence
